news.title: AutoRecLab: Describe the Experiment, Get the Code!
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Empirical evaluation is central to recommender-systems (RecSys) research, but turning experimental designs into executable code remains a manual and error-prone task. We present AutoRecLab, a Python-based autonomous RecSys lab that automates RecSys experiments from natural-language prompts. Given a research idea, AutoRecLab derives explicit experiment requirements, builds and validates a prototype, and iteratively expands it into the requested full experiment. The workflow combines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for documentation...

news.title: AutoViewMem: Self-Configuring Orthogonal Views for Conversational Long-Term Memory
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term memory is essential for large language model (LLM) agents to maintain consistency and personalization over extended interactions. Existing memory systems typically rely on fixed granularities or static schemas, but these designs struggle when heterogeneous information, such as preferences, events, constraints, and temporal updates, is embedded in a single mixed representation. news.title: Learning Cardiac Features: ECG Biometrics Across Time and~Exercise
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21962v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrocardiograms (ECGs) carry subject-specific patterns enabling reliable individual discrimination, forming the basis of ECG biometrics. Beyond authentication, this paradigm holds significant potential to secure sensitive cardiac data and to serve as a pretext task in self-supervised learning. Yet, most studies remain confined to singlesession, resting data, leaving robustness to temporal and physiological variations largely untested. news.title: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won't Reveal
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models can hold knowledge they do not report. A model may sandbag on a capability evaluation, or answer against what it internally knows, and its outputs alone cannot tell whether it is hiding an answer or simply does not have one. news.title: CodeMidas: Scaling Agentic Coding RL Environments from Code Itself
news.summary: arXiv:2609.22068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Training capable coding agents via reinforcement learning (RL) requires diverse tasks with reliable verifiers. Open-source codebases offer a rich source of such tasks, while existing methods typically rely on development artifacts such as issues and commits, limiting the range of tasks that can be extracted. To better scale RL environments, we present CodeMidas, an agentic pipeline that turns implemented functionality in existing codebases into executable RL environments using source code as its only task-specific input. news.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory from User Traffic for Agentic Graphic Design
news.summary: arXiv:2609.22086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Professional graphic design is a long-horizon agentic task in which structured, editable artifacts emerge from many interdependent actions, yet outcomes admit no reliable programmatic oracle. We introduce a continual adaptation framework in which a frozen frontier model operates professional design software through more than 230 tools, while an external procedural memory of natural-language skills accumulates and refines reusable design procedures from experience. news.title: ResNLS: An Improved Model for Stock Price Forecasting
news.summary: arXiv:2312.01020v3 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stock prices forecasting has always been a challenging task. Although many research projects try to address the problem, few of them pay attention to the varying degrees of dependencies between stock prices. In this paper, we introduce a hybrid model that improves the prediction of stock prices by emphasizing the dependencies between adjacent stock prices. news.title: dSTAR: Straggler Tolerant and Byzantine Resilient Distributed SGD
news.summary: arXiv:2412.07151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Distributed model training needs to be adapted to challenges such as the straggler effect and Byzantine attacks. When coordinating the training process with multiple computing nodes, ensuring timely and reliable gradient aggregation amidst network and system malfunctions is essential. news.title: A Hybrid Computational Intelligence Framework for scRNA-seq Imputation: Integrating scRecover and Random Forests
news.summary: arXiv:2511.16923v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables transcriptomic profiling at cellular resolution but suffers from pervasive dropout events that obscure biological signals. We present SCR-MF, a modular two-stage workflow that combines principled dropout detection using scRecover with robust non-parametric imputation via missForest. news.title: Making Latent Evolution Explicit: Operator-Structured Transitions for World Action Models
news.summary: arXiv:2608.27259v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) augment robot policies by predicting how task-relevant scene states may evolve under interaction. Recent WAMs increasingly perform such prediction in latent representation spaces, avoiding full appearance-level generation while preserving control-relevant information. news.title: Reinforcement learning for post-coronagraphic wavefront control
news.summary: arXiv:2609.20880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Direct imaging of exoplanets is limited by the extreme contrast between the star and the planets, which is mitigated using a coronagraph. However, optical aberrations cause starlight leakage through the coronagraph, producing speckles that obscure the planetary signal. news.title: BI-Agent and BI-Bench: Towards Automating End-to-End Business Intelligence
news.summary: arXiv:2609.20886v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Business intelligence (BI) is a cornerstone of enterprise decision-making and is widely used by enterprise users in software such as Power BI and Tableau. In traditional BI workflows, users need to prepare data by (1) identifying relevant tables, (2) performing data transformations, and (3) building join relationships, before they can (4) answer their business questions. news.title: SpaceDiffusion: Over-the-Orbit Diffusion for Space Generate-and-Forward Communications
news.summary: arXiv:2609.20899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Satellite communications are an essential component of sixth-generation (6G) mobile networks, which provide ubiquitous connectivity for global services. However, the satellite uplink remains a critical bottleneck for ground devices: their limited transmit power and antenna apertures result in low data rates and high packet errors. news.summary: arXiv:2609.20904v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hybrid motor-imagery brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs) combining EEG and fNIRS can outperform EEG-only systems by exploiting complementary electrophysiological and hemodynamic information. To obtain such hybrid information when paired EEG-fNIRS acquisition is unavailable or inconvenient, recent studies have focused on EEG-to-fNIRS cross-modal generation. news.title: Trustworthy FinAInce: Unpacking How AI-Mediated Financial Advice is Judged
news.summary: arXiv:2609.20989v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As generative AI is increasingly used as a source of personal financial guidance, understanding how people appraise such advice is important for supporting appropriate reliance. We conducted a randomized vignette experiment with 285 U.S. adults across eight financial decisions, independently varying three advice styles---AI, expert, and online community---and displayed source labels while holding the underlying recommendation consistent. news.title: Scaling Discovery through Test-Time Communication
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Science advances not in isolation but through collaboration, yet existing agentic systems capture little of this. Whether communicating agents help remains an open question with mixed prior results. news.title: Physically Based Rendering in the Latent Space
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Image diffusion models have shown impressive image generation capabilities but are often hard to control, in contrast to classical computer graphics pipelines such as physically based rendering. However, we observe that there is a bridge between light transport phenomena and the distribution of latent space values produced by such models. news.title: How Much of a Real Workload Can LLM-Generated GPU Kernels Actually Reach?
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21058v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language models can now write GPU kernels that outperform PyTorch. We evaluate five model configurations on KernelBench level 1 and find that a frontier model produces correct kernels for 91.1% of problems and independently verified speedups on 22 of 56, including three convolutions, with a median of 1.235x. news.title: PlantShade: Predicting Plant Shadows for Lighting-Aware Robotic Agricultural Operation
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21059v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Plant growth and agricultural production form the foundation of a country's sustainable development and directly impact human livelihoods. Recent advances in frontier artificial intelligence have enabled scientific agriculture with strong potential to improve crop productivity. In this paper, we identify the importance and inherent complexity of plant shade simulation, as shading is a critical factor influencing plant growth. news.title: Aligning with Lived Experience: Heterogeneous Benefits of Fine Tuning in Mental Health Support Generation
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21075v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As access to professional mental healthcare remains limited, many individuals turn to online platforms such as Reddit to seek peer support situated within human lived experience. However, a significant portion of such queries go unanswered, presenting an opportunity for using Large Language Models (LLMs) to fill this gap. news.title: Geometry of Values: Task Vector Composition for Ethical Preference Alignment in Language Models
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in applications that must weigh clashing moral values, yet even strong models exhibit hidden biases and brittle instruction-following across languages. news.title: From Task Success to Productive Success: Evaluating Human-AI Collaboration by Quality and Cost
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21117v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI productivity is often measured by task completion time, economic value, or improvements in outcome quality. news.title: The Stochastic Shift: A New Evaluation Paradigm for Text-to-SQL with AI Operators
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21133v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: SQL has been augmented with AI operators, enabling modern data analytics platforms to derive insights from both structured and unstructured data. news.summary: arXiv:2609.21151v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Molecular solubility directly affects key aspects of molecular development such as reaction feasibility, formulation performance, separation efficiency, and solvent selection. news.summary: arXiv:2609.21190v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ensuring the correctness of LLM-generated code is a core challenge for modern software engineering. news.summary: arXiv:2609.21212v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learned navigation policies typically consume observations as a temporally ordered history, with positional encodings tying each observation to when it was seen, making it difficult to reuse experience from earlier traversals of an environment. news.summary: arXiv:2609.21216v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies based on flow matching generate action chunks through repeated evaluations of an action expert. news.summary: arXiv:2609.21227v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Factual hallucination is commonly defined by incorrect factual outputs. news.summary: arXiv:2609.21228v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models built on pretrained vision-language models have demonstrated strong performance across diverse robotic manipulation tasks. news.title: KnowDemo: Knowledge-Guided Robot Demonstration Generation from Human Videos
news.summary: arXiv:2609.21229v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning robot manipulation policies typically requires substantial demonstration data, which are costly to collect on real robots. news.summary: arXiv:2609.21246v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models map visual observations and natural-language instructions to robotic actions, but distribution shifts can compromise their reliability. news.summary: arXiv:2609.21257v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can propose, implement, and evaluate model changes. news.summary: arXiv:2609.21334v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Effective evaluation of zero-day jamming detectors requires robust adversarial models. news.title: AsymSpec: Context-Asymmetric Speculative Decoding for Agentic LLMs
news.summary: Agentic pipelines blow up on context, so deployments compress inputs — but compression kills accuracy. Standard speculative decoding requires the drafter and verifier to share context, so it can't fix the accuracy/overhead trade-off. AsymSpec breaks the symmetry: a small drafter reads the full context while the big verifier sees the compressed view, fused via contrastive δ-logits with a divergence-aware acceptance gate.

news.title: Prefix Sliding for Efficient Test-Time Scaling
news.summary: Reasoning LLMs keep the entire chain-of-thought in context via full attention, which gets prohibitively expensive on hard problems that need long thinking. The authors observe that most intermediate reasoning tokens lose importance as the model continues, and propose Prefix Sliding : drop tokens that aren't part of the prefix (instructions, tools) or the recent sliding window. The prefix is preserved because it contains the task spec; the window is preserved because recent steps still matter.

news.title: R³: Training Robots to Reason in Natural Language via Reinforcement Learning
news.summary: Can a VLM be trained to reason in natural language about long-horizon manipulation? R³ is a two-stage recipe: mid-train a VLM on expert reasoning traces to set the reasoning style, then single-step rubric-based RL from offline action data to refine it. The reasoner outputs free-form language that steers a low-level policy at test time, instead of using structured traces as auxiliary loss.

news.title: TailSFT: Filtered Fine-Tuning Improves Post-Training Performance
news.summary: Post-RL pipelines are bottlenecked by SFT coverage: RL fine-tunes a base model, so the base must already model the tail of the data distribution. TailSFT filters out the easy sequences during SFT and trains only on the under-modeled tail, with both a theoretical and empirical justification of the filtering rule. On OLMo-3 7B it lifts pass@16 on math/coding by up to 17% absolute, and the resulting checkpoints give up to 4% absolute pass@1 gains in subsequent GRPO.

news.title: VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning
news.summary: "Native visual reasoning" treats image/video generation as the medium of thought, not just the output. VBVR-Pro is a closed-loop testbed that makes this trainable, verifiable, optimizable, and experimentally controllable at scale: task scaling, reliable feedback, and head-to-head substrate comparisons all in one suite. 52 authors spanning CUHK, Oxford (Torr, Khashabi, Müller), Princeton (Kriegeskorte, Millière, Yuille) and others.

news.title: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes
news.summary: cs.CL An open-web-sourcing framework that drives hundreds of browser sandboxes in parallel against hundreds of thousands of real, openly reachable websites, with a Proposer-Solver dual-agent loop turning raw pages into executable tasks and a rule-plus-model cleaning pipeline that rewrites surviving reasoning into a single unified chain-of-thought style. Resulting corpus: 203,238 trajectories, each from a distinct website — bigger and more diverse than prior trajectory datasets. Fine-tuning a compact multimodal model lifts Online-Mind2Web success from 25.66% to 33.33%, with the gain growing as the corpus scales.

news.title: Do Robotic World Models Really Follow Actions? Diagnosing and Aligning Action-Conditioned Generation for Policy Learning
news.summary: cs.RO / cs.CV Introduces WorldEcho, a benchmark that probes action-following over a much broader action distribution than expert-only demos (using visual integrity and SE(3) trajectory alignment), and WorldSync, a three-axis fix that broadens training distribution, grounds intermediate video representations in action-induced dynamics via an Action-Forcing Expert, and aligns predicted-vs-actual changes under interventions. The diagnosis: current world models handle expert actions fine but ignore or break on diverse off-expert trajectories.

news.title: Effective Learning Rate Governs Loss Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
news.summary: cs.LG An empirical scaling law for LM pretraining: loss trajectories collapse across runs when the ratio of learning rate to parameter norm (the "effective learning rate", ELR) is matched, even with very different absolute LRs and norms. The collapse holds across optimizers, architectures, datasets, and model scales with mean errors in the few-x-10^-3 range, below seed-to-seed noise.

news.title: LAION-BVD: A 10-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training
news.summary: cs.CV / cs.LG / cs.CL LAION drops a 10-million-hour open video pretraining corpus: 1.3B platform-specific URLs from CommonCrawl, 80M videos actually downloaded, content-aware scene detection for clips, and synthetic video+audio captions. Models trained on it post competitive results on standard video-text and audio-text benchmarks with monotonic gains as compute grows.

news.title: Latent Action as Intention Enables Efficient Future Imagination for World Action Models (LAWA)
news.summary: cs.RO / cs.CV An architecture that keeps test-time future imagination but skips the expensive future-video branch: a discrete tokenizer pre-trained on action-free data produces manipulation-centric codebook targets, then a continuous latent state anchored to those targets is denoised jointly with executable action chunks. On RoboCasa LAWA hits 65.6% / 80.8% in few-shot / full-data settings — beating matched Fast-WAM by 9.6 / 4.5 points and matching Joint-WAM with 42.9% lower inference latency.

news.title: Reading Is Not Using: Retrieval, Judgment, and the Design of AI Financial Research Workflows
news.summary: cs.CL / cs.AI Identifies a retrieval-integration gap in long-context financial analysis: holding focal-firm information fixed and varying only unrelated context from 2k to 128k tokens, a risk disclosure's influence on investment judgments falls to the noise floor even as direct retrieval remains accurate. The pattern replicates across model families and in real 10-K filings — more capable models postpone but do not eliminate it. Chunk-and-summarize pipelines actively evict relevant info; a targeted, structured restatement adjacent to the decision restores its influence.

news.title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses (Recuris)
news.summary: cs.AI / cs.CL A two-tier memory architecture for long-horizon agents: Working Memory tracks task progress and routes skill selection from Experiential Memory, so skill use is grounded in current needs rather than the full history. Execution traces become structured evidence that localizes failures to specific memory components, which a fixed Meta-Agent then rewrites recursively.

news.title: Right Diagnoses, Decorative Reasoning: A Perturbation Audit of Medical Chain-of-Thought
news.summary: cs.AI / cs.CL A 30-operator medical CoT faithfulness audit: severity reversal, negation flips, demographic swaps, evidence ablation, etc., paired with chain-update × answer-flip joint analysis to classify each model's failure mode. The headline finding: medical LLMs often keep the right diagnosis but produce decorative reasoning that does not track the perturbed question.

news.title: Stream-Aligned Policy Optimization for Asynchronous Agentic RL (SPO++)
news.summary: cs.AI Identifies a math bug in SPO: trajectory-level centering does not center the token-weighted quantity the actor loss actually consumes. SPO++ fixes it by standardizing terminal-outcome advantages under the action-token measure and organizing prompt evidence by the policy event that produced it rather than learner receipt order. On ALFWorld and Math-TIR, the action-token-measure normalization is the single strongest tested component.

news.title: What FID Hides: Detecting, Ranking, and Diagnosing Deviations in Generative Evaluation
news.summary: cs.LG A critical audit of FID/KID scores that everyone in generative modeling uses but nobody really questions. The authors show that visually unrecognizable images optimized only to match Inception mean+covariance achieve FID 24.7 vs. 58.6 for real held-out images. FID is a moment summary that misses distributional differences, and the scalar gap is not even calibrated against sampling variation.

news.title: Erasca's ERAS-0015 (Pan-RAS Molecular Glue) Wins FDA Fast Track for Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer — Phase III PDAC Trial Slated for 2027
news.summary: Erasca (ERAS) announced Aug 24 that the FDA granted Fast Track Designation (FTD) to ERAS-0015, an oral pan-RAS molecular glue, for metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The designation is ERAS-0015's first formal regulatory milestone globally and follows July 2026 AURORAS-1 Phase 1 data showing a 57% unconfirmed 8-week ORR in 7 evaluable 2L+ KRAS G12X pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients at the 32 mg recommended dose for expansion (RDE); 6 of 7 remained on treatment at the May 25 cutoff with no DLTs. FTD enables more frequent FDA interactions, plus eligibility for rolling review, accelerated approval, and priority review. Company plans: a Phase III 1L PDAC trial in 2027, a registration-enabling 2L+ NSCLC trial in H1 2027, and a second Phase III NSCLC study in H2 2027–H1 2028. ERAS was trading +2.72% to $18.11 pre-market.

news.title: FDA Halts Regenxbio's RGX-121 Hunter Syndrome Gene Therapy Again — 5 Asymptomatic Spine MRI Findings, BLA Resubmission Indefinitely Postponed, Stock -25%
news.summary: Regenxbio (RGNX) disclosed Monday Aug 24 that the FDA placed a new clinical hold on RGX-121 (clemidsogene lanparvovec) for Hunter syndrome (MPS II) after investigators found small asymptomatic nodules/cystic masses in the spines of 5 of 48 patients in the CAMPSIITE registrational trial — all treated 3–6 years ago via intracisternal/intraventricular AAV delivery. Radiologists call the findings "likely benign"; no brain masses detected; all 5 patients remain clinically well with stable-to-improving neurocognitive scores. The company now says it will NOT refile the BLA "in the near term" — reversing the June Type-A meeting agreement where the agency (under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas) had blessed an accelerated-approval resubmission in Q3. This is RGX-121's second clinical hold of 2026 (the first came in January when a separate MPS I gene therapy program, RGX-111, produced a brain tumor). RGNX fell 24.81% to $8.06 Monday.

news.summary: Genentech (Roche) signed an exclusive global license (ex-South Korea) for Hanmi Pharmaceutical's HM17321, a proprietary urocortin-2 (UCN2) analog designed as a non-incretin obesity therapy that reduces fat while preserving (and possibly adding) lean muscle. Deal terms disclosed Aug 24: $190M upfront + up to ~$2.12B in development/regulatory/commercial milestones + tiered royalties on sales — making it the largest single-asset out-licensing deal in Korean pharma history. FDA cleared Phase 1 IND in Nov 2025; Hanmi runs the current Phase 1 in healthy volunteers and obese patients, after which Genentech takes over from Phase 2. news.title: GSK's Bepirovirsen (Hibsago) Approved in Japan — World's First Functional Cure Drug for CHB; 19% Functional Cure Rate vs ~1% Standard of Care
news.summary: Japan's MHLW approved GSK's bepirovirsen (brand: Hibsago) on Aug 24 as the first-ever functional cure treatment for chronic hepatitis B in adults with ≥6 months of prior nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy and HBsAg ≤3000 IU/mL + HBV DNA <90 IU/mL at baseline. Approval was accelerated under Japan's SENKU designation for high-unmet-need medicines. B-Well Phase III pooled data: 19% functional cure rate at 6 months (233/1,220) in the broad HBsAg ≤3000 IU/mL population, vs 0/614 on placebo (p<0.001); in the HBsAg ≤1000 IU/mL subgroup, 26% (200/768) achieved functional cure. Bepirovirsen is an antisense oligonucleotide co-developed with Ionis Pharmaceuticals. GSK projects peak sales exceeding $2.7B; decisions pending in the U.S. (FDA Breakthrough + Fast Track), China (Breakthrough + Priority), and elsewhere over the next few months. The drug is partnered in China with Sino Biopharm via CTTQ for fast rollout if approved.

news.title: Rillet Crosses $1B "Unicorn" Mark with $100M Series C — 48-Hour Round Closed by ICONIQ, Sequoia, a16z

The round was unsolicited by Rillet (initiated by investors after a board update showing Q2 ARR doubling) and closed in 48 hours. Customer base passed 600 organizations, all of whom have fully replaced their legacy ERP/accounting systems. Notable: 50% of customers came from Intuit, 30% from NetSuite/Sage Intacct, 20% from Oracle/SAP/Workday/Microsoft.

news.title: EchoWM: Open and Enterable Omnimodal World Models
news.summary: Most "world model" demos are vision-only. EchoWM is the first open release that generates all four modalities jointly — 720p video, environmental sound, music, and speech — while responding to continuous camera motion. The camera-intent abstraction is the bit worth stealing: in first-person scenes it specifies observer motion; in third-person scenes the camera-character dynamics are learned from data with no view-specific controllers. Discrete commands and continuous poses both map to a shared metric-scale 6-DoF trajectory, with dataset-level calibration preserving motion magnitude across heterogeneous sources. The "enterable" part is the design choice that distinguishes it from Oasis/Genie: you don't just watch, you walk.

news.title: How to Train a Critic Stably and Efficiently
news.summary: A principled answer to the GRPO-is-stable-but-critic-is-not question that has been bugging RL-for-LLM practitioners since GRPO ate the field. The paper diagnoses why naive critic-based training recipes blow up on token-level advantages, then ships BPCO (Best-Practice Critic Optimization) : DPPO backbone + value predictions bounded to the reward range + Monte Carlo value targets + unnormalized policy advantages + length-adaptive GAE. Because the critic needs only one sampled response per prompt (not a group of k), the effective sample-efficiency win is roughly k× over GRPO at comparable compute — i.e. a PPO-shaped pipeline becomes competitive with group-based methods if you stop using their default recipes. The headline ablation makes that explicit.

news.title: ProxyFormer: A Dual-Stream Proxy Architecture for Ultra-Long Context and High-Resolution Generation
news.summary: Quadratic attention and growing KV cache are the bottleneck for both million-token context LLMs and high-res image/video generators. ProxyFormer splits each layer into two streams. A fine-grained local stream compresses bottom-up into a small set of proxy tokens ; expensive global interaction happens only in that compressed proxy space; then the globally contextualised proxies decompress top-down back into the local stream. Because the local stream is dense but never attends globally, and the proxy stream is sparse but sees the whole input, the layer runs at sub-quadratic cost with no perceivable loss in long-context retrieval or high-resolution fidelity. Single-author work, but with the ablation tables of a lab.

news.title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
news.summary: The world-model "control vs memory" tension is real: control wants a short rollout horizon (so reactions stay sharp), memory wants unbounded history (so the agent doesn't forget the room it walked through). ReWorld separates the two structurally inside the attention itself. Mixed per-head attention windows: most heads look only at the recent window, a small subset are global, and random head routing keeps the two capabilities from binding to particular heads. Random chunk dropping during training makes sparse histories in-distribution, so at inference the whole past lives under a bounded budget. Result: controllable interactive video that doesn't lose track of where it's been over hundreds of steps — the part every existing world model collapses on.

news.title: SRPO: Self-Reflective Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon Reasoning
news.summary: Self-reflection is the credit-assignment trick humans use to convert sparse outcome feedback into dense guidance; SRPO internalises it for LLM post-training. Concretely: the model analyses its own completed trajectories, synthesises the errors into compact "reflection patches," and a teacher model scores on-policy student rollouts conditioned on those patches — turning the patches into dense, token-level training signal rather than the coarse outcome-only reward that current GRPO/RLOO methods use. The framing is "the reflection is part of the policy, not a separate prompt trick." They report meaningful gains on long-horizon math and tool-use benchmarks where outcome-only rewards are too sparse to be useful.

news.title: Bitcoin Erupts Past $77K to ~$80K on U.S. Treasury Buyback Expansion — $4B+ Short Liquidated, Total Crypto Market Cap Adds $500B to $2.74T
news.summary: On Aug 22–23, 2026, Bitcoin broke decisively out of a weeks-long $62K–$67K range, surging past $77K and briefly topping $79,461 on Friday before settling near $77,300 on Sunday. The trigger: the U.S. Treasury announced it will at least double the size of its long-term bond buyback program to absorb selling pressure, alongside a White House crypto summit where Trump publicly pushed the Senate to pass the CLARITY Act and CFTC Chair Mike Selig pledged to use existing authority to advance the administration's crypto agenda. CoinGlass data shows $4B+ in crypto short positions liquidated in 24h; ~$2.6B poured into US spot Bitcoin and Ether ETFs (BlackRock's IBIT alone took $742M across Aug 20–21) — making this the biggest ETF week of 2026. Total crypto market cap added ~$500B in a week, reaching ~$2.74T (highest since early May). BTC's YTD loss narrowed to ~12% from nearly -30% at the start of August.

news.title: Grayscale Files 5th Amendment for Zcash Trust → "The Zcash ETF" (ZCSH) — First U.S. Privacy-Coin Spot ETF in the Pipeline, 2.5% Fee, Possible 34% DCG Stake
news.summary: Grayscale filed its fifth amended S-1 with the SEC on Aug 21, 2026, advancing its bid to convert the existing Grayscale Zcash Trust into a spot ETF. If approved, the product — renamed "The Zcash ETF" and listing on NYSE Arca under ticker ZCSH — would be the first U.S. spot ETF to directly hold a privacy-focused cryptocurrency. Key terms: 2.5% annual sponsor fee (accrued and paid in ZEC); BNY Mellon as transfer agent; Coinbase Custody as custodian; in-kind creations supported (cash redemptions only at launch). The trust already holds $260M AUM and has traded OTC since 2017. DCG International Investments (a Grayscale/DCG subsidiary) is in nonbinding discussions to contribute ~200,000 ZEC to seed the creation basket — under a June 30 snapshot that would give DCG ~34% of the enlarged fund (potentially higher if you count existing 757,202 related-party shares). The S-3 was filed Aug 21; the parallel Rule 19b-4 exchange filing status has not been disclosed.

news.title: Trump Holds White House Crypto Summit, Sets Sept 15 Senate Procedural Vote on CLARITY Act — Ethics Provision Remains the Blocker
news.summary: On Aug 19, 2026, President Trump convened crypto executives at the White House (Coinbase, Kraken, Ripple, Gemini, Robinhood alongside SEC Chair Paul Atkins and CFTC Chair Mike Selig) and publicly pressured the Senate to pass the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. The Senate left for August recess without voting, and a procedural vote is now scheduled for Sept 15 — the first opportunity after summer recess and the last realistic window before midterm positioning takes over the calendar. Core bill: assigns SEC vs CFTC jurisdiction (SEC for security-like digital assets; CFTC for digital commodities), shields non-custodial DeFi developers under Section 604 (Blockchain Regulatory Certainty Act), creates registration regimes for digital commodity exchanges, and allocates $150M for crypto fraud enforcement. The unresolved fight: an ethics provision covering officials' own crypto holdings — Trump's 2025 disclosure showed ~$1.4B in crypto-related income ($635M from $TRUMP meme coin royalties + $500M+ from World Liberty Financial token sales). Democratic version (Gallego/Alsobrooks): require divestiture and blind-trust compliance, state AG enforcement. Republican/White House version: bar officials + spouses from issuing/sponsoring tokens, $250K/day fines, DOJ enforcement, sunset Jan 2029. Polymarket odds of 2026 enactment: collapsed from 82% in Feb to ~13–45% depending on cut.

news.title: U.S. Spot Bitcoin + Ether ETFs Record Biggest Week of 2026 — $2.6B Net Inflows as BTC Approaches $80K
news.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin and Ether ETFs pulled in roughly $2.6 billion net inflows for the week ending Aug 22, 2026 — the largest weekly haul of the year. Breakdown from Farside: Aug 20 spot BTC ETFs +$606.3M (BlackRock's IBIT took $503.0M); Aug 21 spot BTC ETFs +$307.5M (IBIT +$239.3M); spot Ether ETFs +$219.5M on Aug 20 and +$184.0M on Aug 21. Friday Aug 22 was a record session — Bitcoin briefly touched $79,461 before profit-taking. Total ETF cumulative AUM now exceeds $165B (BTC ETFs ~$120B, ETH ETFs ~$25B, altcoin ETFs ~$20B). ETF flows are the dominant marginal buyer in this rally; spot exchange balances have dropped to multi-year lows.

news.title: Zcash Hits 8-Year High Near $855 on ETF Filing — Privacy Coin Market Cap Crosses $14B (Now #12 Crypto)
news.summary: Zcash (ZEC) surged to roughly $855 on Saturday Aug 23 — the highest price since 2018 — and is now the 12th-largest cryptocurrency by market cap (~$14.5B). The weekly move: +22–30% over 24h and ~70% over the week (from ~$490 on Aug 16 to ~$873). Trading is heavily derivatives-driven: 24h ZEC futures volume hit ~$9.54B vs ~$1.06B spot volume, and open interest sits at ~$1.8B (~13% of market cap). The rally reverses a brutal Q2 — ZEC had crashed from ~$630 to ~$250 in June after developers disclosed a counterfeiting vulnerability in the Orchard shielded pool (since patched via the NU6.2 network upgrade). Three weeks later, the token is more than 3× its June low.

news.title: CLEAR: Continuous Latent Adapter Routing for Utility-Preserving LLM Safety Alignment
news.summary: A targeted fix for the safety-vs-utility trade-off in LLM alignment. Existing global safety tuning (SFT, standard LoRA) writes the same safety signal into the backbone for every input, which degrades benign prompts alongside the harmful ones it intends to suppress. CLEAR attaches a small safety LoRA adapter and gates it continuously per-input by a lightweight hidden-state classifier that decides how strongly to mix the adapter in at each token. The backbone stays frozen. On Llama-3-8B-Instruct this drops HarmBench ASR from 32.3% to 0.5% while raising GSM8K by up to 7.1 points over globally applied SFT / LoRA — i.e. you get the safety benefit without paying the usual utility tax, and often net-improving utility because the global interventions were hurting it.

news.title: OmniAssistBench: Assistant-style Interaction Benchmark for Omni-LLMs
news.summary: A benchmark purpose-built for interactive omni-modal assistants — models that continuously perceive the world (video, audio, gestures) and proactively guide a user toward a goal, not just answer questions about a passive video clip. Static offline datasets can't accommodate the fact that the model's response dynamically changes the user's next action, so OmniAssistBench reverse-engineers the dataset from internet videos: 1000+ expert person-hours to deduce user goals and segment each source into multi-turn clips that simulate continuous interaction. To handle the path-divergence problem (one goal, many valid routes), models are given priors derived from the source video and have to guide the user along the exact same route — turning "creativity" into a measurable mismatch. The headline number: Gemini-3-Pro hits 66.4/100, the open-source Qwen3-Omni-Instruct 51.2/100. Both stumble on visual prompts (hand gestures) and fail to maintain temporal continuity across turns.

news.title: Scaling Muon for Diffusion Transformers
news.summary: First systematic scaling study of the Muon optimizer (matrix-aware, balancing updates across singular directions) on DiTs from 1.3B to 15B parameters, plus a fix for its biggest scaling flaw. The diagnostic: vanilla Muon's per-step 5-iteration Newton–Schulz (NS5) and full-momentum materialization stop paying off at scale — the optimizer time can exceed the model-step savings. The fix is Periodic Row-wise Muon : do the full NS5 spectral refresh every K steps, and use a cheap row-wise constrained update on the live momentum in between. The distributed implementation runs the row-wise path directly on sharded momentum and overlaps the NS5 refresh via bucketed all-gather. Across all scales Muon still beats AdamW on best generative quality by 12.9–19.1%; Periodic Row-wise Muon stays within 0.5% of vanilla Muon at 1.3B–4B, gains 4.5% at 9B, cuts optimizer time by 46.9–54.3%, end-to-end step time by 15.7–24.3%, communication volume by 66.7%, and reaches best quality with 33.7–64.8% less active training time.

news.title: TreeWY: Speculative Verification for Gated DeltaNet Hybrids
news.summary: Modern open-source frontier models (Qwen3.5, the new generation of hybrid linear-attention / Transformer stacks) keep most layers as Gated DeltaNet (GDN) — a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a growing KV cache. That's great for memory but kills speculative decoding: today's approach snapshots the full recurrent state at every draft position, and those snapshots can't be shared across branches of a draft tree, so a wide high-acceptance tree becomes memory-infeasible. TreeWY removes the snapshots entirely. Using a tree-structured WY transform of the gated delta rule, it computes every draft node's output with a single triangular solve, stores a small pseudo-value matrix instead of per-node states, and reconstructs only the one accepted state on commit. On Qwen3.5 35B and 397B serving benchmarks it cuts speculative recurrent-state memory and KV-cache pressure at identical acceptance length — turning the freed HBM into higher throughput and lower TTFT wherever memory is the bottleneck, with only a few percent cost where it isn't. Same memory budget now buys a wider, higher-acceptance draft tree.

news.title: China Releases Three EdTech LLM Group Standards at GSE2026 — First Sector-Level Guardrails for "AI + Education"
news.summary: At the closing of the 2026 Global Smart Education Conference (GSE2026, Beijing, Aug 18–20), China published three group standards for educational large models: "General Educational LLM Technical Architecture Design Specification," "Guidelines for Building Smart Education Systems Based on LLMs," and "Intelligent Teacher Technical Specification." The standards cover data-privacy protection, algorithm-fairness auditing, service-continuity guarantees, and disclosure requirements. Standards work includes VIPKID as a co-drafter. The release comes as China's "15th Five-Year Plan for Education Development" and a five-ministry "AI + Education Action Plan" move into implementation phase.

news.title: Jiuxuewang + Tencent Cloud Launch "Future Learning Center" at WWEC 2026 — "AI Dual-Learning · Dual-Planning" System 3.0 + AI Self-Study Room Franchise
news.summary: At the 12th WWEC World Education Conference (Shanghai, Aug 20), Jiuxuewang Group and Tencent Cloud jointly launched the "Future Learning Center" new product line. The school-side flagship is "XueWang Premium Course Smart Learning System 3.0," targeting middle/high schools with an "AI dual-learning + dual-planning" model that connects weekday in-school learning and weekend tutoring on a single data layer across four terminals (school admin / teacher / student tablet / parent WeChat). The social-side line ships three franchise products — "AI Self-Study Room," "AI Class," "AI Daycare" — already validated across 70 directly-operated studios and 1,000+ partner stores.

news.title: Medly AI (London) Closes $8M Seed Led by Felix Capital — Joins UK Dept. for Education AI Tutoring Pioneers Alongside Pearson & ElevenLabs
news.summary: Medly AI, founded by UCL medical graduates Dr. Paul Jung and Dr. Kavi Samra, closed an $8M seed round (announced Aug 19, covered through Aug 21) led by Felix Capital with Eka Ventures, Ada Ventures, and angels including InvestEngine CEO Andrey Dobrynin and LearnLaunch GP Jean Hammond. The platform combines seven specialized LLMs for exam prep (GCSE, IGCSE, A-Level, IB; US SAT launching now, AP/ACT by year-end). Reached 400K UK users in ~18 months, with 74% of GCSE users improving at least one grade. Medly was also selected for the UK Dept. for Education's AI Tutoring Tools Pioneers Programme (£300K grant) alongside Pearson and ElevenLabs.

news.title: NetDragon (HK:0777) Signs Serbia's First National-Level AI Education Pilot at GSE2026 — Open-Q Ecosystem Goes Live Internationally
news.summary: At GSE2026 closing ceremony on Aug 20, NetDragon Network (HKEX: 0777) signed Serbia's first national-level AI education pilot with the Serbian Ministry of Education. The agreement covers national curriculum development, digital-infrastructure build-out, and local deployment of NetDragon's AI production center. Serbia's ~4,000 teachers are already being trained in batches at the Belgrade Robotics & AI Education Center (a NetDragon-built facility that has become the Balkans' largest digital education lab). NetDragon also formally launched its "On-Demand Learning" framework with a Springer open-access academic monograph co-authored with international scholars.

news.title: Yiqi Education Technology (NASDAQ: YQ) Launches "Teacher Personalized Agent" at GSE2026 — Building Three-Tier AI Agent Stack (Region / Teacher / Student)
news.summary: At GSE2026's "Digital Transformation Toward Smart Education" parallel session (Aug 19–20), Yiqi Education Technology founder & CEO Liu Chang released a "Teacher Personalized Agent" as part of a three-tier agent system: regional-level agent "Zingo" (deployed in Shanghai Minhang district), teacher personalized agent (released today), and student personalized agent. Capabilities include automated essay grading with class reports, one-click AI-generated test assembly from local question banks, and learning-analytics pipelines from mock-exam data to differentiated teaching recommendations. Zingo has been running as an "Agentic Service" (proactive, not just a Copilot) since 2025.

news.title: Compulsion Games Completes Management Buyout From Xbox, Regains Full IP Rights
news.summary: South of Midnight developer Compulsion Games officially separated from Microsoft/Xbox via a management buyout completed Aug 20–21, regaining ownership of all original IPs (Contrast, We Happy Few, South of Midnight) plus publishing rights. CEO Guillaume Provost: "The team told me we would rather eat rocks and drink gasoline than be split up." Microsoft provided financial runway. The split follows Xbox's July restructuring that cut ~9,000 jobs and led to spinoffs of Double Fine, Ninja Theory, and Undead Labs. Compulsion is now meeting with publishers/financing partners for the next project.

news.title: Double Fine Leaves Xbox — Tim Schafer Regains Full Publishing Rights to Game Catalog
news.summary: Tim Schafer's Double Fine Productions became fully independent from Xbox on Aug 21, regaining publishing rights to its entire game catalog (Psychonauts 1/2, Brütal Legend, Broken Age, Costume Quest, etc.). The studio had been part of Xbox Game Studios since the June 2019 acquisition. This is the second studio to officially exit Microsoft's July restructuring program; Compulsion Games completed its MBO the same day.

news.title: Makers Fund Closes $250M Fund IV — Interactive-Entertainment VC Crosses $1.5B AUM
news.summary: Makers Fund, the London/Reykjavik/Tokyo/Singapore/NYC/LA-based VC focused on interactive entertainment, closed its fourth fund at $250M (announced Aug 20), bringing total AUM to $1.5B. Fund I ($180M, 2016) has returned 3.6x invested capital, putting it in the top 1% of global venture funds. Portfolio includes Dream Games (acquired by CVC at ~$5B), FaceIt ($1.5B exit), Medal/General Intuition ($2.3B), Voldex (Roblox publisher), PixAI, and Bossa Studios. Fund IV will broaden beyond games into consumer apps, entertainment, and creation platforms.

news.title: Riot Games Sunsets Active Development of 2XKO — Free-to-Play Fighter Goes Maintenance Mode by EOY
news.summary: Riot Games announced Aug 20 that active development on its free-to-play League-of-Legends fighting game 2XKO will end in December 2026 after a final bug-fix patch. Servers stay online indefinitely and offline play is unaffected. Two more Champions (Lux in September, Samira in October) will still launch. All Champions unlock for everyone, and Riot is refunding every in-game purchase made on or before Aug 20 across all platforms. After active development ends, Ranked is disabled but skill-based matchmaking remains in Casual.

news.title: Roblox Open-Sources Three Child-Safety AI Models to ROOST — PII Classifier Covers 189 Languages
news.summary: Roblox contributed updated versions of three child-safety AI models to the Robust Open Online Safety Tools (ROOST) Model Community on Aug 19: a PII Classifier v2.0 (F1 score 90.52, up from 63.41; language support 17 → 189), Roblox Sentinel v2 (child-endangerment early-warning; accounted for ~70% of cases Roblox detected in the 12 months ending Aug 7), and voice safety classifier v3 (30 languages, 8 violation categories, 61% recall at 1% FPR, 320M params distilled for real-time). Roblox also released a synthetic-conversation benchmark dataset. ROOST was co-founded by Roblox, Google, OpenAI, and Discord in 2025.

news.title: 4DAnyone: Create Anyone in 4D from a Casual Monocular Video
news.summary: Reconstructs animatable 4D humans from an uncalibrated monocular video by first generating reconstruction-grade, multi-view-consistent videos and then lifting them into 4D Gaussian Splatting. Diagnoses the failure mode of off-the-shelf camera-controlled video diffusion as a bounded-attention-context problem when target views exceed a single DiT pass, and fixes it with two designs: Reference Context Packing compresses growing reference views into fixed-length mixed-resolution context with O(1) reference cost; Target Context Routing rotates target-view groupings during denoising so disjoint groups exchange information. Combined with a new in-house MVGameHuman dataset, 4DAnyone beats prior methods on DNA-Rendering and DyMVHumans in both novel-view quality and downstream 4DGS.

news.title: Are LLMs becoming similarly creative? Evidence from three years of models
news.summary: A preliminary analysis of LLM creative outputs across three years of model releases, using sentence-embedding similarity on two open-ended corpora: Infinity-Chat100 (real open-ended user queries) and the Alternate Uses Task (psychometric creativity benchmark). The headline finding is a statistically significant decrease in model output diversity over time, suggesting LLM outputs are converging in creative substance across models — even as verifiable-answer benchmarks keep climbing. The authors are upfront that this is preliminary: no effect size, no p-value, and no model count in the abstract. If the trend holds, they argue, LLM-driven homogenization will progressively diminish human agency in human-AI co-creation.

news.title: Benchmarking End-to-End Frontier Formal Theoretical Computer Science Research of Large Language Models
news.summary: The first expert-validated benchmark for evaluating LLMs on end-to-end theoretical CS research — not just theorem proving. 175 instances drawn from STOC/FOCS/SODA/COLT 2025-2026 papers, with paper-specific definitions, assumptions, and proof dependencies preserved as expert-verified Lean formalizations. The diagnosis is sharp: autoformalization is the binding bottleneck — the best model scores only 11.5 on translating natural-language claims into formal theorem statements, versus 28.6 Pass@8 when proving a human-provided formal statement. Running their automated TCS research framework (generate → formalize → filter → prove) on 64 generated claims yields only 6 that pass expert evaluation and proof verification — meaning limited "research taste" is the second major wall after formalization.

news.title: ConceptGuard: Benchmarking Context-Sensitive Unlearning in Large Language Models
news.summary: Redefines LLM unlearning evaluation around dual-use concepts — facts that are harmful in one framing and useful in another — instead of disjoint forget/retain sets of independent facts. The ConceptGuard benchmark makes forget and retain sets explicitly complementary in concept usage, and evaluation is intent-sensitive, measuring whether the model separates harmful and benign uses of the same knowledge. Across current unlearning methods, contextual separation is weak, forgetting-utility trade-offs are severe, and concept-level control is inconsistent — and the dataset is released.

news.title: EnvHarness: Awakening Static Worlds for Agent Learning
news.summary: A programmable layer of plug-in components that wraps a static environment to reshape its behaviour without modifying the underlying logic. The motivation: LLM agents learn by interacting with environments that are hand-built, blind to the agent's weaknesses, and quickly obsolete as the agent improves — but rebuilding environments from scratch is engineering-heavy. EnvHarness operates through standard interfaces so it works across domains, and every reshaped environment retains its original verifier. An automated companion, EnvRigger, treats the target policy as a black box, observes execution trajectories, and synthesizes EnvHarness components targeting diagnosed flaws, validating them via fresh rollouts. Across five benchmarks in four domains, EnvHarness beats both the original environments and domain-specific environment-generation pipelines — up to a 9.0-point improvement on held-out instances with 9.8% fewer execution steps, and a superior RL optimization signal for continuous policy-environment co-evolution.

news.title: Inducing Task Models from Computer-Use Traces
news.summary: Formalises Task Model Induction (TMI): from a passive, unconstrained stream of screenshots and mouse/keyboard events, (i) discover the latent tasks being done at the same time and disentangle interleaved activity, then (ii) for each latent task induce a structured task model pairing a hierarchical objective model (recursive goal decomposition) with a procedure model (the control flow that actually executed). On controlled human and agent traces TMI recovers interleaved tasks with 0.974 agreement against ground-truth groupings and reconstructs 74.9% of observed execution steps, far ahead of the strongest workflow-induction baseline; skills lifted out of the task models lift held-out task accuracy by 30.0% over the same baseline.

news.title: Pandora's AI Model Routing Box: Efficient Allocation with Costly Value Estimation
news.summary: Frames LLM/model routing as a Pandora's Box problem: each candidate specialist has an expected return that you have to inspect to estimate , and inspection itself is expensive (cheap embedding-based predictors are noisy; fine-tuned estimators that read retrieval results or partial reasoning traces are accurate but costly). Under a Gaussian signal model, the resulting policies have closed-form value-of-information expressions that decide, per (specialist, input), whether refining the value estimate is worth it. The centralized version is "Pandora's Router"; the decentralized version is "Pandora's Bidder", where specialists decide for themselves whether to invest in self-assessment before accepting a query at an offered price. Across three domains — a standard multi-LLM benchmark, retrieval-augmented specialists, and LLMs with variable inference-time reasoning — Pandora's Router matches the routing quality of exhaustive estimation while calling the expensive estimator far less often.

news.title: ReCache: Efficient KV Cache Reuse and Compression for Tool-Augmented LLM Agents
news.summary: Tool/skill schemas recur across agent requests in different combinations and orders, which kills standard prefix caching. ReCache independently caches resource representations and cuts their inference-time cost in two moves: (1) resource-wise attention removes cross-resource interactions and assigns resource-local positions, yielding composition-invariant KV blocks; (2) it restricts resource visibility to contribution-selected layer-KV-head-group routes and retains only invocation-critical fields via structural + semantic pruning. On a benchmark assembled from seven public tool- and skill-use datasets (including resource-disjoint tests), resource-wise attention matches dense-invocation performance (82.3% vs 82.4% Inv-F1) with a 3.655× time-to-first-token speedup. The full framework cuts allocated KV-tensor memory by 92.43% and accelerates attention by 1.423×.

news.title: Swift-Image: Exploring the Performance Frontier of Compact Unified Image Generation Models
news.summary: A compact 6B-parameter single-stream DiT that unifies text-to-image, single-image editing, and multi-image editing under one set of weights. The training pipeline progresses from broad semantic coverage to higher resolution + stronger visual quality + unified generation-editing supervision; post-training is parallel-expert RL followed by multi-teacher on-policy distillation; a Prompt Enhancer decouples high-level reasoning from pixel rendering; and structural pruning + few-step distillation yield 3B and accelerated variants. Total training budget: 243K GPU-hours. Aggregate benchmarks across editing + generation land the 6B model ahead of evaluated open-source peers, and the 3B compressed variant loses almost nothing.

news.title: WithEveryone: Unified Planning and Identity Grounding for Group Image Generation
news.summary: Generates a group image containing up to ten specified identities without collapsing them. The framework injects each selected identity as an addressed token, predicts a structured identity-layout plan, and renders that plan as a visual condition. The novel Layout-Grounded ID Loss supervises identity directly from annotated face regions instead of unstable embedding-based matching, and ID Representation Forcing pre-trains a per-identity prediction before synthesis. On an identity-disjoint benchmark the model lifts face similarity from 0.462 (GPT-Image-2) to 0.499 while cutting copy-paste artifacts from 0.169 to 0.055, covering 97.3% of requested identities with only 2.8% duplicates.

news.title: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
news.summary: A new benchmark that isolates a single scientific question: can an LLM agent design a better training algorithm? Ten frozen research repositories span ten training-algorithm families; an agent has 4 hours on a single B300 to rewrite the training algorithm, the code is rerun from scratch for up to 12 hours, and a hidden evaluator scores the result against the repo's original algorithm under matched compute. Crucially, no agent can win by collecting more data or tuning hyperparameters — only by changing the algorithm itself.

news.title: Break It Down, Pass It On: Cross-Task Skill Transfer in LLM Agents
news.summary: A controlled study of how the way skills are induced from completed tasks affects whether LLM agents can reuse them later. Two axes are isolated: task-level vs. subtask-level induction, and text vs. code skill formats. Result: task-level skills mostly push the agent below its no-memory baseline, while subtask-level skills lift it above — and text skills transfer better than code skills. The two complementary properties, specificity (match to real tasks) and abstractness (relevance distribution), explain most of the variance.

news.title: Learning When to Think: Adaptive Reasoning for Test-Time Compute Allocation
news.summary: A small, sharp paper that lets the model choose its own reasoning depth inside GRPO. The model emits a first-token mode flag — NoThink (answer fast), Short , or Long — learned end-to-end via a shaped reward plus per-mode token caps so the modes don't collapse. On a 1.5B distilled model trained on MATH, the three modes emerge cleanly, and the brief modes end up more accurate than Long — evidence the router is actually sorting problems by difficulty instead of just running longer.

news.title: MidTool: Mid-training Data Synthesis for Agentic Tool Use
news.summary: Argues that mid-training — not just SFT or RL — is the right stage to bake agentic tool use into a base model. MidTool is an open corpus-construction pipeline that mixes large-scale web/PDF/code data with synthesized supervision from real tool APIs, MCP skills, and document-grounded workflows, and explicitly targets four behaviours: recognizing tool affordances, grounding arguments, composing call workflows, and recovering from incomplete information. Mid-training Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base on MidTool-Mix, then continuing with SFT + RL, beats baselines on agentic tool-use benchmarks.

news.title: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null
news.summary: A controlled audit of LoRA self-training on Qwen3-8B that pushes an untrained frozen control through the identical pipeline and finds seven measurement artifacts that each invert a reported finding without the control. A simple greedy-decode ledger manufactures capability changes on an untrained model (mostly an inference-batching artifact), and the popular "expansion statistic" assigns that same untrained model a 0.280 acquisition rate. The authors replace the natural threshold repair with a per-problem exact test against a pooled baseline.

news.title: Beyond Teacher Likelihood: Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning
news.summary: Diagnoses a real failure mode in on-policy distillation: token-level teacher likelihoods reward locally fluent continuations that miss evidence scattered across long inputs. Proposes group-calibrated OPD that uses response-level verifier signals (graded rewards reflecting partial success) instead of raw teacher probability, with calibration across candidate groups.

news.title: EDITBRIDGE: Towards Faithful and Efficient Ultra-High-Resolution Image Editing
news.summary: Reformulates ultra-HR image editing as a *diffusion bridge* — structured data-to-data translation from a low-res edited result to its 4K counterpart, conditioned on the original HR source — instead of the usual noise-to-image denoising. A prior-guided block-wise sparse attention exploits semantic correspondences from the first-stage edit to restrict cross-image interactions to spatially aligned regions, killing the quadratic cost of attending over a 4K feature map.

news.title: From Corpora to Co-Evolving Capabilities: Capability-Centric Data Design for Generalist Image Generation
news.summary: A capability-driven data infrastructure for generalist image generation that decouples three interoperable data engines (T2I grounding, inter-image transformation, image-knowledge association) and aligns them with a multi-stage curriculum that co-evolves task composition, visual-concept distribution, quality, and resolution along the dependency order of capability acquisition. The pipeline curates 440M T2I images, 120M editing pairs, and 27M image-entity pairs, then trains 3B/6B multimodal diffusion models from scratch and reports SOTA on CPI-Bench.

news.title: GS-VLA: Plug-and-Play Viewpoint Canonicalization for Frozen VLA Policies via Gaussian Splatting
news.summary: A lightweight, retraining-free adapter for Vision-Language-Action policies: when the deployment camera angle drifts from the training view, GS-VLA renders a canonical-view observation via 3D Gaussian Splatting and feeds it to the frozen VLA. First work to use Gaussian Splatting specifically as observation-space adaptation for VLAs, not for policy learning itself.

news.title: Multi-Agent AI System for Radiology Report Structuring and Quality Assurance with Independent Radiologist Evaluation
news.summary: A locally deployed, multi-agent pipeline (regex + local LLM specialists) that structures 22,270 sentences from 638 chest/abdominal/pelvis CT reports into standardized anatomical sections, detects Findings↔Impression mismatches, gender-anatomy conflicts, and undocumented critical-finding communications, and was independently evaluated by two board-certified radiologists on a 45-report subset. They agreed the system correctly restructured 69%, incorrectly 4%, disagreed on 27%, and unanimously found no clinically important omissions or fabricated content.

news.title: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification
news.summary: A rigorous re-evaluation of two memory-based self-improving agents that quantifies variance across seeds and shows that the agent's reported "improvement" is heavily dependent on the *order* in which tasks are presented — meaning prior SOTA claims were riding on a hidden curriculum. The authors trace the failure to task and environment underspecification, and show that adding rubrics and environment feedback into the memory bank partially closes the gap, framing underspecification as the root cause rather than a tuning nuisance.

news.title: ReWEIGH the Evidence: Calibrating Token-Level Ordinal Visual Evidence to Mitigate Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models
news.summary: A decoding-time hallucination mitigation for LVLMs. Instead of pooling raw visual-token logits (whose magnitudes aren't comparable across positions), the method projects each visual state through the output head and uses vocabulary ranks — an ordinal, position-invariant evidence signal — to reweight the next-token distribution so image-implausible tokens get suppressed.

news.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
news.summary: A self-play RL framework where a single LLM simultaneously acts as an Environment Designer (writing executable Gym-style training environments) and a Reasoning Agent that learns inside them. The environments are adaptive: the designer reacts to the agent's current skill frontier so the goal distribution keeps expanding as the learner scales, instead of freezing on a fixed task pool.

news.title: Test-Time Scaling in the Wild: Why Exploitation, Not Exploration, Is the Bottleneck
news.summary: First compute-normalized comparison of five TTS families (best-of-N, beam search, self-refine, etc.) across five open-ended generation benchmarks — medicine, law, finance, general chat, creative writing — instead of the usual math/code stress tests. Headline finding: TTS gains collapse outside easy-to-verify domains, and the binding constraint is how to exploit verifier feedback, not how to explore.

news.title: 5 new ways to level up your learning with Search
news.summary: Here’s how you can use Google Search tools to study for classes and standardized tests.

news.title: AutoResearch: Insight In, Hallucination Out
news.summary: A two-stage autonomous research system that decouples Idea Generation from Idea Execution. Idea Generation continuously fuses emerging signals with accumulated knowledge and uses multi-model generation + cross-review; Idea Execution decomposes plans into experiments with independent evidence-based review. On RSICD, an AutoResearch idea bumps recall from 32.84 to 34.69 while recording only 5 audit-confirmed issues vs 11–27 for competing systems.

news.title: Procedural Content Metageneration via Program Search and Continual Abstraction Discovery
news.summary: Evolves complete Python procedural content generators for Sokoban, Zelda, Dangerous Dave, and Lode Runner using LM mutation/crossover, plus CAD (Continual Abstraction Discovery) that extracts reusable primitives into a run-specific helper module. CAD raises mean final best fitness across all eight domain×API comparisons; learned libraries get adopted by most later programs and repeatedly rediscover validation, reachability, and structural utilities.

news.title: StagedWorkspace: A Versioned Workspace for Knowledge-Work Agents
news.summary: Proposes a workspace-state contract that binds parsed records, review diffs, and submitted artifacts to content hashes of native files. With dual parsed/native access, Gemini 3.1 Pro jumps from 29.3% to 63.9% on OfficeQA, and GPT-5.4 Nano climbs from 25.5 to 42.1 on APEX-Agents — a 2x lift with no model changes.

news.title: TokEval: A Tokenizer Evaluation Suite
news.summary: A principled tokenizer evaluation framework that goes beyond fertility and compression, measuring UTF-8 boundary integrity, digit place-value alignment, and other structurally meaningful properties. Information-theoretic metrics predict language modeling ability (Spearman ρ up to 0.80), while structure-sensitive metrics correlate with downstream task accuracy across linguistic, math, and code benchmarks.

news.title: Tuned Diffusion Sampling with Bayesian Optimization (OYS)
news.summary: Treats diffusion-model timestep selection as a black-box optimization problem and optimizes sample quality directly with Bayesian Optimization. A 5-step OYS schedule retains 89–94% of a 50-step schedule's quality, slashing inference cost by 10x. Beats "Align Your Steps" on text-to-image and improves inpainting, working with both simple Euler and DPM-Solver++ samplers without retraining.

news.title: An Empirical Study of Training Pixel-Space Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
news.summary: Pixel-space diffusion models are usually dismissed as too expensive vs. latent diffusion, but no large-scale recipe had been published. The authors run a comprehensive empirical study and find that direct large-scale pixel-space pre-training converges much slower than latent, but a latent-to-pixel post-training strategy recovers the gap. They systematically ablate weight init, data mix, prediction target, decoder, and noise schedule, and produce a recipe whose pixel-space models match or beat their latent-space counterparts at 3.18–4.75× inference speedup .

news.title: ClawGym II: Exploring Black-Box RL on Agent Harness
news.summary: RL training of long-horizon LLM agents through complex agent harnesses has been hard because (a) the harness is opaque, (b) multi-turn trajectories explode, and (c) training/inference consistency is fragile. ClawGym II provides a sandboxed concurrent-rollout infra , a serving proxy at the model boundary that captures calls into prefix trees, and a unified framework that runs both PPO and GRPO over the reconstructed tree. A new mix-harness training mode lets a single model be optimized across heterogeneous harnesses (OpenClaw and Claude Code are tested together). With Qwen3-30A3B, Pass@1 on ClawGym-Bench improves by 9.98 through OpenClaw and 14.81 through Claude Code, stable across 200–400 optimization steps.

news.title: Improving the Matrix Multiplication Exponent with Modern Optimization and AlphaEvolve
news.summary: A new upper bound on the matrix multiplication exponent ω < 2.371177 (vs. the previous record 2.371339 from Alman et al., 2025). The authors reformulate the combination-loss-analysis optimization problem so it can be solved in a larger setting, design a new ML-driven optimizer, then refine it with AlphaEvolve — the same evolutionary-coding loop DeepMind has used to rediscover Strassen-style tricks.

news.title: Proteus: Incremental Memory Activation for Long-Context Sequence Modeling
news.summary: Memory-based sequence models (Titans, Comba, SWLA, Hope-Attention) expose a static memory of fixed capacity for the whole context. Early tokens then over-occupy that memory with no compression pressure, "polluting" it and starving later context. Proteus makes the active memory grow over time — early tokens get a small budget and are forced to compress; later tokens unlock fresh capacity. Plug-in, parameter-free, drops into SWLA / Comba / Titans / Hope-Attention, and gains grow with sequence length .

news.title: Bank Leumi Partners with Galaxy to Bring BTC, ETH, SOL Trading to 2.5M Israeli Customers in 2027
news.summary: Bank Leumi — Israel's largest lender — will let its ~2.5M retail customers buy, hold and sell Bitcoin, Ether, and Solana directly inside its mobile banking app starting in early 2027. Galaxy Digital supplies trading infrastructure (GalaxyOne Institutional) and custody (Custody Infrastructure, formerly GK8). Final sign-off from the Bank of Israel is still pending. This is Leumi's second attempt — a 2022 Paxos partnership was shelved when regulators declined approval.

news.title: BitGo Captures 27.5% of $26.6B Real-World Asset Market, Overtakes Securitize, Ondo, BlackRock
news.summary: Token Terminal data (Aug 15, 18:00 UTC) shows BitGo now holds $7.3B in TVL across real-world asset issuers — 27.5% of the $26.6B sector — ranking first among 21 tracked issuers. Securitize is second at 14.9% ($4.0B), Ondo Finance third at 13.4% ($3.6B), and BlackRock fourth at 10.3% ($2.7B). The RWA market as a whole has grown 156.4% over the measurement period, with Ethereum hosting 56.6% of issuer TVL.

news.title: Cboe BZX Files for First 3x Leveraged Bitcoin and Ether ETFs in the U.S.
news.summary: Cboe's BZX Exchange filed proposed rule change SR-CboeBZX-2026-065 (submitted Aug 10, 2026; publicly reported Aug 16) to list the first 3x leveraged Bitcoin and Ether ETFs in the United States. The funds, sponsored by Volatility Shares LLC, target 3x daily performance of Bitcoin and Ether via CME futures rather than spot. Critically, the Bitcoin fund is structured as a commodity pool under CFTC oversight rather than the Investment Company Act — a novel legal architecture that lets it bypass the SEC's investment-company framework.

news.title: Tether CEO Denies Plans for Proprietary Blockchain Days After First-Ever KPMG Full Audit
news.summary: Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino publicly denied on X (Aug 15) that Tether is building its own blockchain, after CoinMarketCap had grouped Tether with Stripe (Tempo) and Circle (Arc) as "stablechain" issuers. The clarification came just days after Tether completed its first-ever full independent financial statement audit with KPMG U.S., which issued an unqualified opinion on Tether International Limited's 2025 financials. USDT supply stands at ~184.6B with >60% stablecoin market share.

news.title: World Liberty Financial Wins Conditional OCC Trust Bank Charter for $4B USD1 Stablecoin
news.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted World Liberty Trust Company preliminary conditional approval to operate as a national trust bank, moving USD1 stablecoin issuance under direct federal supervision. USD1's ~$4B market cap makes it the fourth-largest stablecoin. The charter shifts issuance away from BitGo Bank & Trust, which had served as USD1's exclusive issuer/custodian. World Liberty joins Ripple, Fidelity, Paxos, and Circle among OCC-conditionally-approved crypto firms. The charter does not include FDIC insurance or a Fed master account.

news.title: Get closer to the game with Gemini and Pixel
news.summary: Google Gemini and Pixel partner with five global football clubs to elevate the fan matchday experience through AI and Smartphone Technology.

news.title: AgentRewind: Recoverable Execution for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
news.summary: Long-horizon agents suffer cascading errors: a bad early action corrupts both the agent's context and the environment, and subsequent "fixes" can't undo it because the world has moved on. AgentRewind records aligned checkpoints of (agent context, controlled environment) so the agent can rewind to any earlier state and resume execution with information from prior attempts. The companion MettleBench evaluates long-horizon engineering tasks with checklists of related requirements.

news.title: Intern-S2-Mobius: Foundation Model with Decoupled Knowledge and Reasoning
news.summary: Introduces Mobius-v0, a knowledge-reasoning-separation architecture with one globally shared Memory (FFN) storing knowledge vectors plus multiple Reasoners (Self-Attn) that iteratively query it via hidden-state carriers. A 7B model trained from scratch matches a strong 7B Transformer baseline using only 62.6% of the training tokens , and the continually-pretrained Intern-S2-Mobius (from Qwen3.5-35B) matches the baseline downstream score while delivering nearly 4× end-to-end inference speedup .

news.title: MathForm: Scaling Mathematical Autoformalization with Knowledge Retrieval and Verification-Guided Refinement
news.summary: Autoformalization to Lean 4 / Mathlib has been bottlenecked by library-specific knowledge and brittle single-pass generation. MathForm (a) retrieves relevant Mathlib definitions and prior formalizations before generation, (b) revises outputs using compiler diagnostics and semantic-consistency feedback, and (c) produces FormalVerse , a Lean 4 dataset of ~ 367K verified examples across diverse mathematical domains. The resulting MathForm-8B reaches 88.06% Syntax-Check Pass@8 and 72.3% (truncated in abstract) type-correct rate across six Lean 4 benchmarks, after SFT + RL.

news.title: SheetCompass: Hierarchical Relation Graphs for Agentic Spreadsheet Reasoning
news.summary: Spreadsheet reasoning is a notorious failure mode for LLMs because real workbooks hide cross-table associations, fine-grained column dependencies, and complex spatial layouts that get flattened away by linearization. SheetCompass builds a hierarchical graph across worksheets, keeps task-relevant state in memory, and dispatches an agentic LLM that reasons over the global spatial context instead of a serialized string dump.

news.title: Wyvern: An Agentic Framework for Generating Grounded Multimodal Reports
news.summary: Wyvern is a multi-agent framework for synthesizing grounded technical reports that mix text, tables, images, and citations end-to-end. The pipeline emphasizes information grounding via a claims auto-revision stage and unifies multimodal outputs into a single report schema. Human evaluation finds figure informativeness beats a recent baseline in 87% of cases; reports rated more useful than 3 alternatives in 63–100% of instances; automated metrics show up to 2.3× citation recall and 1.6× citation precision gains.

news.title: Cardinal Glass to Install World-First Carbon Capture System at Float Glass Plant
news.summary: Cardinal Glass Industries will install what it calls the world's first carbon capture system at its Cardinal FG float glass facility in Winlock, Washington. The system is expected to capture ~130,000 metric tons of CO2 per year and remove up to 95% of CO2 from targeted process streams. The announcement coincides with a parallel Saint-Gobain/AGC electric float glass furnace project.

news.title: European Energy Closes €234.1M Financing for 225 MW Italian Agrivoltaic Project
news.summary: European Energy has reached financial close on €234.1 million in project financing from Credit Agricole CIB, Intesa Sanpaolo, NORD/LB, and Société Générale for the 225 MW Vizzini agrivoltaic project in Sicily, Italy. The facility is integrated with continued agricultural use and biodiversity measures, and benefits from a 20-year Contract for Difference under Italy's FerX scheme. COD targeted for 2028.

news.title: Microsoft PPA-Backed 150 MW Carwarp Solar Park Enters Operation in Australia
news.summary: Recurrent Energy (a Canadian Solar subsidiary) has energized its 150 MWac Carwarp Energy Park in Victoria, Australia ahead of schedule. The project is underpinned by a long-term PPA with Microsoft, uses ~243,000 TOPCon modules from Canadian Solar, and will generate ~405 GWh/year — enough for ~65,000 Australian households. The site has planning approval for a follow-on 120 MW battery storage system.

news.title: OGCI Releases Strategic CCS Deployment Roadmap for Asia-Pacific
news.summary: The Oil and Gas Climate Initiative (OGCI) released a new report titled "CCS in the Asia-Pacific Region," prepared in partnership with the Global CCS Institute. The report examines deployment barriers, financing models, and policy needs across major Asia-Pacific economies — including Japan, Korea, China, Indonesia, and Australia — where industrial CO2 emissions are still rising.

news.title: Saudi Arabia Completes $8.5B NEOM Green Hydrogen Megaproject
news.summary: NEOM Green Hydrogen Company (JV between ACWA Power, Air Products, and NEOM) has completed construction of the world's largest green hydrogen facility at Oxagon in NEOM, Saudi Arabia. The $8.5 billion project has entered the commissioning phase and is expected to produce up to 600 tons of carbon-free hydrogen per day once fully operational, backed by an integrated 4 GW solar + wind power system. Commercial green ammonia exports are targeted for 2027.

news.title: Alaya-EVOKE: From Linear-Scaling Supervision to Endless World
news.summary: An interactive video world model that externalizes persistent scene state into a camera-indexed 3D world-state bank (view-relevant retrieval only) so the denoiser context stays bounded as sessions grow. The teacher uses sparse attention with chunk-wise grouping + selected-distant-frame retrieval + a linear-attention global state, giving linear memory/compute growth over long horizons. A 30-second distribution-matching objective transfers these capabilities to a 3-step student that runs without classifier-free guidance, generating a 1.5 s 384×640 chunk in 2.11 s on a single H200 and hitting SOTA on WBench while staying competitive on VBench-Long and VBench-2.0.

news.title: DARTree: Speculative Diffusion Decoding with Autoregressive Draft Trees
news.summary: A training-free speculative-decoding method that combines a diffusion drafter (predicts a whole token block in parallel) with an AR-style verification tree. DARTree expands a fixed-width candidate tree at every depth in one batch, then best-first prunes to a verification tree so the AR correction head carries causal information down every branch.

news.title: Intern-S2-Preview: Scientific Agentic Foundation Model
