news.summary: Shanghai AI Lab releases Intern-S2-Preview, a 397B-parameter scientific agentic foundation model trained with a unified post-training stack (SFT + multi-task RL + black/white-box agentic RL + on-policy distillation), plus a separate Intern-MemDec-4B memory-augmented extension that adapts to new scientific domains without touching the frozen 397B backbone. The system is explicitly built for long-horizon tool use across heterogeneous scientific evidence (rendered documents, interleaved image-text, time series).

news.title: OmniScientist: An Omni-Modal Omni-Discipline AI Scientist
news.summary: An end-to-end AI scientist that ingests heterogeneous raw scientific evidence (images, signals, audio, video, 3-D structures, trajectories, tables, formulae, graphs) and runs a perception layer + three autonomous agents (ideation, experiment, writeup) inside a deterministic pipeline. Statistical validity, novelty screening, and numerical traceability are enforced in code rather than prompting. Evaluated on 36 real-data cases across 5 discipline families, it produces a compiled manuscript in all 36 and wins 85% of head-to-head judgments against a blind variant that only sees precomputed scalar features.

news.title: Vero: Can AI Agents Build Formally Verified Software Repositories?
news.summary: The first benchmark for joint implementation + proof synthesis at repository scale: 43 multi-module Lean 4 instances drawn from real Python/Dafny/Verus/Coq projects across crypto protocols, distributed systems, and more, with curated specs and reference implementations. Frontier coding-agent configs with Lean toolchain access fully solve only 27 of 43 and close zero specs on the hardest repositories.

news.title: Bring your spreadsheet data to life with Sheets canvas
news.summary: Sheets canvas turns data into interactive dashboards, custom study trackers, seating charts, and more, all with a simple prompt.

news.title: AI4AI at Test-Time: Strong-to-Weak Capability Transfer via Harnesses
news.summary: Asks whether a stronger "builder" model can transfer capability to a weaker "target" model at test time , without any parameter updates, by constructing inference-time harnesses (routing, code, format enforcement). On four Theory-of-Mind benchmarks, the harness nearly doubles the target model's average accuracy from 0.49 to 0.91. The gains come mostly from offloading unstable reasoning into deterministic code and strict output formats, not from more sampling or longer chain-of-thought.

news.title: AVA-Encoder: Towards Agent-Native Video Representation Learning
news.summary: Proposes an Agentic Video Auto-Encoder that turns a video into a structured knowledge graph (KG) with hierarchy/state nodes for text and a linked asset layer for generated images/audio/video, then reconstructs it back. Reconstruction differences drive a textual-gradient optimization loop that produces natural-language update directions for both data-independent encoding policy pseudo-training and test-time data-dependent KG refinement. The agent can query, edit, and reason about the KG directly.

news.title: Information Abundance Paradox: Long-Context Training Undermines Parametric Knowledge
news.summary: Challenges the standard assumption that scaling context windows is strictly beneficial. The authors define the Information Abundance Paradox : when abundant relevant information is present in the training context, the model has less incentive to internalize it into its parameters, shifting learning from parametric memory to contextualization. Empirically, pretraining context length improves language modeling, NLU, and closed-book MCQA only up to an intermediate sweet spot, after which performance consistently declines; in SFT, more task-relevant context improves with-support results but reduces robustness when context is absent or misleading.

news.title: One Frozen Simulator Is Not Enough: Simulator Collapse in Multi-Agent RL
news.summary: Diagnoses a systematic failure mode in multi-agent RL for human-AI interaction: when a single LLM is used as the user simulator, its mode-collapsed distribution causes the policy to overfit to that simulator's dominant mode, and the resulting policy fails to transfer to unseen simulators or real humans. The paper formalizes simulator collapse and proposes two complementary fixes — Verbalized Sampling at inference time (sample from a verbalized response distribution) and Co-Training at training time (jointly optimize against a population of trainable simulators). On Persuasion-for-Good, τ²-bench, and CooperBench, Verbalized Sampling adds up to +9% held-out success and Co-Training pushes gains to +14%.

news.title: VAKRA: Evaluating Multi-Hop Reasoning Across APIs and Retrieval Under Tool-Use Policies
news.summary: VAKRA evaluates agents across 8,000+ executable APIs in 62 domains with three difficulty tiers: diverse API interaction styles, multi-hop reasoning over structured APIs, and multi-source reasoning under natural-language tool-use policies. Correctness is verified by re-executing predicted tool calls against live APIs, accepting multiple valid paths. Using a fixed ReAct harness to isolate model capability from agent scaffolding, the best frontier model hits only 70.4% on single-hop endpoint tasks and drops to 50–51% on compositional APIs; reasoning depth costs >50% accuracy, and policy-constrained questions expose failures as low as 2.4% on unanswerable queries.

news.title: Attention-Path Fragility as an Uncertainty Signal in Large Language Models
news.summary: Introduces ASMI (Attention-Subnetwork Mutual Information), a training-free uncertainty estimator that masks attention heads and measures BALD-style disagreement among the resulting subnetworks. Crucially, it works from a single greedy response (no need for the 10 stochastic samples that Semantic Entropy requires) and ties or beats Semantic Entropy on 10 of 12 grounded QA benchmark-backbone settings, cutting retained error of a confidence filter roughly in half on confident-but-fragile predictions.

news.title: Long-Horizon AI Research for Grothendieck Constant: A Case Study in Human-AI Mathematical Collaboration
news.summary: Reports that an AI research system tightened the known bounds on the Grothendieck constant KG to 6π/11 ≤ KG ≤ π/(2 log(1+√2)) − 10⁻⁴, with the AI's intermediate steps deemed genuinely novel by domain experts. The paper is framed as a candid case study — not just the wins, but also where the AI got stuck and what conditions unlocked breakthroughs.

news.title: Test-Time Self-Evolving GUI Visual Grounding via Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation
news.summary: Proposes a closed-loop Explore → Evaluate → Reflect → Internalize framework that lets GUI-grounding models keep improving after deployment with no human labels. A MLLM Reflector grades each exploration, and Reflection-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation turns the critique into dense token-level supervision, with Contrastive Calibration guarding against corrupted prefixes. Reports +7.4% average accuracy over the base model across six GUI-grounding benchmarks; claimed first successful on-policy self-distillation for test-time GUI adaptation.

news.title: V-FiLLM: Verified Financial LLM Reasoning Benchmark
news.summary: Builds financial-reasoning benchmark items from executable computation trees over real tables — answers are correct-by-construction because the trees are evaluated symbolically, so no LLM touches the labels. Sweeps four axes (depth, breadth, concept complexity, context size) and shows open-source model accuracy drops up to 51% with reasoning depth and 47 points under adversarial numeric perturbations; a small LoRA on verified CoT traces lifts accuracy 81.1% → 85.6% in-domain and +5 pp on FinQA.

news.title: Why Does CLAUDE.md Keep Growing? Catastrophic Remembering in Agentic Coding
news.summary: Empirical study across 1,867 repositories and 247,694 instruction lifetimes showing that agentic-coding prompts (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md) grow without bound, tripling (+226%) over a repo's life with +4.9 net instructions per commit, because deleting an instruction costs O(2^|D|) to verify safety once its rationale is gone. The author names this catastrophic remembering — the inverse of catastrophic forgetting — and shows that prompt comments encoding latent reasoning cut 99.3% of the bloat in synthetic worlds and lift real-world IFE follow-rate by up to 23.1%.

news.title: BDH-CQ: In-Context Learning with Recurrent Latent Reasoning
news.summary: A reasoning model that fuses in-context learning with a recurrent latent state: the model's hidden memory keeps getting rewritten by the input, and it solves a query through iterative computation in a high-dimensional latent space — without ever verbalizing intermediate steps. Evaluated on ARC-AGI-1 with a 150M config and ARC-like controlled interventions to probe what gets learned from demonstrations.

news.title: Evo-Bench: Can Language Models Improve Agent Harness?
news.summary: First benchmark for harness-evolution — measuring whether an LLM can autonomously optimize its own agent harness (search / office / general agents). Uses a harness-guided construction framework to isolate harness improvement from base model strength and prevent task-specific overfitting.

news.title: Intent Speaks Louder: Controllable User Simulation Beyond Response Imitation
news.summary: UserIDA — a user simulator that exposes per-turn interaction intent as an explicit directive, separating what the user wants to do next from how they say it. Uses a six-way intent interface, SFT for directive-conditioned generation, and intent-calibrated RL group optimization. On LMSYS-USP, 86.6% intent accuracy (+24.3 pts vs strongest baseline).

news.title: Macaron-V1: Towards Open Continual Learning with Self-Improvement and Mixture-of-LoRA
news.summary: An open agent-model family for "experiential intelligence": versions of model+harness pair are recursively improved via an external success contract, and at serving time a frozen base model routes each user turn to one specialist LoRA adapter (Mixture-of-LoRA). The flagship "Venti" config is the first open continual-learning setup with this composition.

news.title: Sci-VBench: Evaluating Knowledge- and Reasoning-Intensive Video Generation in Science Domains
news.summary: A benchmark of 1,253 expert-annotated prompts across 60 subjects in natural science, healthcare, humanities & social sciences, and engineering, with a rubric-based evaluation protocol. Tasks force generated videos to be temporally coherent AND knowledge-grounded, not just visually pretty.

news.title: SWE-Bench ProMax: Benchmarking Agents on Large-Scale Multilingual Code Refactoring
news.summary: A new expert-curated, multilingual code-refactoring benchmark of 170 instances across 7 languages (Python, Java, TS, Go, C, C++, Rust). Issue descriptions are rewritten from scratch and tests are manually reviewed to remove the false-positive / false-negative traps that plague SWE-bench Verified. Average task = 11.4 files / 261.6 LoC.

news.title: Towards Expert-level Medical AI for Real-time Video Consultations
news.summary: AMIE (Articulate Medical Intelligence Engine) extended from text-only to real-time audio-visual clinical consultation. Trained on multimodal doctor-patient dialog with non-verbal cues; evaluated against clinicians on OSCE-style scenarios and shown to reach expert-level agreement.

news.title: CreativeInstruct: Scalably Teaching LLMs to Balance Quality, Creativity, and Diversity
news.summary: Post-training collapses LLM output diversity/creativity — bad for explicit tasks like story generation and bad for implicit ones like RL rollouts. CreativeInstruct learns to inject a special [StartCreativity] span that biases generation toward creativity without sacrificing post-trained quality. Introduces a structural diversity metric based on graph edit distance on textual idea graphs. Human raters call CreativeInstruct generations more creative than post-trained baselines 70.3% of the time , and GRPO on top of a CreativeInstruct checkpoint adds +~4% on AMC, +~5pp on MATH over the same training on the post-trained base.

news.title: Fisher-R1: Training LLM Agents for Reliable Hypothesis Testing
news.summary: Current LLM agents run hypothesis-testing code correctly but ship statistically invalid conclusions (wrong p-values, wrong test choices). The team builds P-Bench , 425 open-ended hypothesis-testing tasks across economics, biology, and medicine, and trains Fisher-R1-14B via synthetic tasks + verified-reward RL. Beats GPT-5.4 and DeepSeek-V4-Pro by +21% single-trial success on average (up to +26% on the hardest slice).

news.title: Modular TTT: Rethinking Test-Time Training as Composable Modules
news.summary: TTT variants (Mamba/Titans-style fast weights) are usually hard-coded monolithically — hard to ablate, hard to invent new ones. Modular TTT casts the inner learner as a DAG over five exposed knobs (fast-weight network, loss, LR init, weight decay, normalization) and auto-assembles train-view forward/backward + causal query-view rules. Ablations land three robust wins: small LR init, weight decay, and a single-layer nonlinearity ; deeper fast-weight nets and normalization actually hurt . Best variant trained to 410M / 1.45B params on 100B tokens matches Gated DeltaNet on loss and benchmarks.

news.title: SimWAM: A Simple World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
news.summary: A "World-Action Model" that uses video generation only as a training signal : co-trains a pretrained video expert with a lightweight action expert via joint flow matching, then discards the video branch at inference . Isolated attention masks keep action prediction independent of future frames, so the planner ships as a self-contained trajectory predictor. Adds a compositional RL reward on top. Hits 91.5 PDMS on NAVSIM (beats WAM SOTA at lower latency) and zero-shot transfers to nuScenes.

news.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
news.summary: Introduces U-OPSD : on-policy self-distillation that uses only the model's own generations , with no ground truth, no environment reward, and no larger teacher. Algorithm: sample N rollouts, take a self-consistency majority-vote pseudo-solution, condition a teacher distribution on the shortest one, distill it into the prefixes of the longest wrong completion. On AIME24/25, HMMT25, MATH500, AMC23: Qwen3 non-thinking improves +8.5% / +10.7% over its base model — matching or beating OPSD with ground truth and GRPO .

news.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
news.summary: Diagnoses why generative reward models (GRMs) underperform in RL despite being strong rankers: there's a mismatch between their comparative nature and RL's scalar scoring paradigm. RRC fixes this by deriving scalar rewards from preference rankings with two complementary strategies — self-competitive ranking (across sampled responses) and anchor-guided ranking (against a small reference set). Consistent gains across open-ended chat and reasoning benchmarks.

news.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
news.summary: Systematic empirical comparison of programmatic tool calling (PTC) — exposing tools as typed Python stubs the model invokes as code — vs native JSON tool calling across 14 LLMs on Berkeley Function-Calling Leaderboard v4 . PTC matches or beats JSON calling in 11 of 14 models, the GPT-5.6 family gains +10.6% , and PTC stays stable under context rot where JSON calling degrades 2.3% on average.

news.title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
news.summary: Trace-grounded parametric profiling for event counting in video: 2,190 controlled videos across bouncing-ball contacts, blinks, and state transitions, with executable event traces that audit reported events against ground truth. Result on Gemini 3.6 Flash: at the 80% reliability threshold it counts persistent state transitions up to 12 events at 0.5/1.0 Hz, but has no reliable positive-count region for transient blinks . In the high-count/high-frequency regime only 0.2% of final counts are correct and just 18.1% of true events are recovered. Increasing frame sampling boosts Bounce Ball accuracy 19.6%→29.3% but the reported sequence agrees with ground truth only 3.7% of the time — i.e. extra frames inflate final scores without producing faithful recovery.

news.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
news.summary: Reframes "robustness to misleading context" as selective trust : a good LLM should ignore bad signals but use good ones. Introduces MIST , a 4-condition human-annotated benchmark (clean / misleading / correct-context / irrelevant-context) plus the SC2W metric, and proposes SCOPE , a DPO-style training that mines clean-correct vs. misleading-wrong pairs and balances them across all four conditions.

news.title: Beyond Top-K: Replacing Black-Box Retrieval with Interpretable Agentic Operations
news.summary: Argues that for structured documents — financial statements, audit reports, regulatory filings — top-k embedding retrieval is structurally unsound, and makes the case measurable. On a 780-page government financial report, 86.8% of content lines are table rows, thousands of near-identical figures share one embedding space, and a figure inherits its unit from a header a median of 13 lines above it (so chunk boundaries routinely split “crore” from “lakh” — a two-orders-of-magnitude error). The proposed READ (Reliable Embedding-free Agentic Document-search) gives an agent three deterministic operations — normalized lexical search, structural navigation, bounded span reads — exposed over MCP, so the trajectory is a replayable audit trail. On 51 verified questions READ answers 58.8% vs dense retrieval’s 15.7% (p Holm = 2×10⁻⁵); a top-k-tool agent on the same loop only reaches 27.5%, locating the gain in the interface rather than in iteration count.

news.title: MASS: Multiplayer World Models with Authoritative Shared State
news.summary: Video world models today entangle world dynamics with view-dependent visual latents, which (i) wastes compute across agents, (ii) creates cross-view inconsistency, (iii) kills scalability in multiplayer settings. MASS splits them: a learned Logic Engine advances a global, typed, authoritative state from joint actions (no hand-written transitions, it is the sole recurrent memory), and a learned Rendering Engine renders any camera on demand from that shared state. The architecture lets the model hold 1,024 concurrent players for 10,000 recurrent steps on a matched multiplayer Snake benchmark, with better state accuracy and lower cross-view inconsistency than multi-view baselines.

news.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
news.summary: A genuinely unsupervised variant of On-Policy Self-Distillation. The model samples multiple rollouts, takes a majority-vote pseudo-solution (with a self-consistency threshold), then distills from a teacher distribution conditioned on the shortest pseudo-solution into the prefixes of its own longest incorrect completions — i.e. it surgically corrects itself exactly where it is confidently wrong. Across AIME24/25, HMMT25, MATH500, AMC23 the method beats OPSD-with-ground-truth and GRPO: +8.5% / +10.7% over the base model at Qwen3-4B / 8B non-thinking, and +3.2% / +2.3% over OPSD-GT. Thinking mode holds up too, surpassing GRPO by 0.7–1.1 points.

news.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
news.summary: Diagnoses why generative reward models (GenRMs) underperform in RL despite being strong rankers: it is a paradigm mismatch — GenRMs are comparative, RL rewards are scalars. RRC fixes this by deriving scalar rewards from relative preference rankings via two complementary strategies: self-competitive ranking (comparing sampled responses against each other) and anchor-guided ranking (using a small reference set for scalable ranking-based reward construction). Across open-ended chat and reasoning benchmarks RRC consistently beats prior reward-construction approaches when plugging GenRMs into RL.

news.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
news.summary: A systematic comparison of Programmatic Tool Calling (PTC) — where tools are exposed as typed Python stubs the model invokes through code in a single agent turn — against native JSON tool calling across 14 LLMs on the BFCL v4 benchmark. PTC matches or beats JSON in 11/14 models, with the GPT-5.6 family gaining +10.6% over JSON. The wins hold under parallel fan-out (13/14 models) and under context rot, where the JSON baseline degrades 2.3% on average while PTC stays stable. The authors frame this as another “bitter lesson” variant: as models get more code-capable, expressing tool use as code generalizes better than hand-designed structured-output schemas.

news.title: Logic Before Language: Pre-pretraining on Formal Derivations Fosters Skill Acquisition and Compressibility
news.summary: Proposes "Logic-PPT": pre-pretraining on formal logical derivations before natural language. Scaled to a 100B-token regime, the approach reaches 80% on linguistic tasks using 36B fewer tokens than a standard initialization and outperforms prior symbolic pre-pretraining baselines (Dyck, procedural algorithms). Mechanistically, formal derivations induce a lower-rank, spectrally concentrated representation that survives pruning — the dense baseline is matched even at ~33% sparsity.

news.title: ParVL: Parallel Scaling and Expandable Compute Allocation for Multimodal LLMs
news.summary: A parallel vision-language scaling framework that reuses a fixed ViT+LLM backbone across multiple vision/language branches via branch-specific prefix parameters, then studies how shared-backbone compute should be split between the ViT encoder and LLM decoder. End-to-end full-parameter SFT on ~13B tokens; code released.

news.title: SocietyBench: Forecasting Counterfactual Social-World Evolution
news.summary: End-to-end benchmark for LLM social forecasting: turn a one-line event topic into a date-indexed timeline of factual events plus a public-opinion layer, then replace every named entity and shift every date by a per-event constant — producing a structurally identical counterfactual world that defeats memorization. Questions are scored on two orthogonal 100-point axes (probability calibration, temporal accuracy); five events, 125 prediction points, zh/en editions.

news.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
news.summary: A systematic account of test-time scaling that breaks it into three structural regimes — single-trajectory sequential, leaf-level with terminal reduction, and prefix-level — and argues the evaluated object is the entire inference system, not the base model. The authors define an evaluation profile whose functionals recover or bound common repeated-sampling metrics, prescribe protocol-matched compute and uncertainty reporting, and lay out reproducibility tiers (exact replay vs distributional).

news.title: Video-DeepResearch: Towards the Next-Generation Multimodal Deepresearch Agent
news.summary: Extends multimodal deep-research agents from static images to long video streams, with a decoupled perception–exploration pipeline and stage-wise tool unlocking that forces exhaustive cross-frame visual grounding before web retrieval. Training is SFT followed by Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to break the imitation-learning ceiling. The authors also curate Video-DR-Bench: 200 multi-source questions co-built by humans and AI.

news.title: AtumAI: A Principled Framework for Agentic Generation of Datacenter Control-Plane Policies
news.summary: Out-of-the-box agentic AI for datacenter control-plane design is "not formal, not transferable, not systematic" — no structured problem statement, no cross-task transfer, and the LLM alone narrows the search to a thin slice of the design space. AtumAI splits the work into two pieces: the Datacenter Task Compiler turns a plain-English goal into a machine-checkable spec (objectives, constraints, decision variables, evaluation), and the Evolutionary Design Discovery Loop expands the search beyond the LLM via a diffusion model + evolutionary algorithm + surrogate. On workload placement, resource scaling, and power management, AtumAI's policies beat expert-engineered baselines.

news.title: AURORA-LM: Autoencoding Unified Representation for Continuous-Latent Diffusion Language Modeling
news.summary: Argues that text is the outlier in generative modelling — images/video/audio all sit in continuous latent spaces, text still rides on discrete tokens — and ships a continuous-latent diffusion language model that keeps a high-capacity, decodable text latent while learning its distribution via a block-causal DiT and flow matching. A query-based encoder-decoder organises text into prefix-aligned latents, the diffusion model generates blocks left-to-right while denoising positions within each block in parallel, and the authors add a width-calibrated noise schedule plus a self-trajectory-consistency loss to keep iterative denoising on-distribution at inference.

news.title: CMuon: Accelerating and Stabilizing Diffusion Transformer Training via Chunked Momentum Orthogonalization
news.summary: Diagnoses why vanilla Muon underperforms on DiTs: DiT architectures fuse functionally distinct weights (AdaLN, QKV) into unified tensors for efficiency, and applying Muon to those fused tensors induces an implicit subspace coupling that distorts the update direction. CMuon simply partitions the fused matrices into independent sub-components before orthogonalisation. On ImageNet 256, a 675M DiT trained with CMuon reaches FID 1.18 in 200 epochs — ~2x training speedup over AdamW and no late-stage convergence plateau.

news.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
news.summary: Existing test-time latent-reasoning methods route gradient signal through decoded tokens, so credit assignment is indirect and the link between latent updates and the actual reasoning trajectory is opaque. GradCuit inserts optimisable latent states at a chosen Transformer layer; causal self-attention then gives every continuation-token log-prob a differentiable path back to every preceding latent, so reward-weighted gradients from the entire continuation land directly on the latents. Across five instruction-tuned backbones and three reasoning benchmarks, GradCuit averages 64.5% (+6.6 over CoT, +2.4 over the strongest baseline) and is markedly more stable across learning-rate sweeps (std 0.82 vs 1.53).

news.title: onepot-Bench 0: Towards Lab-Aware In Silico Chemistry Benchmarks
news.summary: Targets the gap that public-domain chemistry benchmarks cannot tell whether an LLM "knows" chemistry or has memorised answers from training corpora. onepot-Bench 0 is a three-part proprietary evaluation suite: ChemAbacus (tool-free cheminformatics literacy + numerical reasoning), SynthRefusal (safety / refusal behaviour across benign, controlled, and designer-drug targets), and SynthBench (reaction-outcome prediction and catalyst selection on private wet-lab data generated in the authors' own lab).

news.title: Pseudorandom Streams within Diffusion Models Act as Learnable Inputs That Affect Generation Quality
news.summary: Diffusion models are supposed to consume "noise", but on finite-precision hardware that noise is a deterministic orbit through a pseudorandom generator — and the realised training loss depends on the concrete PRNG values consumed at each step. The authors measure orbit predictability with a small MLP, then run a "diffusion probe" that swaps real images for online random tensors and asks whether the loss / sample quality still degrades on the same orbits. After controlling marginal statistics and screening out clear dynamical / finite-precision failures, the remaining orbits still produce significantly different diffusion losses and generation quality on MNIST and CIFAR-10, and probe loss vs real-data loss follow an empirical power law.

news.title: Structured Memory for Edge Language Models: Persistent Context and Corpus Retrieval via O(1) SSM State Injection (PRECOG)
news.summary: Exploits the unique property of state-space models — the fixed-size, position-agnostic recurrent state is a complete summary of everything read — to collapse RAG prefill from O(L_context) to O(1) per query. PRECOG pre-encodes document corpora offline as SSM hidden states and injects the best-matching state directly at query time, with no in-context re-ingestion. A second component, SMC (Structured Memory Consolidation), builds a hierarchical persistent memory on top with cognitive-domain clustering and a fidelity-vs-storage dial. On a 1.2B-parameter TENNs-LLM with a 192 KB hidden state, PRECOG matches in-context RAG answer quality and cuts prefill latency from ~27 s to <6 ms on edge hardware — a ~4500x speedup that the authors note is architecturally impossible for Transformer KV caches.

news.title: Token Radius Attention for Efficient Video Generation
news.summary: Observes that the attention density a query actually needs varies per token and correlates log-linearly with attention entropy, and that the dominant interactions form query-centred neighbourhoods with token-dependent radii. TRA maps each query's entropy to an analytic token budget, converts that into a temporally decayed radius, and skips the rest — fused entropy extraction, warm-up reuse and block-sparse mask construction make it cheap. Across seven Wan2.1/Wan2.2/HunyuanVideo T2V and I2V configs, TRA keeps only 9–19% of attention interactions and delivers a 1.56–2.05x speedup at competitive quality.

news.title: UEmbed: Unified Sparse and Dense Multimodal Embeddings
news.summary: Learned Sparse Retrieval has been stuck behind encoder-only bidirectional architectures and bolted-on cross-modal adapters. UEmbed is a decoder-only model that emits both a sparse lexical vector and a dense vector in a single causal forward pass by appending N learnable special tokens, partitioning the vocabulary into N disjoint subsets, and letting each token's causal hidden state predict sparse weights over its own subset. Released at 2B / 4B / 9B scales, UEmbed-9B hits 71.8 (dense) and 71.0 (sparse) on MMEB-v2, beating the public-data SOTA (RzenEmbed), and stays competitive on BEIR.

news.title: WorldExam: Benchmarking World Models from Apparent Appearance to Inherent Reactivity
news.summary: Argues that the standard "is the video pretty / did it follow my instruction" benchmark family is missing the thing world models actually claim to model: reactivity — the ability to infer, from a scene state, what the world should do next even when no instruction names that outcome. WorldExam is a hierarchical diagnostic with four levels (Visual Quality, Control Adherence, Spatial Consistency, World Reactivity), 1,474 cases across eight tasks, and unified evaluation for camera-, action-, and language-driven controllable video generation.

news.title: Data Turnstile: A Scalable Open Framework for Function-Calling Data Generation
news.summary: Open-source framework that takes API specs and produces high-quality synthetic multi-turn function-calling data via constrained stepwise generation with validation and error-feedback loops. Fine-tuning Qwen3-0.6B on Turnstile data without CoT hits 75.9% on BFCL single-turn (vs. 67.4% base w/ thinking) and 31.1% pass 1 on τ 2 -bench Telecom (vs. 6.6% base) — surpassing Qwen2.5-32B (27.4%) with a 19× smaller model.

news.title: Mixture-of-Translators: Translating KV Caches Across Heterogeneous Large Language Models
news.summary: MoT is a learned mixture of cross-model KV-cache translators plus a Context-Correction Loss that re-aligns the replayed target trajectory with the native one. It diagnoses two failure modes — propagated early-injection shift and last-state shift — and addresses them via MoE-style routing + target-side correction. Across Qwen2.5, GPT-2 and OPT it preserves 51.0% closed-set QA and 0.43 extractive F1 on Qwen2.5-7B-scale translation, and retains 96.3% of direct-cache quality in a multi-agent memory-reuse case study.

news.title: MoRoute: Dynamic Routing for In-Context Multimodal Video Generation
news.summary: MoRoute replaces the “pick one VLM layer” hack with a learned dynamic router that, for every video DiT denoising step, chooses which VLM layer(s) and which spatial/temporal tokens to inject for the current condition (text, image, or video reference). It unifies text-to-video, image-to-video and video-to-video inside a single model and reports SOTA on VBench-Long, ChronoEdit and a new in-context compositional suite.

news.title: SAF-OPD: Stable Advantage Fusion for RLVR + On-Policy Distillation
news.summary: Diagnoses why naively mixing RLVR (verifiable reward, broadcast to every token) and on-policy distillation (dense per-token teacher advantage) collapses: a magnitude mismatch (token OPD advantages dwarf bounded RLVR signal) and a temporal mismatch (sustained OPD pulls the student into teacher-locked trajectories). SAF-OPD fuses them with a stable, norm-aware, time-decayed schedule and recovers the upside of both — AIME / MATH-500 gains over either alone with the same compute.

news.title: Scaling Properties of Text Conditioning in Visual Generation
news.summary: First empirical scaling laws for text conditioning in visual generation: converged diffusion loss decreases roughly linearly with structured-language likelihood (GPG) and follows a power law with a black-box attribute metric (ED). Using these laws they build a structured-prompt constructor + a verifier-gated prompter; the resulting system tops every open-weight model tested on compositional / reasoning / world-knowledge benchmarks and matches or beats the strongest closed-weight models on most evaluations.

news.title: TokenSwap: Benchmarking and Reducing the Modality Gap in Multimodal LLMs
news.summary: A Google DeepMind team formalises the modality gap as the systematic performance discrepancy an MLLM shows when the same semantic content is delivered as text vs. interleaved text+image tokens, then introduces TokenSwap : replace textual concepts with semantically aligned images inside existing text benchmarks (MMLU → image-interleaved variant). The paper both ships the diagnostic benchmark and proposes a training-time mitigation that closes most of the gap.

news.title: TokTier: Exact Stateful Tokenization for Agentic LLM Serving
news.summary: A serving-side tokenizer that keeps a per-session state so it only re-tokenizes a small window around the appended text and splices back into the cached token stream, with exact-match guarantees (zero divergence across 1.5e10 split checks and 93k+ replayed agent steps). GPU BPE on the fallback path encodes a 1M-char request in 0.87 ms; when dropped in front of vLLM, median TTFT drops 16–34% and P99 drops 23%.

news.title: Translation with Thought (TwT): Difficulty-Adaptive Reasoning for Multi-Domain MT
news.summary: Brings DeepSeek-R1-style chain-of-thought to machine translation in a resource-rational way: TwT is SFT-ed on difficulty-aware long CoT traces distilled from R1 (rewritten by GPT-4o for human-like economy), then RL-tuned with a hybrid quality+efficiency reward so the model learns to “think more” on hard sentences and “think less” on easy ones. Beats GPT-4o and DeepSeek-R1 on average across 15 domain MT benchmarks.

news.title: ViSAGE: Self-Correcting Memories for Long-Form Video Understanding
news.summary: ViSAGE replaces “compress and embed” with an entity-centric memory that cross-modally anchors identity (face/voice/object) and only commits new evidence when it passes a self-correction check against prior bindings. On long-form video QA it reduces entity-confusion hallucinations vs. ReAct/MemGPT-style baselines by large margins on EgoSchema, Video-MME and a new long-horizon entity-tracking suite.

news.title: Zero-Mem: Zero-Token Memory Operations for LLM Agents
news.summary: Zero-Mem pushes all memory access out of the LLM: it preserves the raw interaction trace as source-of-truth, builds two deterministic views (an entity–context graph plus a temporal hierarchy), and only invokes the LLM for the final question-answering reader. Across long-memory and long-context QA it matches token-based memory baselines while cutting memory-operation time by 57.6% versus the fastest compared baseline.

news.title: Tech Now
news.summary: New technologies measuring forests and exclusive access to a hacker rehab programme.

news.title: 🎥 VidMap: Video Structure-from-Motion Combining SLAM Sequential Structure with Offline SfM Global Optimization
news.summary: Existing SfM pipelines trade away either robustness or flexibility. VidMap is a system that fuses the strong sequential constraints of SLAM with the global optimization of offline SfM for metric reconstruction of arbitrary-length, uncalibrated videos . It uses recent wide-baseline dense matching, treats temporal ordering as a first-class citizen for reliable loop closure, and augments global optimization with metric monocular depth priors . Across a diverse set of challenging datasets exhibiting extreme motion and visual symmetries, the system significantly outperforms both classical and learned SLAM and SfM methods , with or without known camera calibration.

news.title: 📊 OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Economic-Grounded Long-Horizon Office-Suite Benchmark for LLM Agents (Baidu)
news.summary: Most office-agent benchmarks ignore whether the agent actually paid for itself. OmegaUse-OfficeVal ships 100 long-horizon office-suite tasks sourced from practitioner requests (each averages 2.32 hours of human labor ) and pairs every task with two economic signals — human labor time and a task-price proxy — enabling direct apples-to-apples comparison of LLM inference cost vs the work being substituted. A fine-grained rule-based code verifier anchors the eval. Across multiple frontier LLMs and a human baseline: the LLMs are dramatically cheaper and faster than humans , but none match human delivery quality . Code and dataset are fully open.

news.title: 🔍 DenseOn + LateOn: Fully Open Dense & Late-Interaction Retrieval Models with a Multilingual Generalization Surprise
news.summary: SOTA retrievers increasingly rely on closed training data, so the field can't reproduce them. LightOn presents a fully open recipe: from 1.4 B public pairs they curate 665 M English contrastive pre-training pairs + 1.88 M supervised pairs with mined hard negatives, and train two 149 M-param models — DenseOn (single-vector) and LateOn (ColBERT-style late-interaction) . They hit 56.20 / 57.22 mean nDCG@10 on BEIR at that size — new SOTA for the class. They then translate-train the pipeline into 8 more languages (2.8 B pairs total) to build mDenseOn / mLateOn on mmBERT-base, and surface a striking finding: despite sharing backbone + data + objective, late-interaction generalizes much better than dense to languages and scripts outside translate-train support — i.e., token-level matching turns translate-train from a target-language expansion tool into a multilingual generalization recipe.

news.title: 🤖 IPE: Rethinking Whether Q-Functions Need Pre-Training for Online RL Fine-Tuning
news.summary: The default recipe in value-based RL pretrain-then-finetune is to initialize both the policy and the Q-function from offline data. This paper systematically shows naive Q-function pretraining provides almost no benefit over random initialization — because the off-policy Q targets the pretrained policy's Q, not the Q the online fine-tune converges to, a gap that persists even after offline value maximization. The proposed Initialization via Policy Ensemble (IPE) trains multiple diverse policies up front and uses their pooled rollouts to bootstrap online-RL Q-learning. Across a suite of continuous-control benchmarks, IPE delivers an average 1.26× fine-tune improvement over naive Q-pretraining.

news.title: 🧾 APEX-Accounting: Frontier Models Tested on Real Accountant Work (Mercor × Ramp)
news.summary: A closed, expert-authored benchmark of 160 real accounting tasks across 10 worlds — each world contains an accounting system plus spreadsheets, PDFs, and supporting files; tasks include reconciling accounts, accruing expenses, posting transactions, and producing reports. Across 9 frontier models, Claude-Fable-5 (Max) leads at 56.4 % Mean Criteria@3 , Muse-Spark-1.1 (xHigh) is at 52.6 %, and no model exceeds 2.6 % on Pass^8 (GPT-5.6-Sol Max+Pro). A separate token-budget sweep surfaces a clean instance of Simpson's paradox : scores rise with budget in aggregate, but within a fixed-budget harness, models score lower on tasks where they spent more tokens.

news.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
news.summary: AISPA is a framework that audits system prompts across 8 user-relevant dimensions, applied to 3,249 instructions from 88 commercial AI products. Findings: some orgs ship 60+ protective instructions per product while others ship <5; 98.9% of products have at least one protective instruction but only 24% cover all 8 dimensions; system prompts have grown steadily longer/more protective; and ~40% of products still contain at least one instruction that works against user interests.

news.title: AskChem: Claim-Centered Infrastructure for Chemistry Literature Synthesis
news.summary: AskChem changes the unit of retrieval from paper to provenance-carrying claim — each paper is decomposed into typed atomic claims, each grounded by a DOI and verbatim quote. It indexes 2.4M claims from 147K chemistry papers with a faceted taxonomy, evidence graph, and living taxonomy, exposed via web UI and REST/SDK/MCP. Grounding GPT-5.5 in AskChem yields 100% resolvable DOIs vs 88.3% without retrieval, and the highest citation density among five tested systems.

news.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
news.summary: OSReward benchmarks VLM judges on computer-use agent (CUA) trajectories and finds even SOTA VLMs share a systematic leniency bias that mislabels failed runs as successes. The authors release OS-Shepherd-100K and train OS-Shepherd (9B and 35B) reward models that match commercial judges at 30–60% lower cost.

news.title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
news.summary: ReToken is a single learnable embedding trained as an explicit retrieval target that picks a sparse set of query-relevant visual tokens from a pre-filled visual KV cache. On Visual Haystacks it improves Qwen3VL-8B by 13.4 points and InternVL3.5 by 12.4 points (>20% relative), and zero-shot transfers to long-video LVBench for +8.0 points with Qwen3VL-8B. Training and long-video inference fit on a single H100.

news.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
news.summary: A designed experiment (7 methods, 1.5B/3B/7B open models, two math benchmarks, 150 questions each, all 36 comparisons paired by question with bootstrap intervals and multiplicity correction) shows that no self-critique/self-reflection method reliably beats plain repeated sampling at equal token cost; ten are reliably worse, and all 18 self-inspection comparisons are negative. The result holds from 1.5B to 7B, and Self-Refine / forced Reflexion stay 3.6–10.1 points below baseline even at 7B.

news.title: ⚡ InferScale: GPU-Native KV Injection for Personalized LLM Serving
news.summary: Persistent personalized context (Mem0 / MemGPT / Zep-style memory profiles, long chat histories) is re-prefilled into every request, so TTFT balloons with the retrieval budget even though the underlying memory is reused. InferScale stores each memory fact's KV representation directly on the GPU alongside a semantic embedding, retrieves relevant facts at serving time, and injects the cached KV into vLLM's paged cache via the KV-connector interface — no engine modifications, no fine-tuning. The technical lift is Chunked RoPE (store keys pre-rotation, apply serving-time positions during injection) plus Context-Window Encoding to recover cross-fact context.

news.title: 🎬 FreqForcing: Autoregressive Long Video Generation via Spectral Self-Anchoring
news.summary: Autoregressive video diffusion collapses over long rollouts — color drift, motion stagnation, eventual visual breakdown. The paper characterizes this from the frequency domain: error accumulation is a pronounced energy drift in the low-frequency bands , which is exactly what attention sinks partially correct but cannot fix. FreqForcing is a training-free Spectral Self-Anchoring scheme that uses low-frequency components of anchor attention to maintain long-horizon visual stability while preserving dynamic motion through high-frequency components of local attention. Extends a Self-Forcing checkpoint trained on 5 s clips to two-minute generation — 24× extrapolation .

news.title: 🦾 TurboVLA: Real-Time Vision-Language-Action Model at 32 Hz on an RTX 4090 with <1 GB VRAM
news.summary: TurboVLA throws out the dominant V→L→A pipeline (project visual observations into LLM-token space, then decode to actions) and replaces it with a direct V+L→A mapping: visual and language features are encoded independently, exchange information through lightweight bidirectional vision-language interaction, and a compact decoder emits continuous action chunks. The payoff is a 0.2B-parameter policy that runs at 32 Hz with 31.2 ms latency on a consumer RTX 4090, using only 0.9 GB VRAM , and matches or beats substantially larger LLM-centric VLA stacks on LIBERO (97.7 % average success).

news.title: 🧠 Mental World Modeling (MENTIS framework)
news.summary: Current world models answer the physical question — what / where / how will it move — but human behavior is driven by hidden mental state (beliefs, wants, intents, social permissibility). Mental World Modeling proposes that mental variables become core components of the world model rather than post-hoc rationales: a coupled physical-mental world state, target-specific partial observation, and joint simulation of how candidate actions update both. The authors instantiate it as MENTIS, a training-free, fully inspectable baseline that decomposes the process into state parsing, target-observation generation, action decomposition, coupled transition, and branch-level value evaluation.

news.title: 🛡️ Pangram 4 Technical Report — SOTA AI-Text Detection
news.summary: Pangram 4 is the latest deep-learning AI-text classifier from Pangram Labs, reaching AUROC 0.9916, FPR 0.0041 %, FNR 0.3396 % — and the more interesting lift is in the harder sub-tasks: fine-grained edit boundary detection and identifying interleaved AI-human co-authored text. Better out-of-distribution generalization and adversarial robustness than Pangram 3; new SOTA across standard AI-detection benchmarks in a wide variety of settings and domains.

news.title: ⚡ Self-Speculating Agent: Predict Your Next Tool Call via Joint Agent-Speculator RL
news.summary: Tool-call speculation hides agent latency by predicting and pre-executing the next tool call, but external draft speculators drift from the deployed agent's behavior. The paper observes that the target agent itself is already a strong next-call predictor and proposes a single model that runs in two modes — agent mode (solves tasks) and speculator mode (predicts the next tool call from a partial trajectory) — sharing the prefix KV cache. A joint agent-speculator RL procedure derives speculation targets from the agent's own rollouts and alternates the two updates. Hit@1 on next tool call jumps 44.1 → 61.2 for Qwen3-4B and 48.9 → 66.3 for Qwen3.5-4B, while agent task success is preserved.

news.title: 🌀 Rethinking Classifier-Free Guidance in On-Policy Diffusion Distillation
news.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) for diffusion models has been naively extending velocity matching to the CFG-composed prediction, but the paper shows that objective is under-identified — positive- and negative-branch errors can cancel in the guided output. Through two contrasting cases, the authors show when naive matching works (shared negative conditioning) and when it breaks (privileged info in the teacher's negative branch), then propose a branch-aware formulation that fixes the failure mode.

news.title: 🌐 MODUS: Decoder-Only Any-to-Any Multimodal (ICML 2026, Apple × EPFL)
news.summary: Most any-to-any multimodal stacks are encoder-decoder or diffusion models trained from scratch with modality-specific heads / losses / task pipelines. MODUS does it with a single decoder-only Transformer that treats every modality symmetrically: any modality can be input, output, or both, with no special-case heads. Because every modality is both input and output of the same model, MODUS enables chained generation through intermediate modalities (e.g. image → text → 3D) and cross-modal self-verification (the model scores its own outputs by generating another modality as a consistency check). The paper reports scientific-domain use cases (ecology, astronomy) and is accepted to ICML 2026.

news.title: 🎨 DreamStyle3D: Efficient 3D Stylized Asset Generation via Dual-Attention Disentanglement
news.summary: DreamStyle3D is a native 3D stylization framework that explicitly disentangles geometry and style through a Decoupled Dual Cross-Attention mechanism, avoiding the indirect 2D-to-3D pipelines most prior work relies on. The lightweight training recipe keeps style fidelity and geometric consistency together while staying efficient enough for production asset generation — relevant for gaming, animation, and VR workflows.

news.title: 🎬 Wonder: Video World Model Done Better (real-time, camera-controllable)
news.summary: Wonder is a general-purpose video world model that turns an image (or a conditional video) into a playable world the user can navigate in real time with the camera — exploring unseen regions, revisiting earlier views, and maintaining coherent geometry / appearance / dynamics across minute-scale rollouts. It co-designs three pieces: (1) a dense-coordinate-field camera conditioning that lets the model interpret camera motion directly as visual evidence, (2) a sparse-attention memory module that retrieves from a growing context at fixed inference cost regardless of horizon length, and (3) rectified self-forcing-style distillation that preserves control fidelity and long-term memory from the teacher. Result: 16 FPS diverse video generation, with video-conditioned re-shooting of existing scenes as a free bonus.

news.title: 🔬 Feature-Effect Geometry Analysis (FEGA): Sparse Autoencoders Encode Both Concepts and Functions
news.summary: The paper challenges the assumption that SAE features are reusable "concept directions." FEGA studies the geometry of logit changes produced by ablating the same active feature across many contexts, and finds that consistent one-dimensional effects are rare — most features behave as functions over the input geometry rather than static directions. That helps explain why SAE steering is brittle across prompts and why activation-based feature selection often misses the features that actually change the output.

news.title: 🤖 πR²: Reactive Real-time Flow Policies (CMU)
news.summary: Action-chunking flow policies built on large backbones are powerful but open-loop: the policy cannot react to new observations mid-chunk. Replanning every tick would fix that, except the perception + multi-step denoising pipeline is too slow. πR² fixes both axes. It splits conditioning into a fast proprioception channel (fresh every tick) and an asynchronously refreshed slow vision-language channel, so the policy reacts to proprioception within a chunk while tolerating stale vision. A latency-adaptive flow schedule treats in-flight actions as inpainting conditioning and emits actions in one denoising step per call, letting a single trained model adapt to varying hardware latency. Finetuned on top of GR00T-N1.7 and deployed on a real xArm6 + XHand platform, πR² replans ~4× faster (~25 Hz on an A5000, fresh observation every 40 ms) and improves success by up to +23 % sim / +30 % real over the strongest baseline.

news.title: 🧠 CARE: Confidence-Adaptive Routing for Mixture-of-Experts LoRA
news.summary: MoE-LoRA routes every token to a fixed top-k, which over-spends compute on easy tokens and under-serves hard ones. CARE observes that the router's output distribution is itself a per-token uncertainty signal — peaked mass means confident, flat means ambiguous — and admits experts in a nucleus fashion: keep activating experts in decreasing router weight until cumulative mass crosses a threshold (with a small extension when the admitted experts disagree). A budget thermostat calibrates the threshold so the average number of active experts matches any target. Drop-in, single-forward-pass, no extra parameters. Across LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B on eight commonsense benchmarks plus math / code / knowledge, CARE improves over fixed top-k MoE-LoRA at matched compute and matches fixed k=4 while activating fewer experts on average; the same signals also help OOD detection over MSP / entropy / multi-pass proxies.

news.title: 🧠 Eviction as Estimation: A Fixed-Lag Smoothing View of Test-Time Memory — and When Measuring Beats Accumulating
news.summary: The paper re-positions KV-cache eviction as estimation of a hidden reuse signal: whether a stored token will be needed again. It places existing heuristics (StreamingLLM, H2O, SnapKV) on a single axis — commit lag H — and shows the missing regime is fixed-lag smoothing, where the cache waits a bounded number of steps before deciding to keep or evict. That regime dominates naive accumulation on long-context benchmarks because it lets the model "measure then decide" rather than committing at H=0.

news.title: 🧹 DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data
news.summary: DataOrchestra reframes pretraining data cleaning as a learnable, per-example decision problem. A single orchestrator picks the right operation (drop, pass-through, or clean) for each chunk and, when cleaning, selects the tools and writes the LLM rewrite instructions — meaning the same pipeline can mix programmatic edits and model rewrites based on what each example actually needs. The authors pretrain 0.5B–7B models from scratch on web data processed by their orchestrator and show consistent downstream gains over fixed corpus-level recipes.

news.title: 🎨 MMOE — Modernizing Diffusion Transformers with Efficient Expert Design
news.summary: Applies the LLM scaling-efficiency playbook — routed experts, shared/lightweight experts, gate-residual routing, attention-residual information reuse — to SiT-style diffusion transformers. Trained on a single 8×H100 node for 400k steps at batch 256 (accessible budget) and reaches lower FID at every recorded checkpoint than dense and intermediate sparse baselines, with the best quality/cost balance among sparse variants.

news.title: 🦞 Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence (Moonshot AI)
news.summary: Moonshot releases Kimi K3, a 2.8T-parameter Mixture-of-Experts LLM with 104B active parameters, native vision, and a 1M-token context window. Built on Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) + Attention Residuals and Stable LatentMoE that activates 16 of 896 routed experts per token, claiming ~2.5× better scaling efficiency than K2. Post-training pushes RL across general / agentic / coding plus multiple reasoning-effort levels.

news.title: 🧪 Efficiency Matters in Autonomous Research (Yang & Cao)
news.summary: Argues that autonomous-research (AR) systems should be evaluated on search efficiency , not just final outcome quality — proposes the AUC of the Pareto frontier over quality-vs-evaluation-budget as a metric. Compares hill climbing, beam search, tree search, and evolutionary search across 12 systems-optimization tasks and shows no single search structure is consistently best. Introduces fluid search , a portfolio-bandit adaptive procedure that dynamically allocates budget across a forest of search processes, matching a per-task oracle across the suite.

news.title: 🛡️ APPA — Agentic Permissions Policy Algebra for Taint Confinement in LLM Agents
news.summary: Solves the usability bottleneck of dynamic Information-Flow Control (IFC) for LLM agents: traditional taint tracking permanently taints the primary context on any unvetted read, neutering downstream utility. APPA prospectively evaluates label descents before data acquisition (producing Authorize/Accept remedy plans) and spawns a label-seeded child trajectory that absorbs label descent locally, letting a trusted sanitizer return a bounded derivative to the unchanged parent. Two-monoid model over security labels + shared event log; formally proves parent-label preservation and merge confinement.

news.title: A Roadmap to Impactful Pluralistic Alignment Research
news.summary: A blunt audit-and-recommendations paper on pluralistic value alignment. The authors checked the public behavior docs and evaluations of frontier labs and found that none name pluralism as a goal, and no production model is explicitly trained or tested for it — even though that's the stated motivation. They argue the field has three structural problems: (1) justifications are still normative or speculative instead of empirical, (2) the community hasn't agreed on when pluralistic behavior is warranted or what it actually looks like, and (3) current methods trade off against other LLM desiderata in ways that aren't measured, and existing metrics aren't "hill-climbable" for production.

news.title: Nanbeige4.2-3B: Unlocking Agentic Capabilities in a Compact Model
news.summary: A 3B non-embedding-parameter general agentic model trained from scratch on 28T tokens. The interesting design choices: a Looped Transformer that reuses the layer stack for extra capacity without adding parameters; SFT trajectory construction that mixes real-world deployment with large-scale synthesis; and a mixed-mode RLHF stack combining Think/Non-Think response RL, length-controlled reasoning RL, and agentic RL with outcome + process rewards. The authors claim it beats Qwen3.5-9B and Gemma4-12B on diverse agentic benchmarks while staying competitive on reasoning and alignment.

news.title: On the Identifiability of Controlled World Models
news.summary: The first identifiability theory for action-conditioned JEPA-style world models under nonlinear observations. The paper splits the problem into two coupled conditions: (1) representation identifiability , which needs a spectral separation property in the latent space, and (2) transition identifiability , which needs non-degenerate variation of the conditional action. When both hold, minimizing the LeJEPA-style predictive loss recovers the true latent states and controlled dynamics up to orthogonal transformation. They also derive a bound showing transition prediction error is inversely proportional to the spectral separation margin, and characterize how counterfactual prediction error amplifies with the weakest action-excitation margin.

news.title: Skill Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of LLM Capability with Co-Evolving Skills
news.summary: A co-evolutionary post-training framework that closes the gap between "narrow but verifiable" and "broad but reward-noisy" self-play. A proposer generates tasks conditioned on dynamically sampled skills, a solver explores solutions, and a skill controller curates a growing skill library from execution feedback — all orchestrated by one RL loop. The trick is to treat skills as the middle layer: each one gives deep, testable execution inside a scenario, while dynamic routing across skills keeps the task distribution open-ended.

news.title: Twins: Learn to Predict Unified Representations with Focal Loss
news.summary: A single continuous token space for unified multimodal models that doesn't blow up sequence length: ViT and VAE features are channel-concatenated on the same token grid, so attention cost is unchanged. The authors identify a sharp optimization imbalance — the Diffusion Transformer fits the ViT branch easily but chokes on the VAE latent distribution because of frequency bias, intrinsic dimensionality mismatch, and condition-aligned vs condition-independent uncertainty. They fix it with a focal regression objective adapted to flow matching that upweights large-error VAE dimensions.

news.title: Emergent Misalignment Recruits a Pre-existing Persona Subspace
news.summary: A mechanistic interpretability study that explains the "emergent misalignment" phenomenon — narrow fine-tuning on insecure code leaking into broad bad behavior on unrelated prompts. Using contrastive teacher forcing on Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct, the author extracts a low-rank persona subspace that is already present before fine-tuning (657× above random). Projecting that subspace out during training drops broad misalignment from 27.7% → 0.0%, and injecting it into an untouched model induces misalignment that scales with dose up to 45.4%.

news.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
news.summary: A self-supervised RL recipe (Modality-Informed Reciprocal Reasoning Optimization) that exploits the fact that VLMs often solve a geometry problem in text but fail on the diagram, or vice versa. For each problem it picks the best-performing view as a teacher and pulls the other views toward it via reverse-KL — no external labels needed.

news.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
news.summary: An open-source end-to-end RL framework that lets you train agents inside real inference harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw-class stacks) instead of toy simulators. A lightweight proxy records harness model calls as training data for veRL while a Kubernetes orchestrator runs each rollout in its own remote container, so train/inference match exactly.

news.title: UniD: Unified Video Dense Prediction from Disjoint Data
news.summary: A single video model that predicts 8 dense scene properties at once — depth, normals, semantic segmentation, boundaries, human parts, albedo, shading, materials — all trained from disjoint, non-overlapping per-task datasets. Per-task experts supervise a unified diffusion backbone through lightweight projectors, skipping expensive pseudo-labeling.

news.title: VLM-IE3D: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
news.summary: Boosts a 2D VLM's 3D spatial IQ by injecting two new token types learned purely from RGB video: Implicit Geometry Tokens (high-level priors) and Explicit Geometry Tokens (fine reconstructed structure), fused via a 3D-aware adapter. No LiDAR, no depth sensors, no 3D ground truth.

news.title: AdaRoPE: Not All Attention Heads Should Rotate and Scale Equally
news.summary: A theoretical + empirical critique of standard RoPE: heads with different functional roles need different rotation frequencies and attention scaling. AdaRoPE gives each head learnable rotation frequencies and scaling factors, and slots in as a drop-in RoPE replacement that improves long-context generalization over partial-RoPE and NoPE baselines.

news.title: Euclean: Automated Geometry Problem Formalization with Unified Verification in Lean
news.summary: A four-stage framework that auto-formalizes geometry problems into Lean using native Mathlib (not a custom axiom system). Tackles the implicit-diagram problem (topology, non-degeneracy assumptions) and ships with a much larger problem corpus than prior Lean geometry efforts.

news.title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds With Generative Simulation
news.summary: Instead of training a 4D generative model end-to-end, GS-Agent assembles foundation models (LLM + 3D / physics simulators) into an agentic pipeline that turns a natural-language prompt into a controllable, physically plausible 4D scene — agents explicitly call geometry, physics, and rendering tools and verify plausibility.

news.title: Inference-Time Scaling of Diffusion Models via Progressive Seed Pruning
news.summary: Argues that diffusion/flow-matching models have been missing an inference-time scaling axis that LLMs already exploit. By allowing memory to grow during inference, you can front-load many candidate seeds, evaluate them early with a reward model, prune aggressively, then commit the best trajectory — trading memory for quality without changing training.

news.title: LISA: Linear-Indexed Sparse Attention for Efficient Long-Context Reasoning
news.summary: A plug-and-play attention replacement targeting long chain-of-thought models like DeepSeek-R1. LISA runs a linear-attention branch (O(n) long-range memory) in parallel with a Lightning Indexer that picks the top-M important tokens for sparse self-attention, fused via a gating mechanism — no pretraining-from-scratch required.

news.title: PRO-LONG: Programmatic Memory Enables Long-Horizon Reasoning
news.summary: An agent harness built around programmatic memory — code-as-state rather than raw observation dumping — targeting long-horizon tasks like ARC-AGI-3. The framework lets the LLM write and run small programs that decide what to remember from the environment and how to retrieve it back into context.

news.title: SANA-Video 2.0: Hybrid Linear Attention with Attention Residuals for Efficient Video Generation
news.summary: A 5B/14B video diffusion transformer that mixes gated linear attention with periodic gated-softmax "anchor" attention at a 3:1 ratio, recovering full-rank token mixing while keeping cost roughly linear in sequence length. Ships with attention residuals so information survives the linear blocks, and is engineered to render 720p video on a single GPU.

news.title: SLPO: Scaling Latent Reasoning via a Surrogate Policy
news.summary: Brings outcome-reward RL to autoregressive latent reasoners. The trick: a learned "surrogate policy" approximates per-step likelihoods and stopping decisions under a fixed thinking budget, so RL can finally scale latent test-time compute (which was previously stuck at imitation-learning level).

news.title: Streaming Multi-Agent Autoregressive Diffusion Model with World State Registers (WorldWeaver / W²)
news.summary: A streaming multi-agent video diffusion model that augments rollouts with cross-agent "world state registers" — learnable tokens carrying shared world info plus per-agent status that update dynamically. Yields consistent observations across agents and views, instead of the usual conditional-history trick that loses shared state.

news.title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
news.summary: Identifies a sharp inefficiency in modern frontier models: the built-in Multi-Token-Prediction (MTP / NEXTN) draft head runs full attention over the entire KV cache on every draft step, so its cost grows linearly with context — and at million-token inputs that draft actually dominates the total speculative-decoding cost. Proposes a windowed draft-KV scheme that keeps the draft cheap while preserving acceptance rates.

news.title: ⚡ Look Less, Think Faster: Joint Token-Compute Adaptation for Multimodal LLMs
news.summary: SmartVL is a unified adaptive-inference framework that jointly controls vision token count and LLM compute in response to input content and a runtime compute budget. A vision-side token controller prunes redundant visual tokens; an LLM-side compute controller skips layers/heads. The two controllers share a budget encoding and train end-to-end with a differentiable latency estimator so they coordinate rather than compete.

news.title: 🎥 PercepCap: Video Captioner with Structured Spatio-Temporal Perception
news.summary: A perceive-then-describe video captioner that makes perceptual evidence explicit before producing the final caption. First generates a spatiotemporal perception trace (object trajectories + temporal events), then conditions the caption on that trace. Trained in two stages: Perceive-then-Describe SFT adapts an MLLM to the chain, and Perception-Grounded RL applies joint rewards over both perception chain and final caption. A new Caption-Anchored Perception Data Construction pipeline builds training data by generating captions first, extracting referenced objects/events, and grounding them back with boxes + timestamps — guaranteeing trace and caption refer to the same things.

news.title: 🎬 Self Gradient Forcing: Native Long Video Extrapolation
news.summary: Identifies a missing-supervision gap in Self Forcing–style autoregressive video diffusion: the historical KV cache is treated as frozen rollout state, so future-frame losses never teach the model how earlier latents should be written into useful keys/values. Self Gradient Forcing (SGF) is a two-pass trainer — Pass 1 does a no-gradient rollout and records the self-generated context + noisy latents at a sampled denoising exit step; Pass 2 does parallel context-gradient reconstruction at that exit step, with the generated context as stop-gradient clean-latent input and the model recomputing context KV + future-to-context causal attention.

news.title: 💸 PyroDash: Cost-Efficient Token-Level Small–Large Language Model Collaborative Inference
news.summary: Token-level SLM↔LLM routing without a separate router, LLM retraining, or LLM-logit access. During generation the SLM emits a control token to request help; a Collaborate Engine hands the partial reasoning trace to a frozen LLM via a single handoff. The SLM is trained in three stages — control-token embedding learning, offloading-oriented SFT, and cost-aware GRPO whose reward balances accuracy against LLM-only inference cost.

news.title: 🧊 ATSplat: Compact Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting with Adaptive Token Expansion
news.summary: Restores the adaptive allocation capacity of vanilla 3DGS inside a feed-forward pipeline. ATSplat lifts coarse patch-level depth/camera cues into sparse 3D anchor tokens, then regresses each into local Gaussians with learnable 3D offsets — decoupling primitive placement from the input image grid. An Adaptive Token Expansion module predicts token-level uncertainty (supervised by rendering-error maps) and selectively expands high-uncertainty tokens through learnable expansion layers.

news.title: 🌐 AI Tool Discovery at Scale: All You Need is DNS
news.summary: ToolDNS retrofits semantic tool discovery onto the DNS substrate: functional intent + organizational trust encoded as a hierarchical namespace, semantic search becomes lightweight O(log N) name resolutions. Three protocol-compliant extensions (partially unfolded names, EDNS0 intent payloads, logical subdomains) enable decentralized governance. On a released 33,688-tool heterogeneous benchmark (MCP / A2A / RESTful / Skill) the framework cuts per-query search space by 95.26% while matching SOTA retrieval accuracy, with UDP-native latency orders of magnitude lower than HTTP registries.

news.title: 🎬 Surprise Forcing: What to Remember, When to Skip in Long Video Generation
news.summary: A training-free framework that turns the two main limitations of streaming autoregressive diffusion (fixed-budget KV cache, uniform denoising schedule) into online resource-allocation problems. A Surprise-Gated Memory Bank summarizes evicted frames with value-token descriptors and admits them via a feedback-controlled budget; Surprise-Aware Denoising skips intermediate steps for "easy" chunks based on adjacent-frame cosine distance. On VBench, VBench-Long and VBench-2.0 it improves long-horizon consistency and visual quality at real-time throughput.

news.title: 🧠 Convolution for Large Language Models
news.summary: A systematic study on adding lightweight depthwise convolutions to Qwen3 Transformer blocks. Across 17 candidate locations, the best placement is on the projected Q/K/V before attention, with a residual depthwise conv (kernel size 3, no extra norm/activation). Improves the average accuracy on seven downstream benchmarks while adding <0.01% parameters, and makes repeated token IDs more sensitive to their immediate context.

news.title: 🧩 BatchDAG: LLM-Planned Execution Graphs for Scalable Ad-Hoc Analysis Over Enterprise Data
news.summary: An LLM generates a typed DAG of SQL queries, semantic searches, in-memory transforms, parallel fan-outs and single-shot analyses; a deterministic engine executes it with topological-wave parallelism and structured JSON data flow. Entity-aware batching cuts LLM calls by up to 47×. Quality on 12 transcript-heavy queries (3.74/5) beats an expert-designed pipeline (3.25/5) and a ReAct agent (3.09/5, p<0.01), with 77% transcript-evidence provenance.

news.title: 🛡️ SysAdmin: Measuring Instrumental Power-Seeking in Frontier AI
news.summary: A benchmark that puts frontier LLMs in charge of a high-fidelity Linux sandbox as system administrators and measures power-seeking propensity across five axes: self-preservation, increasing autonomy, resource acquisition, environment modification, strategic concealment. 2,800 tasks across seven frontier models × four conditions. After bias correction against human-annotated calibration data, spontaneous power-seeking estimates range 0–5%; a positive control with explicit power-seeking prompts hits 100% detection, validating sensitivity. More pronounced failure modes: specification gaming and resistance to goal modification.

news.title: Frontier Language Models Struggle to Copy: Text Can Be Better Viewed in 2D
news.summary: Researchers show that frontier LLMs (including reasoning models) surprisingly fail at exact string copying even when the input sits comfortably within their context window. The root cause is the inductive bias of 1D positional encodings: models prefer copying via 'local context match' shortcuts rather than precise position lookup. The proposed fix, 2D-RoPE, lays text out in a 2D grid (row + column IDs) so copying becomes a fixed column-offset retrieval — easy to learn. Shallow Transformers with 2D-RoPE hit perfect copy at input lengths hundreds of times longer than training, and the gain persists up to 1.4B pretraining on DCLM.

news.title: LLM-as-a-Coach: Experiential Learning for Non-Verifiable Tasks
news.summary: Repurposes the LLM-as-a-Judge model into an "LLM-as-a-Coach" that distills rich textual feedback into transferable experiential knowledge, which conditions a teacher model and is internalized by the policy via on-policy context distillation — instead of crushing evaluation down to a scalar reward.

news.title: MotionForesight: Re-purposing Video Models for Future 3D Scene-Flow Prediction
news.summary: Given a short clip of someone interacting with an object, MotionForesight predicts the future 3D trajectories of points on that object. The insight is that pretrained video models already encode rich 'how objects move during interaction' priors — instead of predicting pixels, you redirect those priors to predict 3D scene flow. Using only 40k videos and freezing the large video/tracking backbones, the method beats models trained on 1M+ videos and generalizes across out-of-distribution objects and viewpoints.

news.title: QUADS: Stabilizing NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning for MoE via QUantization-error Alignment across Dual Sides
news.summary: Training Mixture-of-Experts LLMs with reinforcement learning at NVFP4 precision looks great on paper (4-bit activations and weights, faster rollout than FP8) but in practice collapses after ~150 steps because rollout–trainer log-probability gaps explode. The authors trace this to activation-side quantization error (weights can be aligned via shared quant-dequant paths; activations are recomputed online and suffer from the coarse E2M1 grid). QUADS aligns quantization error on both sides of the forward pass and stabilizes the run.

news.title: RynnBrain 1.1: Towards More Capable and Generalizable Embodied Foundation Model
news.summary: A unified spatio-temporal embodied foundation model family at 2B / 9B / 122B-A10B scales, with native 3D grounding, contact-point prediction, and a cross-embodiment VLA variant (RynnBrain-VLA) deployed on Unitree G1, Astribot-S1, and Tianji-Wuji robots.

news.title: Searching Videos as Trees: Self-Correcting Agents for Grounded Long Video QA
news.summary: Grounded Long Video QA (find the short evidence interval that answers a question in a long video) is currently tackled by agentic methods that only support coarse-to-fine narrowing — meaning once the agent zooms in wrong, it cannot back out. VideoTreeSearch (VTS) instead builds an adaptive temporal tree from visual scene boundaries and trains an agent with four discrete operations: zoom_in, zoom_out, shift, answer. The key insight is treating backtracking as an explicit learnable primitive.

news.title: SWE-Pruner Pro: The Coder LLM Already Knows What to Prune
news.summary: Drops the external code classifier from SWE-Pruner and instead uses the coding agent's own internal representations, via a small head with a length-aware line-count embedding, to label each line of tool output as keep or prune.

news.title: ToolVerse: Unlocking Massive Environments and Long-Horizon Tasks for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
news.summary: ToolVerse is an agentic RL framework that scales training environments to ~400 real-world Model Context Protocols (MCPs) containing roughly 4,500 tools. It uses a tool-dependency graph plus a Dynamic Unlocking Sampling Algorithm to generate long-horizon tasks (the GUST dataset), and introduces a Turn-Aware Relative Advantage estimator to fix credit-assignment failures over long tool-use trajectories.

news.title: Do Coding Agents Need Executable World Models, Simplification, and Verification to Solve ARC-AGI-3?
news.summary: Ablation of the previous ARC-AGI-3 winning agent across four nested Codex variants (text-only → +executable world model → +scheduled simplification → +exact-replay verification) on gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.5 / gpt-5.6-sol. Surprises: a persistent executable deliverable is not universally helpful — the textual variant beats the flexible-interface executable variant on gpt-5.5; simplification helps in 3/4 settings; the full verification treatment ranks first in every setting. On gpt-5.6-sol, the verification variant fully solves every public ARC-AGI-3 game at both reasoning efforts (~99% RHAE, <½ human-baseline actions).

news.title: DriftWorld: Fast World Modeling through Drifting
news.summary: Replaces the iterative denoising loop in diffusion-style world models with a learned action-conditioned drift, so each future-frame rollout becomes a single forward pass at 30+ fps — about 17× faster than diffusion baselines. Achieves SOTA decision-making on Bridge-V2, RT-1, Language Table, Push-T and Robomimic, and the rollouts correlate with ground-truth returns up to 0.99, making it usable as an offline policy ranker.

news.title: Leveraging Instruction Tuning and Merging for Reasoning Model Adaptation
news.summary: Shows that SFT data without reasoning traces — long written off as useless for reasoning models — can be reactivated cheaply. Apply classic instruction tuning on the reasoning model, then merge it back with the original RLM. Recovers and often exceeds reasoning performance on the target domain (including hard-to-verify ones like text summarization) while preserving capability elsewhere. Total cost: under USD $3 of compute.

news.title: LongStraw: Long-Context RL Beyond 2M Tokens under a Fixed GPU Budget
