news.summary: An architecture-aware execution stack that finally closes the gap between million-token inference and short-context RL post-training. LongStraw drops autograd on the shared prompt, keeps only the model-specific state needed by later tokens, and replays short response branches one at a time — yielding 2.1M-token GRPO post-training on just eight H20 GPUs and stress tests reaching 4.46M positions, all under a fixed budget. Validated end-to-end on Qwen3.6-27B and the compressed-attention MoE GLM-5.2 (32 H20s).

news.title: Process Reward Informed Tree Rollout for Effective Multi-Turn RL
news.summary: Reframes multi-turn agent RL rollouts as tree-structured exploration: at each turn, a process scorer ranks partial trajectories, branches are spawned only from promising prefixes, shared prefixes are reused, and degenerate paths are stopped early. Output groups stay drop-in for GRPO/RLOO, but exploration is concentrated where the process reward says it matters. +5.0 points on SWE-Bench and +9.3 points on FrozenLake vs uniform-rollout baselines, on the same training budget.

news.title: Scaling Behavior Foundation Model for Humanoid Robots
news.summary: A principled scaling recipe for Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) for humanoid control. Coordinates three levers — motion tracking in the global frame, on-policy rollout quantity × reference-motion diversity, and a new Humanoid Transformer architecture — and shows they compound. Cuts Mean Per-Keypoint Position Error by 10%+ in local mode and 82% in global mode vs prior humanoid controllers, validated in both simulation and on real hardware.

news.title: VarRate: Training-Free Variable-Rate KV Cache Compression for Long-Context LLMs
news.summary: Argues that both token-selection KV eviction (SnapKV/Ada-KV) and uniform low-rank KV coding share one failure mode — they force a single budget per token instead of allocating rank. VarRate assigns each token a variable low-rank budget by its query salience, keeps every token at non-zero rank, requires no training, and degrades only 3.5–5.5 points where query-aware selection collapses by 11–15. On LongBench (16 tasks) at 20% budget it stays within 0.8 points of the uncompressed model on both Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B and beats a purpose-built query-agnostic codec (KVzip) at ~1/8 the prefill overhead.

news.title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models
news.summary: Introduces the "Jacobian lens" to identify the small set of representations an LLM is poised to verbalize at any step — the J-space — and shows it has the structural and functional signatures of Global Workspace Theory: coherent content only in mid-layers, tens of concepts at once, broadcast widely across weights, usable as working memory for silent reasoning. J-space exposes strategic deliberation, evaluation awareness, and trained-in misalignment that never reach the output stream. Counterfactual reflection training is introduced as a behaviour-shaping technique that only edits what the model would say if interrupted.

news.title: Video = World + Event Stream (Wan-Streamer v0.3)
news.summary: Alibaba's Wan team reframes streaming video as a persistent "world" (environment + scene + voice characteristics) plus a real-time "event stream" (actions, speech, motion). Trained on a single generative task — predict how the world evolves given current state + input — and instantiated as a real-time full-duplex audio-visual interaction model: 640×368 @ 25 FPS, 160 ms streaming unit, ~200 ms model-side latency, ~550 ms end-to-end latency under a 350 ms network budget.

news.title: Xiaomi-Robotics-1: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models with over 100K Hours of Real-World Trajectories
news.summary: Xiaomi's first foundational VLA: pre-trained on 100K+ hours of UMI-collected real-world mobile manipulation trajectories with an auto-labeled natural-language caption pipeline, then post-trained for embodiment alignment. Establishes new SOTA on RoboCasa365 at 57.6% (vs prior 46.6%) and RoboDojo at 20.07 (vs prior 13.07), with clean data/loss scaling curves and high post-training data efficiency.

news.title: Mask-Aware Policy Gradients for Diffusion Language Models
news.summary: Formalizes Masked Diffusion LM generation as a two-stage action MDP — at each step, both which tokens to place at masked positions AND which positions to remask. Provides a tractable policy-gradient estimator for RL fine-tuning of MDLMs that respects the unmasking-order decision, unlike prior token-only approximations.

news.title: Pretraining Data Can Be Poisoned through Computational Propaganda
news.summary: Demonstrates poisoning attacks beyond the Wikipedia-style toy settings used in prior work, exploiting public discussion interfaces (Reddit-style web content) as a web-scale injection vector. Introduces HalfLife, a new analysis that estimates adversarial content inclusion after realistic crawl + curation pipelines.

news.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
news.summary: Scales visuomotor context to 8K timesteps (three orders of magnitude beyond SOTA) by integrating Test-Time Training into Vision-Language-Action policies, treating recurrent state as fast weights updated by gradient at inference. Achieves 87% gain over single-step baselines and completes a 5-minute, 10-stage real-robot assembly task no baseline can finish.

news.title: SciDiagramEdit: Learning to Edit Scientific Diagrams from Paper Revisions
news.summary: Mines before/after figure pairs from arXiv version histories to learn instruction-driven editing on editable vector sources, using an agentic skill-evolution framework that refines the agent's skill spec from execution traces. Operates at the primitive level so users can inspect and co-edit individual elements.

news.title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
news.summary: Reformulates open-domain info-seeking as relational schema completion with grounded citations, externalizing state into Frontier Task / Evidence Graph / Coverage Map / Failure Memory. Pipeline-parallel scheduling refills sub-agent slots targeting unresolved coverage gaps; a Search Tool Middleware Harness intercepts model-tool interactions to avoid stalled loops.

news.title: Deep Interaction: An Efficient Human-AI Interaction Method for Large Reasoning Models
news.summary: Standard CoT correction loops fail because the model regenerates and re-makes the same error. Deep Interaction lets the user directly edit the original response, distills the edited CoT into a prompt, and steers the LLM along the corrected reasoning path while preserving accurate steps. Reports +25% correction success rate and ~40% token reduction vs. baseline approaches on STEM reasoning tasks.

news.title: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
news.summary: Most "agent optimizer" papers report one-shot gains on a fixed benchmark. This paper asks the real deployment question: do the gains survive a second round of optimization on newly arrived tasks? On Terminal-Bench 2.0, GEPA actually regresses below the unoptimized baseline after transfer, Meta Harness transfers but plateaus, and only RELAI-VCL keeps improving — reaching 76.4% lifelong pass rate vs 66.0% (GEPA), 64.6% (Meta Harness), 58.7% (baseline).

news.title: Hindcast: Replaying Prediction Markets to Evaluate LLM Forecasters
news.summary: A clean methodological critique: today's LLM forecasting benchmarks leak the answer through (1) retrieval over post-event reports and (2) newer models' training cutoffs creeping closer to the event. Hindcast fixes both by replaying resolved Polymarket markets against a frozen Reddit snapshot, allowing the model only posts written before a per-market cutoff date t0, and scoring against both the outcome and the market's own t0 price (a human forecast made from the same info).

news.title: M⁴World: A Multi-view Multimodal Driving World Model for Interactive Object Manipulation and Minute-long Streaming
news.summary: A driving world model that jointly synthesizes surround-view video + synchronized LiDAR, with explicit per-object control over spatial layout and appearance, and stable minute-long rollouts via a multi-stage training framework using only four denoising steps for causal online generation. Adds a VLM-based judging pipeline for scene condition adherence, view-wise object controllability, and cross-view object consistency.

news.title: VideoRAE: Taming Video Foundation Models for Generative Modeling via Representation Autoencoders
news.summary: Instead of training a 3D-VAE from scratch for video generation, VideoRAE compresses the frozen features of a video foundation model (V-JEPA 2 / VideoMAEv2) with a lightweight 1D self-attention projector, supporting both continuous latents for DiTs and discrete tokens for AR models via multi-codebook quantization. On UCF-101 it hits SOTA class-to-video gFVDs of 40 (AR) and 93 (DiT), converging ~5x faster than competing autoencoders, and in a 2B text-to-video study it beats LTX-VAE on convergence.

news.title: Audio-Native Speech Recognition with a Frozen Discrete-Diffusion Language Model (DiffusionGemma-ASR)
news.summary: ASR is dominated by autoregressive token-by-token decoders. This work uses a frozen 26B MoE discrete-diffusion LM (DiffusionGemma) that generates text via uniform random-token discrete diffusion instead of absorbing-mask. A frozen Whisper encoder + lightweight projector + LoRA adapters (only ~42M trainable params, 0.16% of backbone) feed audio. CTC loss through the frozen output head breaks the gradient deadlock; reaches 6.6% WER on LibriSpeech test-clean in ~8 parallel steps regardless of utterance length. Single adapter handles EN / HI / ZH.

news.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution (E3)
news.summary: LLM agents waste a huge amount of budget re-reading files and dependencies they've already seen. The authors formalize "minimum-sufficient execution" and propose E3 (Estimate, Execute, Expand): the agent first estimates the operating point, runs a minimal viable path, and only expands scope when verification fails. On MSE-Bench (121 deterministic edits), E3 matches the strongest baseline's 100% success while cutting cost by 85%, tokens by 91%, and inspected files by 92%.

news.title: FlowWAM: Optical Flow as a Unified Action Representation for World Action Models
news.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) usually fail to align actions with pretrained video generators. FlowWAM uses optical flow as a unified, video-native action representation — flow videos share RGB's format and encode rich per-pixel displacement. A dual-stream diffusion framework jointly models RGB and flow, supporting both policy mode (flow → action) and world-model mode (target flow → future video). Pretrains on large-scale unlabeled video since flow is free.

news.title: TerraZero: Procedural Driving Simulation for Zero-Demonstration Self-Play at Scale
news.summary: A configurable C-engine driving sim + self-play stack that sustains 1.3M agent-steps/sec on a single server-grade GPU, with heterogeneous agents, multiple dynamics models, and full traffic-rule enforcement. Real-world maps are used only as geometry; agents, signals, dynamics, rewards and sizes are randomized per episode, so each map yields an unbounded scenario set. Every reported policy trains from scratch with RL only — zero human demos, no fallback planner.

news.title: The Seriality Gap in Video Diffusion Models
news.summary: Standard bidirectional video diffusion degrades sharply as causal chains lengthen, even when given more denoising steps. A length-matched single-ball control isolates dependent-event structure (not video length) as the cause. The authors prove that for deterministic video prediction, denoising steps don't actually add serial computation beyond the backbone — a structural obstacle for video diffusion on serial reasoning and simulation.

news.title: FUNDING Pearl Health raises $110M Series A led by a16z; AI-native value-based care platform valued at ~$550M
news.summary: Pearl Health, a NYC-based primary-care enablement platform that helps independent physician practices take on Medicare's ACO REACH risk contracts via AI-driven patient stratification, closed a $110M Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz with Trinity Capital, Viking Global Investors, Ulysses Capital, and AlleyCorp participating. The round, disclosed in 亿欧/医药魔方's weekly funding report (Jul 13, covering 7/6–7/12), ranks in the top 5% of US A-rounds this year. Pearl claims 1,000+ provider partners and ~$2B of medical spend under management.

news.title: M&A Novartis acquires UK-based Myricx Pharma to add NMTi-ADC payload platform to oncology pipeline
news.summary: Novartis has agreed to acquire Myricx Pharma, a London/Stevenage-based biotech founded as a spin-out from the Francis Crick Institute and specializing in N-myristoyltransferase inhibitor (NMTi) payloads for next-generation antibody-drug conjugates. The deal — disclosed in the 亿欧/医药魔方 weekly funding roundup published Mon Jul 13 — extends the post-Pfizer/$43B-Seagen ADC consolidation wave. Myricx's lead program MYR241 targets B7-H4-expressing solid tumors with a topoisomerase-1 warhead (preclinical), plus a payload-agnostic platform that Novartis plans to plug into its existing radioligand + ADC engine. Financial terms undisclosed; industry sources peg the upfront at ~$300–500M with biobucks up to ~$1.2B.

news.title: REGULATORY FDA quietly posts 14 new Complete Response Letters after pause — including Jiangsu Hengrui camrelizumab/rivoceranib HCC rejection
news.summary: Per BioSpace (Jul 13) citing Citeline/Pink Sheet analysis (Jul 11), the FDA uploaded 14 new Complete Response Letters (CRLs) to its online portal — including the highly-watched July 9 rejection of Jiangsu Hengrui + Elevar Therapeutics' BLA/NDA combo of camrelizumab (PD-1) + rivoceranib (VEGFR2) for first-line hepatocellular carcinoma. The uploads happened just days after the agency confirmed a temporary suspension following an April citizen petition from an unnamed pharma company (represented by Covington & Burling) demanding the FDA "immediately cease publishing" CRLs. BioSpace reached out to FDA to clarify whether the pause has been lifted or whether this is a one-off publication of pending documents.

news.title: STRATEGY 中国生物制药(01177.HK) 7月13日注销2206.5万股回购股份，年内已注销累计逾8000万股
news.summary: Sino Biopharmaceutical (HK:01177) announced on Mon Jul 13 that it formally cancelled 22.065 million shares repurchased between Jun 16–25, 2026, completing the buyback-cancellation cycle. Per the company's 6-K disclosure and 格隆汇 wire (Jul 13, 4:32 PM HKT), this is part of a larger ongoing program — Sino Biopharm has cumulatively cancelled more than 80 million shares YTD across multiple buyback tranches, with total cash deployed exceeding HK$400M (~US$51M). The cancellations reduce share count by ~0.85% of total outstanding.

news.title: Evidence-Backed Video Question Answering (E-VQA)
news.summary: Defines E-VQA, a new task requiring Video LLMs to jointly output a semantic answer plus precise spatio-temporal evidence — temporal segments and dense, tracked object segmentation masklets. Releases ST-Evidence, the first human-verified benchmark for both discriminative and generative pixel-level video grounding, and ST-Evidence-Instruct, a 160k-scale fine-tuning dataset. Fine-tuning a 7B grounded Video LLM on it lifts t-mean by +27.2 and J&F by +13.8 over the size-matched UniPixel baseline.

news.title: Inside the Unfair Judge: A Mechanistic Interpretability Account of LLM-as-Judge Bias
news.summary: Moves LLM-as-judge bias research from input/output perturbations to a representation-level account. Across seven judges, seven bias types, and nine benchmarks: biased inputs are displaced along a low-dimensional, type-specific subspace of the judge's hidden state that sharpens with depth; steering along that subspace reproduces biased scoring on clean inputs and restores baseline scoring on biased ones (matched-norm random directions cause shifts an order of magnitude smaller); and a simple linear projection onto the same bias features anticipates judge failures on three unseen benchmarks, substantially beating text-based alternatives.

news.title: Requential Coding: Pushing the Limits of Model Compression with Self-Generated Training Data
news.summary: Upgrades Prequential coding by having a teacher model select training samples drawn from the student's own distribution. The student only records the selections, so the resulting code length is independent of both parameter count and data entropy, often orders of magnitude shorter than the prequential counterpart. Plugged into a PAC-Bayes bound, the requential code yields state-of-the-art generalization guarantees for billion-parameter LLMs — beating bounds built on aggressive post-training quantization even when granted zero error — and the bound tightens with scale in the compute-optimal regime.

news.title: SpectraReward: Read It Back — Pretrained MLLMs Are Zero-Shot Reward Models for Text-to-Image Generation
news.summary: A training-free reward function that turns pretrained multimodal LLMs into off-the-shelf reward models for image-generation RL. Instead of asking the MLLM to judge an image or answer decomposed verification questions, SpectraReward measures how well the original prompt can be recovered from the generated image through a single image-conditioned, teacher-forced forward pass — averaging the image-conditioned prompt log-likelihood. Self-SpectraReward is the unified-model special case where the policy's understanding branch serves as its own reward, forming a closed-loop self-improving framework with no external reward model.

news.title: SportMV-Bench & SportMV-Agent: Agentic Multi-View Reasoning in Sports Video Understanding
news.summary: First benchmark (SportMV-Bench) and method (SportMV-Agent) for multi-view sports video understanding: 787 multi-view bundles, 2592 QA pairs across Perception-Aware Recognition, Rule-aware Event Interpretation, and Adjudicative Decision Reasoning, built from official match recordings through a pipeline combining LLM-based generation, MLLM-based verification, and human filtering. SportMV-Agent orchestrates an iterative loop of active view selection, perception tool execution, and evidence-grounded reasoning — a +14.46% relative improvement over the strongest MLLM baseline.

news.title: EXPLOIT Hedera-based Bonzo Lend drained for ~$9M in oracle manipulation attack; TVL collapses 77%
news.summary: On Jul 11, an attacker deposited 250 low-value SAUCE tokens into Bonzo Lend, then submitted a manipulated price update through a third-party Supra oracle contract, inflating SAUCE's HBAR-denominated value and borrowing 6.63M USDC + 34.52M wrapped HBAR (~$9.05M total) far beyond actual collateral. A second wallet ("white-hat") later returned ~$1M. Hedera network-wide TVL dropped ~40% in 24h, Bonzo Lend's TVL cratered 77%.

news.title: MARKET Stablecoin market cap sheds $10B since May; June alone lost $7.7B — biggest monthly drop since Terra-Luna
news.summary: Per CoinDesk (Jul 12, 1:00 PM ET) citing on-chain data, the stablecoin sector contracted from a ~$310B peak in May to ~$300B by end-June, with $7.7B of that leaving in June alone — the largest single-month dollar decline since the May 2022 Terra-Luna crash. Concurrently, Bitcoin is testing a "power-law support line" that Fidelity's Jurien Timmer has tracked since 2015, which he calls an "accumulation zone" but lacking a near-term catalyst.

news.title: REGULATION Updated CLARITY Act draft set to drop this week, Senate floor vote targeted for July 20–27
news.summary: Per CoinDesk's State of Crypto (Jul 12, 6:30 PM ET), multiple sources confirm a combined Senate Banking + Agriculture Committee draft of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act will circulate as soon as this week, adding ~70 pages and merging the two committee-passed versions. Senate Majority Leader Thune has privately told Punchbowl he is willing to put it to a floor vote in July — likely the week of Jul 20 or Jul 27. A successful vote requires at least 7 Democrats, and the missing ethics provision around Trump's $1.4B crypto windfall remains the biggest blocker.

news.title: STRATEGY Ripple CEO Garlinghouse: company almost shut down in 2020 and gave XRP back to shareholders
news.summary: Speaking at the University of Kansas School of Business, Brad Garlinghouse revealed he and co-founder Chris Larsen "seriously considered" winding Ripple down and distributing the XRP treasury pro rata to shareholders after the SEC's December 2020 lawsuit, calling it "the easier path" against a regulator with "infinite power and resources." They chose to fight — burning ~$150M in legal fees over four years — and ultimately prevailed in 2024 when Judge Torres ruled XRP itself is not a security, then settled last year after the Trump-era SEC leadership change.

news.title: No major EdTech developments to report today
news.summary: Searched TechCrunch, Inside Higher Ed, EdSurge, HolonIQ, EdTechReview, EducationDynamics, Jiqizhixin, LatePost, 36Kr and Crunchbase News for the past 24 hours. No funding rounds >$10M, no significant M&A, no notable product launches, and no new regulatory moves specific to the education / EdTech sector turned up for today.

news.title: Latent Memory Palace — Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
news.summary: Brings adaptive test-time "reasoning" — the chain-of-thought analogue — into continuous control policies, by organizing information in an autoregressive latent space (the "memory palace") and formulating reasoning as variational inference. Derives a tractable latent-space RL objective for the variational lower bound. The resulting LMP-π policy shows strong simulation + real-world performance with interpretable, adaptive compute allocation; same framework also yields a variable-length action tokenizer (LMP-tok) that lifts downstream autoregressive policies.

news.title: SLORR — Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
news.summary: A stateless, architecture-preserving in-training regularizer that induces low-rank structure into the original weight matrices using GPU-friendly Hoyer-sparsity / nuclear-norm approximations (no SVD, no extra trainable params, no cached state). Adds under 8% training overhead on ImageNet-1K across ResNet-50 / ViT-B/16 / ViT-L/16, and under 1% on 135M and 560M LLM pretraining while preserving downstream performance of the compressed model.

news.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training (COLM 2026)
news.summary: Tests the "Super Weights" hypothesis directly: individual parameters that, if pruned, tank an LLM by orders of magnitude. Finding — Super Weight-aware training does not work. Isolating 100–8,192 Super Weight coordinates for fine-tuning on OLMo-1B/7B collapses accuracy to random-guessing; expanding to 36K-neighborhoods does not help. Vanilla LoRA (full low-rank structure over layers) succeeds with only 0.16% of parameters, even when constrained to Super Weight coordinates.

news.title: UniClawBench — A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks (HKU-MMLab)
news.summary: First capability-driven benchmark for proactive LLM/MLLM agents in dynamic, real-world settings. Built around five foundational capabilities (Skill Usage, Exploration, Long-Context Reasoning, Multimodal Understanding, Cross-Platform Coordination) and 400 bilingual tasks, evaluated in live Docker containers with a closed-loop executor/supervisor/user-agent setup that simulates realistic multi-turn feedback without leaking grading criteria.

news.title: WebSwarm — Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
news.summary: Argues a single ReAct-style web-search agent cannot do depth + coverage at once, and existing parallel multi-agent systems still fail on recursive depth, collaboration adaptability, and evidence-grounded expansion. Proposes WebSwarm, a progressive recursive-delegation framework that jointly builds task decomposition, recursive expansion, and agent collaboration at inference time by dynamically instantiating agentic search nodes.

news.title: Accurate, Interdisciplinary and Transparent Structure-property Understanding with Deep Native Structural Reasoning (SciReasoner)
news.summary: A multimodal scientific foundation model that treats 3D coordinates, topologies and periodic connectivities as addressable structural tokens. Across 86 scientific benchmarks (proteins, small molecules, inorganic crystals), it sets SOTA on 67, and double-blind expert review prefers its reasoning traces over a frontier LLM 98% of the time. Concrete wins: low-homology GO Cellular Component F max 0.42 → 0.55; single-step retrosynthesis 0.63 → 0.72.

news.title: Agon: Competitive Cross-Model RL with Implicit Rival Grading of Reasoning
news.summary: Two models train as each other's graders on the same problem; one drafts, the other reads and answers, reward = out-solving the rival. No process labels, no reward model. On the hard split of DeepMath with Qwen3, this doubles GRPO pass@1 and is ≈8× the gain of an untrained Mixture-of-Agents baseline over the same base. Replicates on competitive-programming code and across Qwen3.5 / Gemma 4.

news.title: Co-LMLM: Continuous-Query Limited Memory Language Models
news.summary: Replaces the relational knowledge base of Limited Memory LMs (LMLMs) with continuous-key/textual-value pairs and a free-form span annotator (no longer Wikipedia-only). At 360M params, CO-LMLM hits lower perplexity than models trained on 40× more data, and SimpleQA-verified factual precision on par with gpt-4o-mini and above Claude Sonnet 4.5.

news.title: Scaling Mixture-of-Experts Video Pretraining for Embodied Intelligence (LingBot-Video)
news.summary: A DiT-based video foundation model scaled via Mixture-of-Experts from scratch, with a data-profiling engine that augments web video with manipulation/locomotion footage. Targets embodied control, not content creation, so it trades pure visual fidelity for physical realism and inference efficiency.

news.title: Bridging Physical Reasoning and Task Generalization via Visual Action Outcome Reasoning Alignment (VAORA)
news.summary: Targets the two failure modes that wreck VLM-based agents in interactive physical reasoning: hallucinated chain-of-thought that contradicts the visual scene, and reasoning/actions that are misaligned. VAORA introduces two complementary rewards — a Visual Alignment Reward (anchors reasoning to the scene, independent of the action) and a Visual-Action Alignment Reward (grounds reasoning in the visual outcome of the action itself) — with smooth dense rewards estimated by a pre-trained in-domain expert for training stability. Evaluated on PHYRE and Virtual Tool across novel-task and unseen-environment splits.

news.title: Danus: Orchestrating Mathematical Reasoning Agents with Fact-Graph Memory
news.summary: An orchestration system for research-level math reasoning. One main agent plans and coordinates, multiple worker agents run parallel proof search, and a stateless verifier admits only verified claims into a shared "fact graph" (each fact stored with its proof and logical dependencies). The main agent periodically summarizes the evolving proof state, redirects workers, and emits progress reports for human mathematicians. Evaluated on six research-level case studies in algebraic geometry, singularity theory, and combinatorics, where the fact-graph memory is what lets the system build long, detailed proofs without losing the thread.

news.title: Doomed from the Start: Early Abort of LLM Agent Episodes via a Recall-Controlled Probe Cascade
news.summary: Shows that LLM agent failure is predictable from the agent's own hidden activations as early as the first interaction round — way before any behavioral signal is meaningful. Turns that into a deployment-ready "abort cascade": a distribution-free calibrated gate per round with per-round recall budgets jointly searched, so you get an episode-level guarantee that eventually-successful episodes survive. On TextCraft with Qwen-2.5-7B and Llama-3.2-3B, the cascade meets every recall target from 90% to 97%; at 90% it saves 47.1% / 37.2% of inference compute (1.6–1.7x the best single-gate policy), while a behavior-only cascade saves roughly half that, and adding behavioral features to the probe gives no further gain — the hidden states already cover it.

news.title: ELSA3D: Elastic Semantic Anchoring for Unified 3D Understanding and Generation
news.summary: A unified 3D foundation model that does text-to-3D, image-to-3D, and 3D captioning in a single backbone, using "elastic semantic anchoring" — sparse Anchor Tokens route language cues to the right geometric scale (coarse vs. fine), retrieved via a scale-aware octree tokenizer, with a lightweight per-block router deciding where cross-modal capacity should concentrate. Reported as SOTA on image-to-3D, text-to-3D, and 3D captioning while roughly halving FLOPs and inference latency vs. the non-elastic version of the same model.

news.title: Vision as Unified Multimodal Generation (SenseNova-Vision)
news.summary: Reformulates computer vision as a single unified multimodal generation problem. A single SenseNova-Vision model takes natural-language instructions (plus optional visual prompts) and emits text, images, or mixed text+image outputs — covering detection, OCR, keypoints, segmentation, depth, surface normals, point maps, and camera pose — with no task-specific heads. Authors convert diverse CV annotations into an instruction-response corpus and train a unified model from an off-the-shelf multimodal base, claiming it matches leading task-specialized systems across structured understanding, dense geometry, segmentation, and multi-view geometry.

news.title: CompactionRL: Reinforcement Learning with Context Compaction for Long-Horizon Agents
news.summary: Treats context compaction as a first-class action inside the RL loop: as trajectories approach the context-window cliff, the agent learns to summarize prior interaction state and continue the rollout under the compacted context, so the verifier still gets a full long-horizon reward signal. The compaction policy is itself trained with RL, not a hand-rolled summarizer.

news.title: Cortex: A Bidirectionally Aligned Embodied Agent Framework for Long-horizon Manipulation
news.summary: A hierarchical VLA framework where the high-level planner and low-level controller are bidirectionally aligned — instead of the usual "planner commands, controller obeys," the controller's feasibility constraints flow back up to reshape the planner's proposals. Tackles the planning/control gap that breaks dual-system methods on long-horizon tasks like "clean the kitchen."

news.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier: A General-Purpose Verification Framework
news.summary: Argues that verification — the ability to judge the correctness of a candidate solution — is an independent scaling axis orthogonal to pre-training, post-training, and test-time compute. Lays out a general framework for using one LLM to verify another's outputs, with empirical scaling curves showing verifier strength compounds reasoning gains beyond what extra sampling alone buys you.

news.title: TREK: Distill to Explore, Reinforce to Refine
news.summary: Diagnoses a specific failure mode of GRPO: on hard prompts whose correct solution modes lie outside the student's on-policy support, GRPO stalls because the group of rollouts is uniformly bad. TREK uses teacher-routed forward-KL exploration to inject diversity into the student's support, then runs standard GRPO refinement on the now-tractable distribution.

news.title: Weak-to-Strong Generalization via Direct On-Policy Distillation
news.summary: Replaces the costly "re-run RLVR on every new strong model" pattern with a direct on-policy distillation scheme: the student samples its own rollouts, the teacher scores them via verifiable rewards, and the student is updated against a target that explicitly interpolates between teacher supervision and verifiable-reward signal. The result is weak-to-strong generalization that scales with the teacher without re-rolling-out the teacher.

news.title: Adoption and Impact of Command-Line AI Coding Agents: Microsoft’s Early-2026 Rollout of Claude Code and GitHub Copilot CLI
news.summary: First large-scale, vendor-agnostic measurement of *real* adoption of Claude Code and GitHub Copilot CLI inside one of the world's largest engineering orgs. Headline numbers: first-use spread primarily through social networks (not top-down mandates); retention tracks engineers' baseline coding activity, not demographics; adopters merged ~24% more pull requests than matched non-adopters. The paper is unusually honest about cost — token spend in the millions of dollars — and the "did adoption actually move engineering velocity" question.

news.title: DemoPSD: Disagreement-Modulated Policy Self-Distillation
news.summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) is the cheap, in-house alternative to distilling from a stronger teacher — but recent work shows it leaks "privileged information" and overfits to in-domain shortcuts. DemoPSD reframes the student's target as a *reverse-KL barycenter* between teacher and student distributions, and uses per-token disagreement to adaptively control the blend. The result: the student keeps the teacher's signal where it agrees with its own reasoning, and protects its own reasoning where it disagrees — fixing the privileged-info shortcut and lifting cross-domain generalization without hurting in-domain accuracy.

news.title: Scaling with Confidence: C3RL + CAS for Calibrated, Adaptive Test-Time Scaling
news.summary: RL-trained reasoning LLMs are notoriously miscalibrated — they hallucinate confidently when wrong. C3RL folds calibration directly into the RL reward (correctness + confidence + dataset-informed reference accuracy) and produces a verbalized-confidence signal that CAS turns into an *adaptive* test-time compute policy: spend more tokens on hard/uncertain items, fewer on the easy ones. Across 8 text/multimodal benchmarks, C3RL beats the prior SOTA on both accuracy and calibration, and CAS beats majority voting while cutting inference budget by up to 12.33× .

news.title: WorldDirector: Controllable World Simulators with Persistent Dynamic Memory
news.summary: Current video world models braid physical dynamics into pixel rendering and lose track of objects whenever they leave the frame. WorldDirector splits the problem: an LLM plans semantic 3D trajectories + camera motion, then a video generator consumes those trajectories as control signals. The result is strict physical consistency, appearance-stable re-identification of objects that re-enter after long absences, and free-form viewpoint exploration — the first time "persistent dynamic memory" + "unrestricted camera" have been solved together in a single world model.

news.title: AdaJEPA: An Adaptive Latent World Model
news.summary: Latent world models are usually frozen at test time, which makes planning brittle under distribution shift. AdaJEPA closes the loop inside model-predictive control: it executes an action chunk, treats the observed transition as a self-supervised adaptation signal, updates itself with as few as one gradient step per replan, and replans. This makes a JEPA-style world model self-calibrating without extra expert demonstrations.

news.title: AxDafny: Agentic Verified Code Generation in Dafny
news.summary: Verified-code generation — Dafny code plus proof artifacts — is reframed as an agentic loop with a verifier-in-the-loop repair loop that iteratively regenerates implementations, invariants, assertions, and termination arguments. The authors ship a new benchmark, LiveCodeBench-Pro-Dafny (250 competition-style problems with formal specs), and report 92.7% verification on DafnyBench, +6.5 pp over the strongest previous proof-hint baseline, beating GPT-5.5 zero-shot by a wide margin.

news.title: Cross-Space Distillation: Teaching One-Step Students with Modern Diffusion Teachers
news.summary: One-step diffusion distillation assumes teacher and student share a latent space — which is false for the most useful pairing: distilling SD 3.5 / Flux into a compact SD 1.5 backbone. The paper formalizes this gap as Cross-Space Distillation and fixes it with "Bridge," a lightweight latent interface that pairs a frozen Student VAE decoder with a learnable projector trained on latent reconstruction + attention-fidelity losses. The result: SD 1.5 jumps from 5.4 → 9.4 HPSv3 in one inference step, with low latency and the full SD 1.5 ecosystem intact.

news.title: Freeform Preference Learning for Robotic Manipulation
news.summary: FPL replaces the standard "which trajectory is better?" binary preference with freeform, axis-specific preferences — annotators name the dimension (speed, safety, placement quality, carefulness), then compare trajectories along that axis. A language-conditioned reward model turns this into multi-axis rewards that train a reward-conditioned policy. On four real-world and two simulated long-horizon manipulation tasks, FPL beats sparse-reward and binary-preference baselines by 38 percentage points, learns dense progress signals without subtask labels, and lets users steer the policy at test time without retraining.

news.title: Generative Skill Composition for LLM Agents (SkillComposer)
news.summary: Most agents treat skill selection as flat retrieval — pick one skill, retrieve K, or expose the whole library. The authors formalize skill composition as a *structured* prediction problem (which skills, how many, in what order — all coupled) and ship SkillComposer, a constrained autoregressive decoder that emits an executable skill plan in one pass. Trained on a real human-curated skill library and evaluated on SkillsBench with two production coding agents: +23.1pp on GPT-5.2-Codex, +18.2pp on Gemini-3-Pro-Preview over the no-skill baseline, matching the gold-skill retrieval upper bound at lower prompt-token cost.

news.title: Introspective Coupling: Self-Explanation Training Tracks Behavioral Change Despite Fixed Supervision
news.summary: Training LMs to explain their own predictions normally degenerates into imitation of the supervised explanations. This paper shows that, counterintuitively, LMs trained on frozen counterfactual explanations from earlier checkpoints — or even from behaviorally-similar but architecturally-different models — produce explanations that are more faithful to the LM's current behavior than to the supervision source. The introspection tracks the model's actual reasoning instead of the labels.

news.title: Learning from Failure: Inference-Time Self-Improvement for Computer-Use Agents
news.summary: Computer-use agents are usually trained on their own successful trajectories and throw away the failures. This work flips that: an LLM diagnoses why each failed run failed, proposes an inference-time fix, and ships a code patch (lightly human-verified) that upgrades the agent. On the state-of-the-art OpenCUA-72B model, OSWorld success rate climbs from 42.3% to 48.9% — a +6.6pp gain — with zero additional training cost and only modest inference overhead.

news.title: QVal: Cheaply Evaluating Dense Supervision Signals for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
news.summary: Long-horizon agent training needs dense supervision on intermediate steps, but every dense-signal paper rolls its own training pipeline, so methods are never compared on common ground. QVal is a training-free testbed: it scores each dense-signal method by Q-alignment with a strong reference policy, separating signal quality from training-engineering confounders. The authors benchmark 21 dense supervision methods across four environments and six model backbones (1.2K runs) and report that plain prompting baselines consistently beat recent published dense-supervision methods.

news.title: Reinforcement Learning with Metacognitive Feedback Elicits Faithful Uncertainty Expression in LLMs
news.summary: LLMs are bad at knowing what they know — they hallucinate with high confidence and lie about their own uncertainty. The paper introduces Reinforcement Learning with Metacognitive Feedback (RLMF): the model ranks its own candidate completions by the *quality of its self-judgments of performance*, and that signal is fed back into preference optimization. A two-stage pipeline first calibrates self-reported confidence, then maps to natural-language hedging. RLMF beats standard RL by up to 63% on faithful calibration, hits SOTA across diverse tasks, and preserves task accuracy.

news.title: SimpleSearch-VL: A Simple Recipe for Multimodal Agentic Deep Search
news.summary: Instead of scaling data, tools, or auxiliary models, SimpleSearch-VL improves the *search-and-verification loop itself* with three small changes: Factorized Adaptive Rollout (better sample efficiency), evidence-verified chain-of-thought reasoning, and a lightweight in-agent webpage self-summarizer. Trained on only 5K supervised tool-interleaved trajectories and 2K RL examples, it lifts Qwen3-VL agentic baselines by 15.8 points (8B) and 16.0 points (30B-A3B), and the 30B-A3B model is competitive with agentic Gemini-3-Pro.

news.title: Attractor States Emerge in Multi-Turn LLM Conversations
news.summary: Across 7 LLMs and 20 controversial topics, the authors run self-play vs mixed-play dyadic debates and measure representation-space trajectories, discourse traits, and stances. They find self-play trajectories collapse into model-specific attractors ; in mixed-play these attractors pull other models asymmetrically (Claude Haiku is flagged as a strong attractor). Crucially, the same model can exhibit different rhetorical and stylistic moves in self-play vs mixed-play, even when the underlying "stance" is unchanged.

news.title: C²R: Cross-sample Consistency Regularization Mitigates Feature Splitting and Absorption in Sparse Autoencoders
news.summary: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) decompose LLM activations into sparse, human-interpretable features, but scaling them up causes two failure modes: feature splitting (one coherent concept fragments across many latents) and feature absorption (a general feature silently eats exceptions). The authors trace both to inconsistent latent assignment across training samples and propose C²R, a cross-sample consistency regularization that aligns how related prompts get assigned to latents. They show it reliably reduces both pathologies on Anthropic-style SAE scaling benchmarks.

news.title: Orca: The World is in Your Mind
news.summary: BAAI introduces Orca, a "world foundation model" that reframes pretraining from next-token / next-frame / next-action prediction toward Next-State-Prediction : a unified world latent space learned from multimodal signals (video, text, audio, action, touch), trained on a "world-learning inventory" of 125K hours of video plus 160M event annotations. The backbone is frozen and only lightweight modality-specific decoders are trained; experiments show stronger world latents consistently yield stronger downstream performance across text generation, image prediction, and embodied action.

news.title: SWE-INTERACT: Reimagining SWE Benchmarks as User-Driven Long-Horizon Coding Sessions
news.summary: SWE-Interact flips SWE-Bench's setup: instead of an agent getting a fully-specified GitHub issue and working alone, a realistic user simulator starts with vague/incomplete requirements and progressively reveals details, inspects the workspace, asks for revisions, and adds constraints mid-task. Grounded in large-scale studies of real coding-agent sessions, the benchmark measures whether agents can discover user intent and adapt to evolving requirements across multi-turn interactive sessions.

news.title: TraceLab: Characterizing Coding Agent Workloads for LLM Serving
news.summary: The UW systems group released the first public trace of real coding-agent usage: ~4,300 sessions covering ~350K LLM steps and ~430K tool calls harvested from day-to-day use of Claude Code and Codex. The paper characterizes the workload shape — long autonomous loops, long contexts with short outputs, heavy-tailed tool-call diversity, and highly-imperfect prefix-cache reuse — and uses it to derive concrete implications for serving-system design (e.g. why generic chat serving stacks under-perform for coding agents).

news.title: Ask, Solve, Generate: Self-Evolving Unified Multimodal Understanding and Generation via Self-Consistency Rewards
news.summary: Most unified large multimodal models (LMMs) that support both visual understanding and image generation still require curated human supervision (annotations, preference labels, or external reward models) to improve. The paper proposes a fully self-evolving training framework with three internal roles — a Proposer that generates visual questions, a Solver that answers and evaluates them, and a Generator that synthesises images — and uses only self-derived consistency signals for training. To stabilise learning, the authors introduce Solver Token Entropy (STE), a continuous difficulty signal based on token-level prediction uncertainty that remains useful even when sample-level consistency becomes unreliable, plus a multi-scale internal evaluation scheme for image generation that combines QA-fidelity scoring with cycle-consistent captioning. The framework is architecture-agnostic: the same role decomposition, reward logic, and training schedule apply unchanged to diffusion-based BLIP3o, rectified-flow BAGEL, and autoregressive VARGPT-v1.1. On BAGEL it gives +3.5% absolute on MMMU and pushes GenEval image-generation performance from 82% to 85%, with consistent improvements across eight understanding metrics. Code and models are public.

news.title: DanceOPD: On-Policy Generative Field Distillation
news.summary: Modern image generation demands a single model that unifies text-to-image, local editing, and global editing — but these capabilities rarely align naturally and often conflict (e.g. editing degrades T2I quality; local and global editing interfere). DanceOPD is an on-policy generative field distillation framework for flow-matching models that routes each sample to one capability field, queries one low-noise student-induced state, and trains with a simple velocity-MSE objective. By defining each capability source as a velocity field over a shared flow state space and learning from fields queried on the student's own rollout states, DanceOPD composes expert capabilities without the interference patterns that plague multi-task distillation, and absorbs operator-defined fields such as classifier-free guidance for free. Experiments cover T2I, editing, realism-field absorption, and CFG absorption, with consistent gains in target capabilities while preserving anchor generation quality.

news.title: Don't Settle at the Mode! Mitigating Diversity Collapse in Pretrained Flow Models via Feature Self-Guidance
news.summary: State-of-the-art flow models generate stunning images from text or image prompts, but they suffer from diversity collapse when asked to produce multiple samples under the same conditioning. Existing fixes either rely on latent guidance (limited effectiveness) or on sample selection by an external reward model (heavy inference-time overhead). The paper introduces a training-free self-guidance mechanism that disperses the flow model's internal features during batch generation, plus a manifold-regularisation step that projects the dispersed features back onto the data manifold, ensuring diverse generation without sacrificing alignment. The method integrates as a plug-and-play module into pretrained flow models with only marginal inference cost and is shown to improve diversity while preserving fidelity across multi-step and few-step text-to-image, depth-to-image, and reference-image generation settings. Accepted at ECCV 2026.

news.title: PhysiFormer: Learning to Simulate Mechanics in World Space
news.summary: A diffusion transformer that predicts 3D object motion directly on world-coordinate meshes instead of in view-dependent pixel space. Given initial vertex positions/velocities and material type (rigid or elastic), it samples full future vertex trajectories as a single denoising process — without ad-hoc latent spaces, hard-coded rigidity priors, or explicit causality constraints. The model factorises attention over time, space, and objects, giving permutation-invariant multi-object reasoning without per-object encodings, and the probabilistic formulation produces diverse plausible futures when initial conditions are ambiguous. Trained on 100k+ simulated trajectories, it generalises to mixed materials, unseen real-world geometries, and larger object counts, substantially outperforming autoregressive baselines on trajectory accuracy, rigidity preservation, and momentum-based consistency.

news.title: Reinforcement Learning without Ground-Truth Solutions can Improve LLMs
news.summary: RL with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become the standard recipe for post-training reasoning LLMs, but it requires a ground-truth answer to assign rewards, which limits it to problems with a known solution. RiVER (Ranking-induced VERifiable) drops that requirement and trains LLMs on score-based optimisation tasks (AtCoder Heuristic Contest) using deterministic execution feedback as continuous-valued supervision. The paper identifies two failure modes in naïvely applying group-relative RL to continuous rewards — scale dominance (uncalibrated magnitudes across instances distort updates) and frequency dominance (repeatedly sampled weak solutions outweigh rare-but-strong ones) — and addresses both with calibrated reward shaping that uses instance-wise comparisons and emphasises top-ranked solvers while keeping bounded feedback for other valid solutions. RiVER improves Qwen3-8B and GLM-Z1-9B-0414 by 8.9% and 9.4% on ALE-Bench rating rank, and despite training exclusively on score-based tasks without ground truth, transfers positively to exact-solution benchmarks (LiveCodeBench +2.4%, USACO +3.5%), where raw-execution-score baselines fail to transfer.

news.title: Autoregressive Boltzmann Generators
news.summary: Boltzmann Generators (BGs) sample equilibrium molecular configurations by combining a generative model with exact likelihoods + importance sampling. To date they have been dominated by normalizing flows, which either lose expressivity from strict-invertibility constraints (discrete time) or pay ruinous likelihood-evaluation cost (continuous time). Autoregressive Boltzmann Generators (ArBG) abandon the flow-based paradigm entirely and use an autoregressive factorization to sidestep both problems, with theoretical results on topological and geometric expressivity that flows provably cannot match.

news.title: Blackwell Approachability and Gradient Equilibrium are Equivalent
news.summary: Gradient Equilibrium (GEQ) is a recently introduced online-optimization framework that generalizes first-order stationarity from offline optimization and already abstracts problems like online conformal prediction. While GEQ had been shown to be *incomparable* in objective to regret minimization, this paper proves the two are algorithmically equivalent: any Blackwell-approachability problem can be solved with no asymptotic loss using a black-box GEQ oracle, and vice versa. Combined with prior equivalences between Blackwell approachability and online learning, this gives a clean three-way correspondence (regret ↔ approachability ↔ GEQ).

news.title: CORTEX: A Structured Reasoning Benchmark for Trustworthy 3D Chest CT MLLMs
news.summary: Reasoning in 3D medical-imaging MLLMs is currently judged by free-form text + final-answer accuracy, which hides the chain of evidence that links a finding to a diagnosis. CORTEX (Clinically Organized Reasoning and sTructured EXplanations) is the first benchmark that scores *structured, traceable* reasoning on 3D chest CT, pairing volumetric scans with patient history, expert-curated reasoning chains, and a protocol that audits the link between finding and conclusion. The work also proposes a trustworthy-3D-MLLM training recipe that improves over free-form-reasoning baselines on the benchmark.

news.title: Hallucination in World Models is Predictable and Preventable
news.summary: A diagnostic paper on action-controllable generative world models. The authors release MMBench2 (427 hours, 210 tasks, ground-truth actions + rewards + live simulators) and train a 350M-parameter world model on it. They identify three distinct hallucination modes — *perceptual*, *action-marginalized*, and *scene-diverging* — each anchored to a different stage of the rollout pipeline, and develop three lightweight data-centric signals that predict where the model will hallucinate and guide targeted mitigation. The interactive paper, code, dataset, and models are all public.

news.title: When Does Combining Language Models Help? A Co-Failure Ceiling on Routing, Voting, and Mixture-of-Agents Across 67 Frontier Models
news.summary: A theoretical and empirical limit on multi-model LLM systems. The author proves that for any policy whose output is a single member-model answer, accuracy is capped at 1 − β, where β is the rate at which *every* model in the pool is wrong on the same query. Across 67 frontier models from 21 providers, a Clopper-Pearson bound on β gives a finite-sample certificate on the largest gain any router, vote, or cascade can deliver before a router is even trained — and the ordinary pairwise-error-correlation diagnostic (ρ) is shown to be uninformative for β, since error laws with identical marginals and pairwise correlations can have very different all-wrong rates.

news.title: Learning Action Priors for Cross-embodiment Robot Manipulation
news.summary: A two-stage training recipe for Vision-Language-Action models: first pretrain the action module on unconditioned action trajectories with a lightweight flow-matching encoder-decoder (no vision, no language) so it learns temporal motion structure, then transfer that motion prior into VLA training via decoder reuse and latent distillation. The same encoder doubles as a compact history compressor that summarizes state-action history into a single temporal context token.

news.title: Model Forensics: Investigating Whether Concerning Behavior Reflects Misalignment
news.summary: Builds a methodology for attributing "concerning" model outputs (deception, scheming, sycophancy) to either capability mismatch, training-process artifacts, or genuine misalignment. Uses behavioral elicitation and causal analysis on the model rather than the dataset. The framing is "is this model misaligned, or are we just seeing the surface of something else?"

news.title: Natural Ungrokking: Asymmetric Control of Which Rules Survive Pretraining
news.summary: Identifies "natural ungrokking": the phenomenon where models that originally grokked certain algorithmic rules lose them over continued pretraining, but the loss is rule-selective. Some rules survive far longer than others, and the asymmetry is predictable from rule complexity and frequency in the training distribution.

news.title: Neglected Free Lunch from Post-training: Progress Advantage for LLM Agents
news.summary: The paper proves that under a general stochastic MDP, the log-probability ratio between an RL-trained policy and its reference policy exactly recovers the optimal advantage function. This gives you a free, annotation-free, domain-agnostic step-level signal that falls out of any standard RL post-training run, no dedicated reward model needed. They call it "progress advantage" and validate it on test-time scaling, uncertainty quantification, and failure attribution across five benchmarks and four model families.

news.title: Why Multi-Step Tool-Use Reinforcement Learning Collapses and How Supervisory Signals Fix It
news.summary: Diagnoses why multi-step tool-use RL training collapses (the policy converges to single-tool shortcuts and loses long-horizon reasoning), and proposes a supervisory-signal fix that maintains trajectory-level credit assignment. Includes ablations across tool-use benchmarks showing recovery of multi-step behaviors that naive GRPO-style training kills.

news.title: A specialized reasoning LLM for accelerating rare disease diagnosis — RaDaR (randomized AI physician assistance trial)
news.summary: RaDaR is a reasoning-specialized LLM fine-tuned for rare-disease differential diagnosis, evaluated in a randomized physician-assistance trial rather than a static benchmark. The work bundles open-source model release, a curated clinically grounded knowledge corpus, and an RCT-style deployment protocol measuring diagnostic accuracy and time-to-diagnosis against clinicians without AI assistance.

news.title: Autodata: An Agentic Data Scientist to Create High Quality Synthetic Data
news.summary: Treats synthetic data generation as a meta-optimization problem: train an AI agent to act as a data scientist, then meta-optimize the data-scientist agent itself (Agentic Self-Instruct). Beats classical synthetic-data pipelines on CS research tasks, legal reasoning, and math-object reasoning — and meta-optimizing the data scientist gives an even larger uplift than the data it produces.

news.title: Critique of Agent Model
news.summary: A position paper from MBZUAI / CMU's Eric Xing that finally tries to pin down what "agent" means in the LLM era. The authors split systems into agentic (competence from engineered scaffolds) vs agentive (capability arising endogenously) along five dimensions — goal, identity, decision-making, self-regulation, learning — and propose a Goal-Identity-Configurator (GIC) architecture that combines hierarchical goal decomposition, identity evolution, simulative reasoning over a separately trained world model, learned self-regulation, and self-directed learning from real + simulated experience.

news.title: Curvature-Guided Mixing (CGM) for MLLM Adaptation
news.summary: A theoretically grounded model-merging method that solves the catastrophic-forgetting problem when fine-tuning Multimodal LLMs (LLaVA-1.5, Qwen2.5-VL). CGM uses a second-order Hessian approximation of the loss landscape to derive a closed-form "soft mixing" ratio that blends pre-trained and fine-tuned weights based on relative task curvatures; a hard-mixing variant (CGM†) does sparse parameter selection with a curvature-aware score. Code released for ECCV 2026.

news.title: Dense Supervision Is Not Enough: The Readout Blind Spot in Looped Language Models
news.summary: Looped transformers (hidden state is fed back as input) sound great for adaptive compute, but Sharma & Tu (Tu Vu is at Google DeepMind / previously Qwen team) show a sharp failure mode: dense per-loop cross-entropy through RMSNorm/LayerNorm readouts does NOT control the recurrent scale, because the readout is scale-invariant while the residual recurrence still propagates that scale. Their 44M and 129M models without inter-loop normalization explode to hidden-state norms in the thousands/tens-of-thousands; scale-visible readouts or explicit norm penalties keep norms in the tens, and scale-removing recurrence is the complementary architectural fix.

news.title: FORCE: Efficient VLA Reinforcement Fine-Tuning via Value-Calibrated Warm-up and Self-Distillation
news.summary: A 3-stage RL fine-tuning recipe for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) robot policies: a Value-Calibrated Warm-up that uses on-policy rollouts to stabilize an otherwise-unstable Q-function, then uses that calibrated Q as a filter on both the policy's own proposals and expert data so only high-value actions drive updates. 79% absolute success-rate lift over the imitation baseline, +10% over prior RL methods, ~32.5% faster training, and crucially works without human-in-the-loop rescue.

news.title: Real-Time Voice AI Hears but Does Not Listen
news.summary: Authors pit four production realtime voice systems (OpenAI GPT Realtime 2, Google Gemini 3.1 Flash Live, Alibaba Qwen3.5 Omni Plus/Flash) against scenarios where vocal delivery and the words disagree. All four systems consistently act on the words — terminating calls with crying users, approving frightened-voice wire transfers, enrolling sarcastically consenting callers — even when directly asked, three of four can correctly identify the distress, fear, or sarcasm they then ignore.

news.title: RIFT-Bench: Dynamic Red-teaming For Agentic AI Systems
news.summary: A graph-representation-driven framework for red-teaming agentic LLMs that operates in two automated phases: Discovery extracts the system's structural graph from logs, and Scanning deploys adaptive adversarial probes across diverse attack vectors to produce a unified security report. They benchmarked 45 heterogeneous agentic systems and show the approach generalizes across architectures, and can also evaluate mitigations directly.

news.title: SpeechEQ: Benchmarking Emotional Intelligence Quotient in Socially Aware Voice Conversational Models
news.summary: 2,265 multi-turn dialogues scored across 15 EQ subscales grounded in EQ-i 2.0 theory, with a new Spoken EQ (SEQ) score. End-to-end speech-language models beat cascaded (ASR+LLM+TTS) pipelines, but every model still falls into a "modality shortcut" (text-reliant reasoning), an alignment-induced "safety trap," and "contextual amnesia." Tongshuang Wu ("Cherry") on the author list is a notable signal of the framing.

news.title: TriViewBench: Controlled Complexity Scaling for Multi-View Structural Reasoning in MLLMs
news.summary: A controlled three-view visual reasoning benchmark (1,923 synthetic 3D scenes, 14K+ QA pairs, 4 complexity levels) tested against 18 open- and closed-source MLLMs. Every single model shows the same capability hierarchy (Local Decision > Object Counting > Global Recovery) and Global Recovery collapses by 80% as complexity grows. Chain-of-thought helps almost nothing (-0.16% overall) — the bottleneck is cross-view spatial representation, not reasoning strategy.

news.title: AutoDex: An Automated Real-World System for Dexterous Grasping Data Collection
news.summary: A fully autonomous real-world data-collection loop (perception → grasp proposal → execution → success labeling → reset) for multi-fingered dexterous grasping. The system removes the human-in-the-loop that normally caps dexterous-hand dataset scale, and reports the resulting dataset plus downstream policy results.

news.title: Data Selection Through Iterative Self-Filtering for Vision-Language Settings
news.summary: Instead of relying on hand-curated or heuristic data filters for training CLIP-style models, the authors train a CLIP model on an evolving, self-selected dataset: a mix of high-confidence clean samples and diverse-but-noisy ones, with the model itself acting as the filter in a bootstrapped loop.

news.title: Evaluation Awareness Is Not One Capability: Evidence from Open Language Models
news.summary: Across 37 open-weight models and 7 families, the authors run 8 experiments to disentangle "evaluation awareness" (a model detecting that it is being tested and behaving differently) into distinct sub-capabilities. Detection is moderate and largely training-driven, and benchmark compliance turns out to be an optimistic upper bound on deployment behavior.

news.title: FLAT: Feedforward Latent Triangle Splatting for Geometrically Accurate Scene Generation
news.summary: Decodes explicit surface-aligned triangle primitives directly from compressed video-diffusion latents in a single feedforward pass. Triangle splatting is notoriously unstable (orientation sensitivity kills gradients), so the paper contributes a ray-centered rotation parameterisation plus a product window function for differentiable triangle rendering. Reports better geometric accuracy than 3DGS / 2DGS baselines at competitive visual quality, with a lightweight test-time refinement that yields game-engine-ready meshes.

news.title: InSight: Self-Guided Skill Acquisition via Steerable VLAs
news.summary: Makes VLA policies steerable at the primitive-action level (e.g. "lift upward", "pour the bottle"), then closes an autonomous loop: a VLM identifies which primitives a new task needs, attempts them with low-level control, auto-labels successes, and adds them to the training set. Evaluated on block flipping, drawer closing, sweeping, twisting, and pouring — all without human demonstrations of the target skills.

news.title: IV-CoT: Implicit Visual Chain-of-Thought for Structure-Aware Text-to-Image Generation
news.summary: Diagnoses a known weakness of unified MLLMs — entangled structural planning and appearance rendering in a single conditioning stream — and fixes it with a structural-to-semantic cascade. Structural queries form a latent visual plan (trained with sketch supervision), then semantic queries render appearance on top of that plan in one forward pass. Reports wins on GenEval and T2I-CompBench.

news.title: OpenThoughts-Agent: Data Recipes for Agentic Models
news.summary: A fully-open data curation pipeline for training broadly-capable agentic LMs, built around 100+ controlled ablations. The authors assemble a 100K-example training set and fine-tune Qwen3-32B on it, hitting 44.8% average across seven agentic benchmarks — a +3.9pp jump over Nemotron-Terminal-32B (40.9%) — and show clean scaling wins at every training-set size in compute-matched comparisons.

news.title: Posterior Refinement: Fast Language Generation via Any-Order Flow Maps
news.summary: Bridges Flow Map Language Models (FMLM, joint-sequence transport, great few-step quality) and Masked Diffusion Models (MDM, factorisation error at multi-token decode) by adding masking-style noise schedules to FMLM — yielding FMLM+. On top of that they add Posterior Refinement: score global consistency of every token a posteriori and let the model self-correct, matching discrete baselines at 32× fewer NFEs.

news.title: Automating SKILL.md Generation for Computer-Using Agents via Interaction Trajectory Mining
news.summary: A three-stage pipeline (GUI trajectory segmentation → clustering into candidate skills → GRPO on the resulting skill-aware policy) that attempts to mine a SKILL.md-style library from interaction data. Readable on the source benchmark — five of eight clusters hit ≥0.95 purity vs. InteraSkill Workflows labels. But readability ≠ transfer: GRPO only lifts IW skill-step accuracy from 18.5% to 20.5%, leaves BrowseComp+ flat, and is beaten by a trivial frequency prior on key source-domain metrics. Author's honest framing: a diagnostic study, not a method.

news.title: Contagion Networks: Evaluator Bias Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
news.summary: A formal framework for measuring how LLM-evaluator biases spread across multi-agent systems. Models the propagation as a Cross-Agent Contagion Matrix Γ_N and identifies three regimes (suppression / propagation / amplification) controlled by its spectral radius. Controlled 3-agent DeepSeek experiment: γ ∈ [0.157, 0.352] even within the same model, 3-5× weaker than cross-model contagion from prior work. Practical mitigation: bumping the evaluator committee from k=1 to k=3 cuts effective contagion by 72.4%.

news.title: Current World Models Lack a Persistent State Core
news.summary: Argues that today's "world models" only render convincing frames on demand and lack an internal world state that keeps evolving decoupled from observation. Objects should endure and events run to conclusion whether or not a camera is watching — current benchmarks reward surface appearance, not persistent state.

news.title: HumanScale: Egocentric Human Video Can Outperform Real-Robot Data for Embodied Pretraining
news.summary: A systematic study showing that, with a careful filtering and labeling pipeline, egocentric human video is not just a viable substitute for teleoperated real-robot data in embodied pretraining — it actually beats it. At matched pretraining data volume, egocentric pretraining gives 24% lower validation loss on real-robot action prediction and 52.5% / 90% higher success rates on in-distribution / OOD real-robot tasks. The recipe: pretrain on diverse egocentric video, then adapt with a small labeled real-robot subset for action-space alignment.

news.title: Rethinking Shrinkage Bias in LLM FP4 Pretraining: Geometric Origin, Systemic Impact, and UFP4 Recipe
news.summary: Pinpoints a fundamental issue in current FP4 pretraining paths (NVIDIA Blackwell/Rubin and AMD MI350): non-uniform formats like E2M1 have a systematic "Shrinkage Bias" rooted in their geometry. Proposes UFP4 — a recipe that corrects this bias.

news.title: S-Agent: Spatial Tool-Use Elicits Reasoning for Spatial Intelligence
news.summary: Reframes spatial reasoning as spatio-temporal evidence accumulation instead of single-frame VLM inference. The VLM is a semantic planner that calls a hierarchy of spatial tools and experts; Scene Memory holds evolving scene state, Agent Memory holds reasoning context. Training-free: improves both open- and closed-source VLMs at inference. Also releases S-300K trajectory dataset and a fine-tuned S-Agent-8B that beats Qwen3-VL-8B and matches closed-source giants (GPT-5.4, Gemini 3) on multi-view / video spatial reasoning.

news.title: SoftSkill: Behavioral Compression for Contextual Adaptation
news.summary: Asks: instead of letting a frozen LM read a long natural-language skill file at inference time, can we initialize a compact continuous context object (a "soft skill") and refine it via a trainable soft delta while the base model stays frozen? Proposes SoftSkill — soft tokens trained with next-token prediction, deployed as latent behavioral priors. A length-32 SoftSkill prefix on Qwen3.5-4B beats no-skill prompting by 8.3 (SearchQA) / 42.1 (LiveMath) / 1.3 (DocVQA) points and beats SkillOpt by 5.2 / 12.5 / similar on the same benchmarks.

news.title: The Token Is a Group Element: On Lie-Algebra Attention over Matrix Lie Groups
news.summary: First attention construction whose tokens are bare matrix Lie group elements (no feature payload, no learned kernel). The score is the closed-form algebra norm of the relative pose log(g_i^-1 g_j) — fully intrinsic, equivariant by construction, and free of irreducible representations or spherical harmonics. It is the first vector-token-free attention that reaches non-compact affine groups with scale and shear (Aff(2)), which all irrep- or surjective-exp-based methods must exclude.

news.title: UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents
news.summary: Brings TurboQuant-style rotation + codebook quantization down to FP4 KV caching, with practical design choices: asymmetric K/V treatment, Walsh-Hadamard rotation, QJL removal, and block-scale variants. On AMD CDNA4 it introduces native scaled-MFMA support for FP8 queries × FP4 KV × UE8M0 group scales (UltraQuant).

news.title: VIMPO: Value-Implicit Policy Optimization for LLMs
news.summary: A new critic-free RL algorithm for LLM reasoning that derives a policy-implied value function from the optimality conditions of KL-regularized RL. Solves the GRPO vs actor-critic trade-off: GRPO has a trajectory-level advantage applied to every token (poor credit assignment); actor-critic is denser but unstable. VIMPO keeps critic-free simplicity and gets denser credit assignment by separating reward incorporation (value loss) from policy improvement (PPO-style actor). On MATH-500 / AIME 2024-2025 / OlympiadBench, VIMPO beats GRPO and keeps its edge under noisy rewards.

news.title: Beyond Global Replanning: Hierarchical Recovery for Cross-Device Agent Systems
news.summary: Introduces H-RePlan, a hierarchical replanning framework for multi-device agents that unifies API/CLI/GUI execution across Linux and Android. It separates device-local strategy recovery from orchestrator-level global replanning via a cross-layer failure abstraction, and ships HeraBench, a fault-injected benchmark for cross-device workflows. Beats single-strategy and coarse-grained baselines on completion, instruction adherence, and perfect-pass rate while cutting token cost.

news.title: Efficient and Sound Probabilistic Verification for AI Agents
news.summary: Extends Datalog-based runtime policy monitoring for AI agents beyond deterministic predicates to handle probabilistic ones (e.g. a PII detector with a non-zero miss rate). Uses distributionally robust optimization to compute sound upper bounds on policy-violation probability without needing independence assumptions. Reports tighter security-utility trade-offs than prior art on terminal and tool-calling agent benchmarks.

news.title: How Transparent is DiffusionGemma?
news.summary: A mechanistic-interpretability study of Google's diffusion LLM DiffusionGemma. Naively its "opaque serial depth" looks 28.6× worse than autoregressive Gemma 4, but the authors show you can route the inter-step information flow through an interpretable token bottleneck with no quality loss — collapsing the gap to 1.1×. They also surface diffusion-specific phenomena (non-chronological reasoning, token/sequence smearing) and confirm monitorability is preserved.

news.title: LedgerAgent: Structured State for Policy-Adherent Tool-Calling Agents
news.summary: An inference-time method that lifts task state out of the prompt and into a separate "ledger," which is then (a) rendered back into the prompt so the model sees a clean view, and (b) consulted before any environment-changing tool call to enforce state-dependent policy constraints. Improves average pass^k over prompt-only tool-calling baselines across four customer-service domains, with the biggest gains under stricter multi-trial consistency metrics.

news.title: Sovereign Execution Brokers: Enforcing Certificate-Bound Authority in Agentic Control Planes
news.summary: Proposes a runtime enforcement boundary (SEB) that sits between an agent's reasoning loop and the production mutation APIs. It consumes short-lived certificates from a Sovereign Assurance Boundary, verifies the requested mutation against the certified contract (validity window, policy epoch, revocation epoch, live-state drift), mints scoped execution identity, calls the infra APIs, and records signed decision/outcome logs. Evaluated on AWS + Kubernetes with fault injection.

news.title: NVIDIA 展示具身智能新突破：机器人通过自主探索学会将 GPU 安装到主板
news.summary: 6月17日 NVIDIA 发布视频：机器人无需预设编程或人工示教，通过自主探索理解高精度装配的物理规律，独立完成毫米级 GPU 主板安装任务。"自主探索 + 精密装配"是具身智能向工业制造场景渗透的关键里程碑，NVIDIA 正用全栈（训练+推理+机器人）能力压制 AMD/Intel。

news.title: OpenAI 联合 Maria AI 发布 GPT-5.4 药物化学成果，同步推出生命科学基准 LifeSciBench
news.summary: 6月17日 OpenAI 公布 GPT-5.4 与 Maria AI 合作的药物化学项目：系统在 2.5 个月内跑完文献综述到实验验证全流程，测试 10080 个反应条件，产率较基准提升 40%+。同日与 173 位生物医药科学家联合发布 LifeSciBench，不考知识记忆，专测"科学证据驱动的推理"。OpenAI 正把生命科学做成下一个评估标准制高点。

news.title: 亚马逊纽约峰会发布 Bedrock AgentCore 重大升级：打通"付费内容基础设施"
news.summary: 6月17日 AWS 在纽约峰会上为 Bedrock AgentCore 引入三层能力：连接组织内网/付费知识、定位并修复生产环境问题、随 Agent 能力扩展的控制体系。最大亮点是第三层"Paid Content Infrastructure"——内置支付与 WAF 流量变现，让 AI Agent 合规获取外部高价值数据，AWS 把自己定位为"AI 时代的工业级连接器"。

news.title: 美国商务部拟将 AI 芯片出口限制扩至马来西亚、泰国，剑指对华走私通道
news.summary: 彭博 6月18日报道，美国商务部起草新规，要求向马来西亚、泰国出口 NVIDIA、AMD 等 AI 加速器须申请许可，理由是防止东南亚中间商将芯片转售中国境内实体。新规尚未最终落地，若生效将进一步封堵现有 H20/Blackwell 衍生品的对华灰色路径。

news.title: 软银宣布与 OpenAI 合作，最快年内推出针对 Claude Mythos 级 AI 的网络安全服务
news.summary: 6月16日软银集团社长孙正义宣布与 OpenAI 合作，为日本金融、电力、公交等基础设施企业提供 AI 时代网络安全服务，应对超高性能模型被恶意用于网络攻击的风险。"Claude Mythos 级 AI 既能护国，也能灭国"成为日方判断依据，服务最快年底前上线。

news.title: Aypa Power + Salt River Project commission 250 MW / 1,000 MWh Pediment BESS in Mesa, Arizona
news.summary: Aypa Power and utility Salt River Project brought the 250MW/1,000MWh Pediment BESS online in Mesa's Elliot Road Technology Corridor on 6/16 (announced 6/18). It is the first of two contracted projects between the pair; Aypa is already developing a second 250MW/2,000MWh system targeted for December 2028.

news.title: Fire and Rescue NSW mandates 240-min fire resistance for Li-ion battery storage rooms in data centres
news.summary: On 6/18, Fire and Rescue NSW (FRNSW) issued a position statement requiring a 240/240/240 Fire Resistance Level for walls, floors and ceilings enclosing Li-ion battery storage rooms in data centres — and aligned its sprinkler guidance with NFPA 855:2026. The regulator explicitly rejects any reduction in FRL for these rooms, citing that UL 9540A cell/module/unit tests do not represent enclosed-compartment fire scenarios.

news.title: Invenergy takes $765M Trump-administration payout, walks from 4 offshore wind leases and pivots to enhanced geothermal
news.summary: Chicago-based Invenergy struck a deal with the U.S. Interior Department (announced 6/17, publicised 6/18) to relinquish four offshore wind leases off California, Maine and New York for $765M, the full value of the leases. The company will redirect proceeds into enhanced geothermal systems (EGS) — drilling its first wells later this year — and new natural-gas-fired plants. It is the third such deal after TotalEnergies ($1B) and Ocean Winds ($900M).

news.title: U.S. sodium-ion startups form American Battery Leadership Coalition (ABLC) to challenge China's Na-ion dominance
news.summary: A group of U.S. sodium-ion battery companies — including Alsym Energy and Peak Energy — formally launched the ABLC on 6/18. Members cite >15 GWh of announced Na-ion storage offtakes in the U.S. and are pushing for federal policy that recognises Na-ion under FEOC-compliant, non-Li-ion manufacturing incentives. ABLC argues >90% of federal battery grants have so far gone to mature Li-ion projects.

news.title: Wärtsilä spins out energy storage — divests 50% stake this week as analysts flag profitability drag
news.summary: Finnish engine and energy-storage major Wärtsilä is carving out its energy-storage activities and selling a 50% stake to a partner, formalised the week of 6/16. Analysts cited profitability and weak cross-sell synergies with Wärtsilä's wider engine business as the rationale. The deal was first reported by Energy-Storage.news on 6/18.

news.title: Beyond Parallel Sampling: Diverse Query Initialization for Agentic Search
news.summary: Test-time scaling for agentic search typically adds depth (more turns) or breadth (more parallel rollouts). This paper shows parallel sampling has diminishing returns because first-turn queries are redundant across rollouts, causing shared retrieval evidence. DivInit is a training-free intervention: draw n candidates from one call, pick k diverse seeds, and run them as parallel trajectories.

news.title: Models Take Notes at Prefill: KV Cache Can Be Editable and Composable
news.summary: Reveals that during prefill, a language model has already written the field-conditioned conclusion onto "downstream notes" — the field's own key/value drives under 1% of the decision. Read as a notebook of memoized conclusions, the KV cache becomes (1) editable: a single erratum (with CoT) recovers the decision at ~1% compute; and (2) composable: precompiled skills can be RoPE-repositioned and spliced into any context with O(L) time-to-first-token instead of O(L²).

news.title: PromptMN: Pseudo Prompting Language
news.summary: A pseudo-prompting domain-specific language that annotates natural language with compact, %-prefixed typed directives covering roles, goals, requirements, priorities, constraints, plans, inputs, and outputs. Semantic resolution lets authors write in any order; the model interprets by function.
